Resolution sources and verification
- Primary sources for verification include: White House Briefing Room (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), U.S. Department of State Press Releases/Media Notes (https://www.state.gov/press-releases/; https://www.state.gov/media-notes/), and USAID Press Releases (https://www.usaid.gov/news-information/press-releases). Past examples of qualifying announcement formats include the White House’s Oct 18, 2023 $100 million announcement  and references to the June 2024 $404 million U.S. announcement. If multiple qualifying announcements occur, a single instance is sufficient for “Yes”; otherwise resolve “No.”

question: Between 2025-10-15 00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, will the Council of the European Union adopt a 19th sanctions package against Russia?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- The Council of the EU adopted the 16th sanctions package against Russia on 24 February 2025.
- The Council adopted the 17th sanctions package on 20 May 2025; while the press release title says “EU agrees 17th package,” the body states “The Council adopted today the 17th package of economic and individual restrictive measures”.
- The Council adopted the 18th sanctions package on 18 July 2025, with a press release titled “EU adopts 18th package of economic and individual measures” stating “The Council adopted today a 18th package of economic and individual restrictive measures…”.
- On 19 August 2025, European Council President António Costa said the EU was “moving forward with the preparation of the 19th package of sanctions” against Russia.
- On 16 September 2025, discussion of a new Russia sanctions package was removed from an EU meeting agenda with “no new date planned” at that time.
- On 19 September 2025, Reuters reported that the European Commission proposed a 19th package to member states, including measures touching energy (e.g., advancing an LNG import ban to 1 January 2027), finance (transaction bans on additional banks and crypto platforms), export controls, and listings; proposals require member-state agreement before adoption.
- On 25 September 2025, Poland’s energy minister said the proposed 19th package would close a loophole on imports of certain LPG fractions (e.g., butane/isobutane) used to circumvent prior bans.

Why this is forecast-relevant now: A 19th package has been publicly trailed and formally proposed, but not adopted as of 2025-10-01; adoption requires Council action and has shown variable timing and internal negotiation in prior rounds, leaving uncertainty for Q4 2025.

Helpful references (for context and verification):
- Council press releases for the 16th, 17th, and 18th packages demonstrate the usual phrasing and publication venue used when adoption occurs.
- The Council’s timeline pages also summarize measures by package and date (useful for cross-checking).
resolution_criteria:
Resolution window and timezone:
- Eligible adoption events must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive). All dates/times referenced are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

What counts as “adopt a 19th sanctions package against Russia”:
- Adopt means that the Council of the European Union has formally adopted a new, numbered package of restrictive measures targeting Russia, and this is explicitly stated in an official Council press release.
- For the purposes of this market, a qualifying press release must:
  1) be published on the official Council of the EU website under Press releases and statements (consilium.europa.eu), and
  2) explicitly reference that the Council “adopted” (or “has adopted”) the “19th package” of “sanctions” and/or “economic and individual restrictive measures” against Russia (wording may include phrases like “Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine”), in the body text of the release. Note: Past practice shows that even when a title says “EU agrees [n]th package,” the body text states “The Council adopted today…”; for example, on 20 May 2025 the 17th package press release body stated adoption.

Primary source of truth:
- Council of the European Union press releases: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/ (search within for relevant Russia sanctions entries). The 16th and 18th packages show the typical adoption phrasing used in press releases.

Timing determination:
- If the qualifying Council press release is dated within the resolution window, the question will resolve Yes. If the press release only indicates political agreement without stating that the Council “adopted” the 19th package in the body text during the window, this does not count.
- If no qualifying Council press release dated within the window is found by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the question resolves No.

Clarifications and edge cases:
- The press release must pertain to a package “against Russia” (e.g., “Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine: EU adopts 19th package of economic and individual measures”). If paired measures concerning Belarus are included in the same communication, this still counts as long as the Council’s press release itself characterizes the adoption as the 19th package against Russia.
- Proposals by the European Commission, draft texts, political announcements, agenda items, or discussions without formal adoption do not count.
- Individual listings or targeted measures published outside a numbered package do not count unless the Council explicitly labels them as adoption of the “19th package.”
- If multiple packages (e.g., 19th and 20th) were adopted within the window, this question only concerns whether the 19th was adopted within the window.

Definitions (for clarity; links provided for general reference):
- Council of the European Union (“the Council”): one of the EU’s institutions where government ministers negotiate and adopt laws and policies. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_the_European_Union
- Sanctions package / restrictive measures: In this context, the numbered set of economic and/or individual restrictive measures targeting Russia, as described in Council press releases (e.g., the 16th, 17th, and 18th packages).
- Press release: An official news item published by the Council on consilium.europa.eu under “Press releases and statements,” which includes a date and explanatory body text.

Resolution procedure:
- The resolver will search the Council’s press releases page for an item that meets the criteria. If found with a date within the specified window, resolve Yes; otherwise resolve No. Examples of the required wording appear in prior adoption press releases for the 16th and 18th packages.

question: Will the U.S. FDA approve topical ocular reproxalap (Aldeyra Therapeutics) for the treatment of dry eye disease on or before December 31, 2025?
background:
As of October 1, 2025, Aldeyra Therapeutics reports that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted for review the resubmitted New Drug Application (NDA) for topical ocular reproxalap for the treatment of dry eye disease (DED) and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of December 16, 2025. Earlier in 2025, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter (CRL) stating that the NDA failed to demonstrate efficacy in adequate and well-controlled investigations; the CRL did not identify safety or manufacturing (CMC) issues. Aldeyra stated its intent to resubmit the NDA mid‑year 2025. Reproxalap is described by the sponsor as a small‑molecule modulator of reactive aldehyde species (RASP) being developed for DED and allergic conjunctivitis.

Key definitions and context for forecasters:
- FDA: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is the federal agency responsible for evaluating NDAs for safety and efficacy. NDA approval means FDA has determined the drug is safe and effective for its proposed use(s), labeling is appropriate, and manufacturing and quality controls are adequate.
- NDA: A New Drug Application is the formal request by a sponsor for FDA approval to market a new pharmaceutical in the U.S..
- PDUFA: The Prescription Drug User Fee Act authorizes FDA to collect user fees to help expedite drug reviews; the current authorization (PDUFA VII) covers fiscal years 2023–2027.
- Dry eye disease (DED): A multifactorial disease of the ocular surface characterized by tear film instability, hyperosmolarity, ocular surface inflammation and damage, and neurosensory abnormalities.
- Topical ocular (eye drops): Administration of liquid drops directly to the eye’s surface.

Primary resolution source: FDA’s Drugs@FDA database (“FDA‑Approved Drugs”) will be used to verify approval status and dates for the relevant NDA.
resolution_criteria:
Time window: Eligible events must occur between 2025‑01‑01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive).

Question to resolve: Will the FDA grant approval of an NDA for topical ocular reproxalap (regardless of final trade name) for the indication of treating dry eye disease (DED) within the time window?

Definitions (for resolution):
- “Approve” or “approval” means the FDA issues an approval action for an NDA, such that the product is authorized for marketing for the specified indication in the U.S., consistent with FDA’s definition of NDA approval (i.e., FDA has determined the drug is safe and effective for its proposed use(s), labeling is appropriate, and manufacturing/quality controls are adequate).
- “Topical ocular reproxalap” refers to the small‑molecule drug candidate known as reproxalap, administered as eye drops, sponsored by Aldeyra Therapeutics, and submitted to FDA for DED.
- “Dry eye disease (DED)” is as defined in the background above.

Resolution rules:
- Resolve Yes if, by the end of the time window, either of the following is true for the DED indication:
  (a) The relevant entry in FDA’s Drugs@FDA database shows an Approval action for reproxalap’s NDA for DED; or
  (b) The FDA publishes an official announcement (e.g., press release or announcement page) stating that FDA has approved reproxalap for DED.
- Resolve No if neither (a) nor (b) occurs within the time window, or if the FDA issues a Complete Response Letter, Refuse-To-File, or other non‑approval action only, or if any approval pertains solely to a different indication (e.g., allergic conjunctivitis) or a non‑topical ocular formulation.

Primary source of truth: FDA’s Drugs@FDA database entry for the product/indication. If Drugs@FDA has not yet updated by the end date, resolution may rely on an official FDA announcement as described above. Supporting context on the NDA and current review timeline derives from Aldeyra’s public communications and FDA background sources.

question: Will the United States raise the universal reciprocal tariff baseline (for non‑listed partners) above 10% between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Summary of current policy as of October 1, 2025: Executive Order (EO) 14257 established an additional ad valorem duty (“reciprocal tariff”) that applies universally at 10% to imports, except where otherwise provided, and set country‑specific rates for trading partners enumerated in Annex I; implementation occurs via modifications to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) and publication in the Federal Register. Subsequent Presidential actions modified partner‑specific rates and procedures but, as of July 31, 2025, confirmed that goods from foreign trading partners not listed in the then‑current Annex I remain subject to the universal 10% rate unless expressly provided otherwise. Other actions in mid‑2025 adjusted timelines, suspended or extended certain headings, or addressed PRC‑specific measures, without changing the universal baseline rate for non‑listed partners.

Key definitions and authoritative references:
- “Ad valorem duty”: A tariff calculated as a percentage of the value of the goods. See general definition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_valorem_tax. EO 14257 imposes “an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 percent” on imports, except as otherwise provided.
- “Universal reciprocal tariff baseline”: The additional ad valorem duty rate applicable to imports from foreign trading partners not enumerated in the most current Annex I (i.e., not assigned a partner‑specific rate), as established by EO 14257 and any subsequent amendments.
- “Listed partner” vs. “non‑listed partner”: “Listed” refers to foreign trading partners enumerated in Annex I of EO 14257 or successor Annexes with partner‑specific rates; “non‑listed” refers to any foreign trading partner not so enumerated at the relevant time.
- “HTSUS”: The Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States, maintained by the U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC), provides tariff classifications and rates; EO 14257 and subsequent actions modify HTSUS (including Chapter 99) to implement reciprocal tariffs. Reference: https://hts.usitc.gov/.
- “Federal Register”: The official journal for U.S. government rules, proposed rules, and notices; reciprocal tariff EOs and implementing notices are published here. Reference: https://www.federalregister.gov/.
- “White House Presidential actions”: Official EOs and proclamations are posted here: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/.

Status quo details (for forecasting context):
- EO 14257 states: “all articles imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 percent,” except as otherwise provided; and partner‑specific rates apply to “trading partners enumerated in Annex I”. EO 14257 also authorizes further modifications to increase or decrease duties in response to retaliation, alignment, or changes in manufacturing capacity, and delegates implementation authority to modify HTSUS via Federal Register notice.
- The July 31, 2025 action “Further Modifying the Reciprocal Tariff Rates” maintained the 10% ad valorem rate for foreign trading partners not listed in Annex I, while reorganizing HTSUS headings to facilitate partner‑specific rates; it explicitly states unlisted partners remain at 10% under EO 14257, as amended.
- A July 10, 2025 Federal Register notice extended a temporary suspension related to certain headings and timelines without altering the universal baseline rate above 10%.
- An August 14, 2025 Federal Register action continued PRC‑specific suspensions/adjustments and did not change the universal baseline for non‑listed partners.
- A September 10, 2025 Federal Register action modified scope, procedures, and annexes (e.g., updating lists of excluded goods and steps to implement agreements), while signaling potential future adjustments but not changing the universal baseline rate at that time.

Why this question is high‑entropy and non‑trivial: As of October 1, 2025, the universal baseline remains 10%, but EO 14257 explicitly provides authority and processes to modify duties in response to evolving trade, security, and economic conditions (including retaliation or alignment by trading partners), making a near‑term increase plausible yet uncertain. Recent actions show active management of partner‑specific rates and HTSUS structure, indicating potential for further changes before year‑end. Forecasters must assess political and economic drivers, negotiation dynamics, and administrative timelines for promulgating and making effective any change above 10%.

Suggested verification sources on resolution date: Federal Register entries for EO 14257 and subsequent modifications (search by EO number and keywords like “reciprocal tariff,” “Annex I,” “HTSUS Chapter 99”), and White House Presidential actions for any EO/proclamation modifying the universal baseline rate. See examples of relevant entries: EO 14257 in the Federal Register ; White House action on July 31, 2025 ; FR notices on July 10, August 14, and September 10, 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve YES if, between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, there is a formally enacted and effective Presidential action (e.g., Executive Order or Proclamation) and/or implementing Federal Register notice that sets the universal reciprocal tariff baseline (the additional ad valorem duty applicable to goods from foreign trading partners not listed in the then‑current Annex I) strictly greater than 10.000% as of 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025. Resolve NO otherwise.

Operational details:
- “Formally enacted and effective” means the measure is published (White House Presidential actions and/or Federal Register) and has taken effect per its stated effective date (e.g., with respect to goods entered for consumption on or after a specified date/time). Announced intent without effective implementation does not count.
- The determination hinges on the baseline rate applicable to non‑listed partners at resolution time. Partner‑specific rate changes, temporary suspensions of particular headings, or PRC‑only adjustments do not count unless they explicitly change the universal baseline rate for non‑listed partners.
- If multiple actions exist, the latest action in force as of 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025 governs. Verify by checking the most recent White House Presidential actions and Federal Register notices modifying EO 14257, its annexes, or HTSUS Chapter 99 notes.
- Primary resolution sources: Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/) and White House Presidential actions (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/). EO 14257 and subsequent modifications explicitly state that HTSUS modifications and notices will be published in the Federal Register, enabling unambiguous verification.

question: Will CoreWeave publish a statement that its Active Power is at least 900 MW between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Company and current metrics: CoreWeave, Inc. (Nasdaq: CRWV) reported that it ended Q2 2025 with approximately 470 MW of Active Power and increased total Contracted Power by ~600 MW to 2.2 GW, via its Q2 2025 press release and earnings materials.
- Management guidance toward year-end: On the August 12, 2025 earnings call, management said they were “on track to deliver over 900 megawatts of active power before the end of the year,” and reiterated a plan to “end the year with over 900 megawatts of active power.” These statements are forward-looking guidance rather than confirmations of current levels.
- M&A and power footprint context: On July 7, 2025, CoreWeave announced an agreement to acquire Core Scientific, stating that through the acquisition it would own approximately 1.3 GW of gross power across Core Scientific’s footprint, with over 1 GW of potential additional gross power for expansion; the transaction was expected to close in Q4 2025. Note that “gross power” in this context includes capacity supporting both HPC contracts (~840 gross MW) and crypto mining (~500 gross MW) and is not the same as CoreWeave’s “Active Power” metric.

Why this question: The company’s Q2 status (~470 MW Active Power) and management guidance (targeting >900 MW by year-end) set up meaningful uncertainty about both execution and whether CoreWeave will publish an official, unambiguous statement of having reached ≥900 MW of Active Power before the end of 2025. Construction timelines, interconnects, potential acquisition close, and disclosure practices introduce real execution and communication risk.

Key definitions and clarifications:
- Active Power: For the purpose of this question, “Active Power” means the specific metric labeled “Active Power” as reported by CoreWeave in its official investor communications (e.g., press releases, investor presentations, SEC filings, or earnings call transcripts posted on CoreWeave’s Investor Relations site). We do not infer or convert other power metrics to Active Power unless CoreWeave itself labels them as such. If a document uses “Active Power,” we take that term at face value as CoreWeave’s own metric. CoreWeave’s Q2 2025 materials report ~470 MW of Active Power but do not provide a formal definition beyond the label.
- Contracted Power: A separate CoreWeave-reported metric referring to contracted capacity (~2.2 GW as of Q2 2025) which is not interchangeable with Active Power.
- Gross power (Core Scientific context): Refers to the aggregate gross power across Core Scientific’s footprint (including crypto mining capacity) per the acquisition announcement and is not the same as Active Power.
- Power units: Megawatt (MW) and Gigawatt (GW). 1 GW = 1,000 MW. See general definitions for watt and multiples (e.g., https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watt#Multiples). Unit conversions are allowed for resolution (e.g., “0.9 GW” equals 900 MW).
- Acceptable phrasings: “≥ 900 MW,” “at least 900 MW,” “over 900 MW,” “more than 900 MW,” “0.9 GW or greater,” or a specific number that is ≥ 900 MW. For this market, statements using “approximately X MW” will be interpreted as X MW for threshold comparison (e.g., “approximately 910 MW” counts as 910; “approximately 900 MW” counts as 900).

Current status data points forecasters may use:
- Active Power as of Q2 2025: ~470 MW.
- Contracted Power as of Q2 2025: ~2.2 GW.
- Management guidance for year-end 2025: on track to deliver/end the year with over 900 MW Active Power (forward-looking as of Aug 12, 2025).
- Acquisition backdrop: Agreement to acquire Core Scientific; ~1.3 GW gross power cited; expected Q4 2025 close; conversion of crypto facilities to HPC is a potential future action and not indicative of current Active Power.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will CoreWeave publish a statement that its Active Power is at least 900 MW between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC?

Start and end dates (UTC):
- Start: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC

Resolve Yes if, within the above window, CoreWeave publishes any eligible document that contains a statement satisfying ALL of the following:
1) It explicitly references “Active Power.”
2) It unambiguously indicates Active Power is ≥ 900 MW (e.g., “≥ 900 MW,” “at least 900 MW,” “over 900 MW,” “more than 900 MW,” “0.9 GW or greater,” or a specific figure ≥ 900 MW). Unit substitutions are allowed with 1 GW = 1,000 MW.
3) It is stated as a present or past fact (e.g., “we now have…,” “as of [date] we had…,” “we ended  with…,” “we have surpassed 900 MW”), not solely as a future plan, target, or expectation (e.g., “on track to deliver,” “targeting,” “expect to reach” will NOT count on their own).
4) It pertains to CoreWeave’s consolidated business (including subsidiaries). If the Core Scientific acquisition closes, any consolidated Active Power figure is eligible provided it is labeled “Active Power.”

Eligible document types and sources:
- CoreWeave Investor Relations site (investors.coreweave.com), including: press releases, investor presentations/slide decks, earnings call transcripts posted on the IR site, and SEC filings linked from the IR site.
- CoreWeave corporate newsroom (coreweave.com/newsroom), specifically official press releases.
- SEC’s EDGAR (sec.gov) filings by CoreWeave (e.g., 8-K, 10-Q, 10-K) if they contain the qualifying statement and are filed within the window.

Interpretation clarifications:
- “Approximately”: For threshold comparison, “approximately X MW” will be interpreted as X. Thus “approximately 900 MW” is treated as 900 MW; “approximately 910 MW” is treated as 910 MW.
- Metrics that do NOT count: Statements solely about “Contracted Power,” “Gross Power,” “Nameplate,” or similar capacity measures do not count unless the statement explicitly labels the metric as “Active Power.”
- Forward-looking-only statements do not count: E.g., “on track to deliver over 900 MW” without an accompanying present/past statement at or above the threshold will not satisfy the criteria.
- Conflicting statements: If multiple statements within the window conflict, the most recent-dated statement within the window prevails for resolution.
- Accessibility: If the original source is temporarily unavailable, archived copies (e.g., via Internet Archive or the IR site’s CDN mirror) of eligible sources are acceptable if they clearly show publication within the window.

Resolution:
- Yes if at least one eligible document within the window satisfies all criteria.
- No if no eligible document within the window satisfies all criteria (including if CoreWeave provides only forward-looking statements or only non-Active Power metrics during the window, or provides no applicable disclosure at all).

Primary sources to check at resolution time:
- investors.coreweave.com (Financials > Quarterly Results; News)
- coreweave.com/newsroom
- sec.gov EDGAR filings for CoreWeave (CRWV)

Reference data points supporting background and scope come from CoreWeave’s Q2 2025 press release and earnings materials and related communications , and the Core Scientific acquisition press release.

question: Will the European Commission adopt a DMA non-compliance decision imposing a fine on Alphabet (Google) between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Digital Markets Act (DMA). The DMA is Regulation (EU) 2022/1925, an EU law that sets obligations for designated “gatekeepers” and empowers the European Commission to enforce compliance, including via non‑compliance decisions and fines.
- Alphabet designated as a gatekeeper. On September 6, 2023, the Commission designated six gatekeepers under the DMA: Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, and Microsoft. Designated gatekeepers had six months to ensure compliance with DMA obligations for their core platform services.
- Investigations into Alphabet’s compliance. On March 25, 2024, the Commission opened non‑compliance investigations into Alphabet under the DMA, including: (i) Google Play “steering” restrictions; and (ii) self‑preferencing in Google Search. The Commission indicated it intended to conclude these proceedings within 12 months; if it finds an infringement, it can impose fines up to 10% of total worldwide turnover (or up to 20% for repeated infringement).
- Preliminary findings to Alphabet. On March 19, 2025, the Commission sent two sets of preliminary findings to Alphabet under the DMA concerning Google Search and Google Play, noting that preliminary findings do not prejudge the outcome of the investigation.
- Enforcement precedents in 2025. On April 23, 2025, the Commission adopted DMA non‑compliance decisions against Apple and Meta and announced fines of €500 million and €200 million, respectively. This confirms the Commission’s practice of publishing formal non‑compliance decisions that include fines on the official DMA portal and press communications.
- Official publication venue. The Commission publishes DMA information, updates, and decisions on its official Digital Markets Act portal at digital‑markets‑act.ec.europa.eu.
- Corporate identification. Alphabet Inc. is the parent holding company of Google LLC; Google LLC is Alphabet’s largest subsidiary operating services such as Google Search and Google Play.

Why this question is non‑trivial now: The Commission has advanced Alphabet cases through formal investigations and preliminary findings, and has issued non‑compliance decisions with fines to other gatekeepers in 2025. Whether Alphabet (Google) will receive a formal non‑compliance decision imposing a monetary fine during the specified window remains uncertain, creating a high‑entropy policy forecasting problem linked to ongoing enforcement dynamics.

Key definitions and links:
- Digital Markets Act (DMA): Regulation (EU) 2022/1925. Official text: EUR‑Lex CELEX:32022R1925 (link: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/1925/oj/eng).
- Gatekeeper: An undertaking designated under Article 3 of the DMA to which DMA obligations apply; Alphabet is one of the six gatekeepers designated on 2023‑09‑06.
- Non‑compliance decision: An implementing act adopted by the Commission under Article 29 DMA establishing that a gatekeeper failed to comply with obligations (e.g., Articles 5–7) or measures specified in enforcement decisions; it orders the gatekeeper to cease non‑compliance and can follow preliminary findings and consultation steps.
- Fine (under the DMA): A monetary penalty imposed by the Commission pursuant to Article 30 DMA. For infringements of Articles 5–7, fines may be up to 10% of total worldwide turnover, and up to 20% for repeated infringements within eight years; Article 30 also provides other fine types for specified procedural infringements.
- Alphabet (Google): For this question, “Alphabet (Google)” refers to Alphabet Inc. and its subsidiary Google LLC (and any legal entity in the Alphabet group that is the addressee of the relevant DMA decision). Background references: Alphabet Inc. overview (Wikipedia) and Google LLC overview (Wikipedia).
- Official publication source: European Commission DMA portal (https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu) and Commission press releases/press corner; the portal is the Commission’s official site for DMA information.

Additional context on Alphabet’s current DMA enforcement status:
- Open proceedings and preliminary findings specifically identify suspected issues in Search and Play; the Commission’s stated 12‑month intention to conclude proceedings provides a temporal marker but does not guarantee timing or outcome.
- Recent non‑compliance decisions with fines against other gatekeepers show fines are being used in DMA enforcement, but each case is fact‑specific and outcome‑dependent.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on whether, during the period from 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 through 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, the European Commission publishes an official DMA non‑compliance decision that imposes a fine on Alphabet (Google), as defined below.

Event window and timezone:
- Eligible events must occur and be published between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.

Definitions for resolution:
- “Non‑compliance decision” means an implementing act adopted by the European Commission pursuant to Article 29 of Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 (DMA) that establishes a gatekeeper’s failure to comply with DMA obligations or measures, and orders the gatekeeper to cease non‑compliance.
- “Fine” means a monetary penalty imposed by the European Commission under Article 30 of the DMA. For the purpose of this question, the decision must impose a fine under Article 30 in relation to non‑compliance with Articles 5–7 or other specified measures (as enumerated in Article 30(1)); fines for purely procedural infringements (e.g., failure to supply information) also constitute “fines” under Article 30, but they only resolve this question if they are imposed within a non‑compliance decision under Article 29.
- “Alphabet (Google)” means Alphabet Inc., Google LLC, or another Alphabet group legal entity that is the addressee of the relevant DMA decision; Alphabet is a designated DMA gatekeeper.
- “Published” means that the European Commission makes the decision or an official press communication explicitly stating the adoption of a DMA non‑compliance decision imposing a fine available on its official websites (the DMA portal and/or Commission Press Corner/Newsroom). The Commission’s DMA portal is the official site for DMA information.

What counts (Yes):
- A European Commission non‑compliance decision under Article 29 DMA against Alphabet (Google) published within the event window, where the Commission explicitly states in the decision or an accompanying official press communication that a fine has been imposed (e.g., “has fined” with an amount specified), consistent with Article 30 DMA.

What does not count (No):
- A non‑compliance decision published outside the event window.
- A non‑compliance decision without a fine (e.g., ordering remedies but imposing no monetary penalty).
- A fine imposed outside an Article 29 non‑compliance decision (e.g., a standalone procedural fine not tied to a non‑compliance decision).
- Preliminary findings, opening of proceedings, statements of objections, consultations, or workshop materials that do not constitute an adopted Article 29 non‑compliance decision.
- Reporting solely by third‑party media without an official Commission publication.

Primary resolution sources (verification steps):
1) Check the European Commission’s DMA portal for Alphabet‑related enforcement pages and decisions: https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu.
2) Check Commission Press Corner/news releases for DMA decisions and fines during the window (e.g., pages similar to the April 23, 2025 Apple/Meta decisions): confirmation language typically includes “found [X] in breach” and “has fined [X] €…”.

Resolution:
- Resolve Yes if an official Commission publication during the window clearly indicates the adoption of an Article 29 DMA non‑compliance decision that imposes a fine against Alphabet (Google), per definitions above; otherwise resolve No.

Notes and edge cases:
- If the Commission adopts such a decision during the window but delays web publication until after December 31, 2025, the question resolves No (publication within the window is required).
- If the decision names a specific Alphabet group legal entity (e.g., Google LLC) as addressee, it qualifies, provided it is within the Alphabet group as defined.
- If multiple relevant decisions are published during the window, any single qualifying decision suffices to resolve Yes.
- If the Commission publishes only preliminary findings or opens additional proceedings during the window without adopting a non‑compliance decision imposing a fine, resolve No.

question: By 11:59:59 pm Eastern Time on December 31, 2025, will an official source confirm that definitive agreements to implement the U.S.-majority TikTok joint venture have been executed?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Legal posture: On January 17, 2025, the U.S. Supreme Court upheld the federal law requiring TikTok (owned by ByteDance) to be sold to an American entity or face a U.S. ban, establishing that continued operation in the U.S. depends on effectuating a qualifying divestiture.
- Enforcement timing: On September 16, 2025, a Presidential Executive Order further extended the pause on federal enforcement of the law until December 16, 2025. On September 25, 2025, the White House published a Presidential action describing a framework for a “qualified divestiture,” and directed the Attorney General not to enforce the Act for 120 days to permit completion of the contemplated divestiture; the document also notes the framework would be effectuated “once its implementation agreements are executed”. A same-day White House fact sheet emphasized the 120-day non-enforcement window to allow completion and described key governance and ownership parameters.
- What the contemplated U.S.-majority TikTok joint venture (JV) entails: According to official White House materials, the U.S. TikTok application would be operated by a newly established U.S.-based joint venture that is majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, with ByteDance owning less than 20% of the JV’s equity and holding only one of seven board seats (Americans to hold six of seven seats). The materials indicate that algorithm/control and content-moderation decisions would be under the JV, addressing national security concerns, with the framework becoming effective when implementation agreements are executed.
- Deal status as of late September 2025: Reuters reporting contemporaneous with the White House announcements indicated that while a framework was approved, the transaction details were not yet finalized; investor stakes were subject to change and “numerous details need to be fleshed out,” signaling that definitive agreements had not been signed. Additional reporting described that structural elements were still under discussion, and ByteDance would remain a significant minority shareholder with roles delineated between the JV and ByteDance-affiliated operations, reinforcing that final implementation documents were pending.
- Likely resolution sources: If a U.S.-listed investor party enters into material definitive agreements, the company would typically disclose entry into such agreements in a Form 8‑K within four business days under Item 1.01, providing a clear, time-stamped regulatory record. The White House publishes official statements at whitehouse.gov, and TikTok’s official newsroom hosts company press releases and statements.

Why this question is uncertain: The framework exists, enforcement has been paused to permit completion, and reporting suggests active negotiations—but execution of definitive/implementation agreements remained outstanding as of late September 2025. Execution by year-end is plausible but not assured, creating genuine uncertainty suitable for forecasting.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone:
- Eligible announcements must be first published between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC (inclusive) and 2026-01-01 04:59:59 UTC (inclusive), which corresponds to 11:59:59 pm Eastern Time on 2025-12-31.

Question subject:
- “U.S.-majority TikTok joint venture” refers to the U.S.-based entity described in official White House materials as the vehicle to operate TikTok’s U.S. application, majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, with ByteDance owning less than 20% and Americans holding six of seven board seats, and with algorithms/content-moderation under the JV’s control. The announcement must unambiguously refer to this JV construct (or a materially equivalent structure explicitly identified by the White House as the qualified divestiture).

What counts as “definitive/implementation agreements” and “executed”:
- “Definitive/implementation agreements” are the binding transaction agreements that implement and establish the JV described above (e.g., joint venture agreement/operating agreement, equity subscription/sale agreements, IP/technology license and operational agreements), as opposed to preliminary, non-binding documents such as term sheets, memoranda of understanding, or agreements in principle. For publicly listed parties, the execution of a “material definitive agreement” as defined under SEC Form 8‑K Item 1.01 constitutes sufficient evidence that a definitive agreement has been executed.
- “Executed” means signed by duly authorized representatives of the relevant parties such that the agreement(s) are binding. For SEC filings, the disclosure of entry into a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01 within four business days is acceptable confirmation.

What qualifies as a “publicly announce”/acceptable sources:
- Any one of the following, published within the time window, qualifies:
  1) An official White House publication on whitehouse.gov (e.g., Presidential actions, fact sheets, press statements) explicitly stating that the definitive/implementation agreements establishing the U.S.-majority TikTok JV have been executed.
  2) An official press release or statement posted on TikTok’s official newsroom (newsroom.tiktok.com) explicitly stating that such agreements have been executed.
  3) An official press release/statement posted on the official website of the new U.S. JV (if operational) explicitly stating execution of such agreements.
  4) A regulatory filing on the SEC’s EDGAR system by any U.S.-listed company that is a party to the transaction (e.g., an investor or partner), disclosing entry into a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01 that unambiguously pertains to executing the agreements that establish the JV described above.
  5) A report by Reuters or the Associated Press that contains an on-the-record, attributed statement by a named official of the White House, TikTok, or a party to the agreements, explicitly confirming that such definitive/implementation agreements have been executed. Reports relying solely on anonymous sources do not qualify.

Qualifying language (examples):
- Phrases such as “the parties have executed definitive agreements to establish the U.S.-majority TikTok joint venture,” “implementation agreements have been signed,” or “entered into binding definitive agreement(s) to form the JV described by the White House framework” qualify. Phrases like “agreement in principle,” “framework agreement,” “non-binding term sheet,” “letter of intent,” “intends to,” or “will pursue” do not qualify.

Resolution:
- Resolve YES if at least one qualifying announcement (as defined above) is published within the time window explicitly stating that the definitive/implementation agreements to establish the U.S.-majority TikTok JV have been executed. Otherwise, resolve NO.

Tie-breakers and conflicts:
- If conflicting reports exist, prioritize official publications (White House, TikTok newsroom, JV official site) and regulatory filings over media reports. If a qualifying source issues a correction or retraction before the deadline that makes it clear the agreements were not executed, resolve NO.

Notes for verifiers:
- The White House framework and enforcement delays are detailed in Presidential materials dated September 16 and September 25, 2025.
- Board composition and ownership constraints cited above come from official and wire reports.
- Reuters reporting indicates the deal was not finalized as of late September 2025, supporting that resolution was still open as of the start of the window.

question: Will the U.S. government publicly certify that TikTok has executed a “qualified divestiture” under the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act by December 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Statutory framework: The Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (Pub. L. 118-50) restricts distribution/maintenance of “foreign adversary controlled applications,” and provides that if a “qualified divestiture” is executed, the prohibition does not apply or ceases to apply to that app (§2(c)). “Qualified divestiture” means a divestiture or similar transaction that the President determines, through an interagency process, (A) would result in the app no longer being controlled by a foreign adversary, and (B) precludes any operational relationship between the U.S. operations of the app and formerly affiliated entities controlled by a foreign adversary, including cooperation on a content recommendation algorithm or any data-sharing agreement (§2(g)(6)). The Act expressly includes “TikTok” in the definition of “foreign adversary controlled application” (§2(g)(3)(A)(ii)) and defines when an entity is “controlled by a foreign adversary” (§2(g)(1)). Congress.gov text: https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/7521/text [link provided for convenience; authoritative claims above are sourced to the Act as summarized].
- Enforcement timing and delays: The Act’s prohibitions as applied to TikTok became effective in January 2025, but Executive Order 14166 suspended enforcement for 75 days to allow orderly consideration, with DOJ directed not to enforce or penalize conduct during that period or prior to the order. Subsequent presidential actions further delayed enforcement, including an extension until December 16, 2025. On September 25, 2025, a further presidential action (“Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security”) directed the Attorney General not to enforce the Act for 120 days from that order and described criteria the President evaluated regarding a contemplated divestiture.
- Status of a potential TikTok divestiture: The September 25 Federal Register publication states that, following an interagency process, the President determined a contemplated Framework Agreement would, once implementation agreements are executed, constitute a “qualified divestiture” under the Act, outlining criteria such as: U.S.-based joint venture with less than 20% ownership or control by foreign adversary persons, U.S. control of algorithms and code and content-moderation decisions, storage of sensitive U.S. user data in a U.S.-run cloud, and intensive monitoring/retraining of recommendation models by trusted U.S. security partners. These statements pertain to a proposed/anticipated transaction; they do not themselves certify that a qualified divestiture has been executed. Separately, contemporaneous reporting described a U.S.–China framework, investor lineup, and stated enforcement would be delayed further, though some details remained unresolved.

Why this question is forecastable: A final, public certification that TikTok has executed a qualified divestiture (as defined in the Act) is a binary, verifiable event that could plausibly occur before year-end but is not yet known. It depends on legal, regulatory, and transactional milestones that remain uncertain as of September 30, 2025.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves using publicly available, authoritative U.S. government sources. Time zone is UTC.

Resolution window: From 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive.

Operationalized question: Resolve YES if, during the resolution window, an official U.S. government publication on a federal.gov domain explicitly states that TikTok has executed a “qualified divestiture” under the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act and that the President has determined/certified that condition pursuant to §2(g)(6) of the Act; otherwise resolve NO.

Accepted forms of evidence (in order of precedence):
- A notice, executive order, presidential memorandum, determination, or other presidential action published on FederalRegister.gov that explicitly states the President has determined/certified that TikTok has executed a “qualified divestiture” under the Act.
- A presidential action or statement on WhiteHouse.gov that explicitly states the same.
- An official determination or certification posted on a relevant federal agency’s.gov site (e.g., Department of Justice) that explicitly states the same.

Key term definitions (for resolution):
- “TikTok”: the application specifically listed in §2(g)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act.
- “Qualified divestiture”: as defined in §2(g)(6) of the Act; the President must determine, through an interagency process, that the transaction (A) results in TikTok no longer being controlled by a foreign adversary and (B) precludes any operational relationship between TikTok’s U.S. operations and formerly affiliated entities controlled by a foreign adversary, including cooperation on a content recommendation algorithm or any data-sharing agreement.
- “Operational relationship” (for avoidance of doubt): includes, at minimum, cooperation regarding content recommendation algorithms and data-sharing agreements, per the Act’s illustrative examples in §2(g)(6)(B).
- “Publicly certify” (for this market’s purposes): an explicit statement in an official U.S. government publication (as enumerated above) that the President has determined/certified that TikTok has executed a qualified divestiture under the Act. Media reports, company press releases, leaks, or statements lacking explicit certification language do not count.

Inclusions and exclusions:
- Inclusion: A public document that explicitly states that the qualified divestiture “has been executed” and that the President has determined/certified that the resulting structure satisfies §2(g)(6). If such a certification document also states (or a companion official document states) that, under §2(c), the prohibition does not apply or ceases to apply to TikTok, that supports but is not required for a YES, provided the certification criteria above are met.
- Exclusion: Documents that only state a proposed or contemplated transaction “would” or “will, once executed, constitute” a qualified divestiture do not count (e.g., characterizations like those in the September 25, 2025 Federal Register publication describing a framework agreement).
- Exclusion: Publications posted before 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC (even if still live on a government site) do not count toward a YES; the certification must be newly published within the resolution window.

If conflicting publications exist, resolve based on the most authoritative source per the precedence above, favoring FederalRegister.gov over WhiteHouse.gov, and those over other.gov publications. If multiple qualifying publications appear, use the earliest qualifying publication time stamp within the window for resolution. If no qualifying publication appears within the window, resolve NO.

Primary reference texts for verification and definitions: the statutory definitions and mechanics in the Act as published on Congress.gov ; relevant presidential actions on FederalRegister.gov and WhiteHouse.gov documenting enforcement delays and contemplated divestiture criteria.

question: Hillman Solutions (HLMN): Will Q3 2025 net sales be at least $425.0 million?
background:
Company and fiscal calendar context
- Hillman Solutions Corp. (Nasdaq: HLMN) reports on a 52–53 week fiscal year ending on the last Saturday in December; in a 52‑week year, each quarter consists of 13 weeks. The company recognizes revenue when control transfers to customers and presents “Net sales” as its GAAP top‑line. Monetary amounts in financial tables are stated as “dollars in thousands” (USD).
- In 2025, Hillman’s Q1 covered the thirteen weeks ended March 29, 2025, and Q2 covered the thirteen and twenty‑six weeks ended June 28, 2025; by convention, Q3 follows as a 13‑week period ending in late September (e.g., Q3 2024 ended September 28, 2024).

Recent results and guidance relevant to forecasting Q3 2025
- Q1 2025 net sales were $359.3 million, up 2.6% year over year (thirteen weeks ended March 29, 2025).
- Q2 2025 net sales were $402.8 million, up 6.2% year over year (thirteen weeks ended June 28, 2025).
- Management updated full‑year 2025 net sales guidance to a range of $1.535–$1.575 billion in the Q2 2025 release.
- For seasonality context, Q3 2024 net sales were $393.3 million (down 1.4% YoY) for the thirteen weeks ended September 28, 2024, and Q4 2024 net sales were $349.6 million (thirteen weeks ended December 28, 2024).
- Hillman typically issues a press release for Q3 results in early November; for example, Q3 2024 results were released on November 5, 2024 at 7:30 a.m. ET.

Why the $425.0 million threshold?
- Given the updated FY2025 net sales guidance range of $1.535–$1.575 billion (midpoint $1.555 billion) and reported H1 2025 net sales totaling $359.3m + $402.8m = $762.1m, the implied H2 requirement spans roughly $772.9m–$812.9m to meet the low end through midpoint. With Q4 2024 at $349.6m for reference, a Q3 outcome around the mid‑$400m range would keep multiple full‑year scenarios in play, making $425.0m a balanced and uncertain threshold for Q3 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Question
- Between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, will Hillman Solutions Corp. report GAAP “Net sales” for its fiscal third quarter of 2025 that are greater than or equal to $425,000,000 (USD)? Resolve YES if ≥ $425.0 million; NO otherwise.

Definitions and scope
- “Fiscal third quarter of 2025” (Q3 2025) means Hillman’s 13‑week period that immediately follows Q2 2025 (which ended June 28, 2025) and precedes Q4 2025, consistent with the company’s 52/53‑week fiscal calendar ending the last Saturday in December.
- “Net sales” refers to Hillman’s GAAP revenue line as presented in its consolidated financial statements, recognized when control of goods or services transfers to customers; sales taxes are excluded, and discounts/rebates are netted in determining net sales.
- Currency and units: All amounts are in U.S. dollars. If the primary source presents financial tables labeled “(dollars in thousands),” the authoritative figure is the exact GAAP Net sales amount from those tables (i.e., the thousands figure multiplied by 1,000). If a narrative headline figure differs from the financial tables, the tables take precedence.
- Synonyms: If the press release or filing uses “Revenue” interchangeably with “Net sales” for the quarter’s top‑line GAAP amount, treat it as equivalent for resolution purposes, but prefer the labeled “Net sales” line where both appear.

Primary resolution source (use the earliest available in this order of precedence)
1) Hillman’s Q3 2025 earnings press release on the company’s Investor Relations News page (e.g., prior Q3 releases are posted there), or on the Investor Relations Financial Results page for the relevant quarter.
2) The Form 10‑Q for the thirteen‑week period comprising Q3 2025, filed with the U.S. SEC and accessible via EDGAR and/or Hillman’s IR site.

Timing and contingencies
- The market‑moving event (publication of the Q3 2025 results) is expected to occur within the resolution window based on historical practice (e.g., Q3 2024 released Nov 5, 2024). If both a press release and a Form 10‑Q are available and present differing GAAP Net sales for Q3 2025, use the Form 10‑Q figure.
- If Hillman issues a correction or restatement of the Q3 2025 net sales figure before 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, resolve using the latest corrected figure available by that deadline. Corrections issued after this deadline will be ignored for resolution.

Scoring
- YES if GAAP Net sales for Q3 2025 are ≥ $425,000,000 as per the sources above. NO if they are < $425,000,000.

question: Between 2025-04-24 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the European Commission adopt and publish an additional DMA non-compliance decision and/or impose a DMA fine on Meta that explicitly concerns its advertising model (beyond the 2025-04-23 decision)?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- On 2025-04-23, the European Commission adopted a non-compliance decision against Meta under the Digital Markets Act (DMA) and imposed a €200 million fine. The decision found Meta’s prior “consent or pay” advertising model non-compliant because it did not give users the required specific choice to opt for a service that uses less of their personal data but is otherwise equivalent. The Commission stated it is assessing Meta’s updated option introduced in November 2024 that allegedly uses less personal data for ads. Commission materials from the same date also describe the breach as failing to give consumers the choice of a service that uses less personal data.
- The 2025-04-23 decision explicitly limited its scope to Meta’s original “Consent or Pay” advertising model for the period March–November 2024 and noted this was without prejudice to the Commission’s ability to investigate Meta’s “Additional Ads” (i.e., less-personalized ads) option later.
- In November 2024, Meta announced a free “Less Personalized Ads” (LPA) option in the EU/EEA and Switzerland, describing it as relying on less data (primarily contextual signals from a current session plus minimal data such as age, location, gender, and ad engagement) and noting that ad breaks would be introduced in this low-data mode. Meta also reduced the price of the “Subscription for No Ads” at that time.
- Subsequent reporting indicated Meta was unlikely to propose further changes to its model in mid-2025 despite Commission warnings of potential daily fines, and suggested new EU antitrust/DMA charges could be likely, underscoring ongoing enforcement risk in 2025.

Why this is forecastable: The Commission has said it is assessing Meta’s updated ads option  and expressly left open further action beyond its April 2025 decision. However, follow-on decisions or fines are uncertain in timing and substance, making year-end 2025 a plausible but non-trivial window.

Key definitions and scope for this question:
- European Commission: The EU’s executive institution responsible for enforcing the DMA. For resolution, we rely on official Commission publications (Press Corner, Digital Strategy DMA pages) and the Official Journal/EUR-Lex.
- Digital Markets Act (DMA): Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 on contestable and fair markets in the digital sector.
- Meta: Meta Platforms, Inc. (provider of Facebook and Instagram in the EU/EEA).
- Advertising model (for this question): Meta’s approach to serving ads to users of Facebook and/or Instagram in the EU/EEA, including but not limited to: (a) the “consent or pay”/“pay or consent” model found non-compliant on 2025-04-23; and (b) the “Less Personalized Ads” (also referred to as “Additional Ads” or “less-personalized ads”) option introduced in November 2024, which Meta describes as relying primarily on contextual signals from a user’s current session and a minimal set of data (age, location, gender, and ad engagement), potentially with unskippable ad breaks.
- Non-compliance decision (for this question): A formal Commission decision under the DMA finding that Meta has not complied with one or more DMA obligations, akin to the decision adopted on 2025-04-23 against Meta’s “Consent or Pay” model.
- Fine (for this question): A pecuniary penalty imposed by the Commission under the DMA within a decision, distinct from periodic penalty payments. Only fines count for a YES outcome; periodic penalty payments do not count.

Status quo summary as of 2025-10-01:
- Meta has one DMA non-compliance decision and fine already adopted on 2025-04-23 regarding its earlier model.
- The Commission has publicly stated it is assessing Meta’s November 2024 less-personalized ads option , and the April 2025 decision’s scope suggests further action could target the updated model.
- Media reporting in July 2025 suggested the Commission warned of possible daily fines and that additional charges were likely, while Meta was unlikely to make further changes at that time.
resolution_criteria:
Resolution timing: This question resolves based on information available up to 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Eligible actions must occur between 2025-04-24 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Question: Will the European Commission adopt and publish an additional DMA non-compliance decision and/or impose a DMA fine on Meta that explicitly concerns Meta’s advertising model within the eligibility window?

Operational rules:
- “Additional” means beyond the Commission decision adopted on 2025-04-23 concerning Meta’s advertising model (document number C(2025) 2091; scope limited to March–November 2024). Any new decision must be a separate decision adopted on or after 2025-04-24.
- “Adopt and publish” is satisfied if, by the resolution timestamp, at least one of the following is publicly accessible for the new action: (a) a Commission Press Corner press release describing the adoption of the decision; (b) a Commission Digital Strategy/DMA news post describing the adoption; (c) the decision or its summary notice in the Official Journal/EUR-Lex (e.g., a C-series summary). Examples of such sources for the April 23 action are available on Commission sites and EUR-Lex.
- “Explicitly concerns Meta’s advertising model” means the decision text and/or official Commission communication states that the subject matter pertains to Meta’s ads model on Facebook and/or Instagram (e.g., “pay or consent,” “less personalized ads,” “Additional Ads,” or equivalent references to ad personalization/data use in the EU/EEA). Decisions focused on unrelated conduct (e.g., Marketplace tying under antitrust law) do not count.
- What counts for YES: Any of the following adopted and published within the window: (1) a new DMA non-compliance decision against Meta that concerns its advertising model (fine included or not); or (2) a Commission decision under the DMA imposing a fine on Meta that the Commission states concerns its advertising model (even if combined with a non-compliance decision). Periodic penalty payments alone do not count as a “fine.”
- What does NOT count: (a) Informal statements, speeches, leaks, or media reports without an adopted decision; (b) actions under other legal frameworks (e.g., DSA, GDPR, antitrust) unless expressly stated by the Commission as a DMA decision; (c) periodic penalty payments without an accompanying fine; (d) any decision adopted before 2025-04-24 or after 2025-12-31 UTC.

Resolution sources and precedence:
- Primary sources: European Commission official publications (Press Corner and Digital Strategy DMA news pages) describing the adoption of the decision/fine.
- Secondary/backup: The Official Journal/EUR-Lex publication of the decision or its summary (e.g., C-series).
- If primary and secondary sources conflict, the decision text/summary on EUR-Lex prevails.
- If needed for confirmation of adoption timing or scope, reputable wire services (e.g., Reuters) may be used as supporting evidence, but cannot substitute for the absence of an adopted Commission decision.

Adjudication:
- YES if, by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, such an additional DMA non-compliance decision and/or DMA fine concerning Meta’s advertising model has been adopted and published as defined above. NO otherwise.

Notes:
- The Commission’s April 23, 2025 decision and €200m fine regarding Meta’s earlier model are excluded from counting for this question; they are background only.
- The April 2025 decision’s stated scope (March–November 2024 original model) and the Commission’s ongoing assessment of the November 2024 “less personalized ads” option motivate the plausibility of further action in 2025.

question: By December 31, 2025 (23:59:59 UTC), will a signed definitive agreement be publicly announced to transfer the right to operate TikTok’s U.S. service to a U.S.-organized entity in which ByteDance and its affiliates will own less than 20% on a fully diluted basis at closing?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- On Sept 25, 2025, the U.S. President signed an order stating that a proposed deal framework for TikTok’s U.S. operations satisfies statutory requirements, with enforcement of the earlier divest-or-ban law delayed to allow completion. Reporting indicates the plan envisions ByteDance owning under 20% of the new U.S. venture, with the algorithm controlled in the U.S..
- The New York Times reported the envisioned U.S. TikTok company at about a $14 billion valuation and noted negotiators were given until mid-January to finalize the deal.
- Reuters reported that Americans would hold six of seven board seats in the new U.S. TikTok entity, with ByteDance choosing one, and that the recommendation algorithm would be secured, retrained, and operated in the U.S. outside ByteDance’s control.
- Additional analysis suggested a joint venture may handle data security and algorithm licensing/management, with ByteDance as a significant minority stakeholder (around 20%) in that JV and potentially receiving substantial licensing or other fees tied to U.S. profits; the exact structure remains fluid.

Why this is forecastable and uncertain:
- There is clear political and regulatory momentum toward a divestiture that brings TikTok’s U.S. operations into compliance with U.S. law, paired with a specific ownership threshold (<20%) and U.S. control provisions.
- However, material deal details (e.g., which entity precisely holds U.S. operating rights, the precise ByteDance stake across layered entities, and final algorithm control/licensing arrangements) were still being negotiated as of late September 2025 , creating genuine uncertainty about whether a definitive, binding agreement meeting all criteria will be signed and publicly announced by year-end.

Key concepts and where to find evidence:
- For public companies, “entry into a material definitive agreement” is disclosed on Form 8‑K, Item 1.01, typically within four business days; these filings are accessible on the SEC’s EDGAR system. 8‑K is a current report intended to disclose timely, material events, and Item 1.01 covers material agreements not in the ordinary course of business.
- Definitions used below are standard in U.S. securities and tax contexts: “affiliate” and “control” per SEC Rule 405 ; “U.S.-organized entity” (i.e., domestic corporation) per IRS guidance ; examples of “definitive agreements” in M&A include stock/asset purchase agreements and merger agreements. Ownership measured “on a fully diluted basis” includes all shares that could be created by convertible securities, options, warrants, etc..

Primary sources likely to provide resolution evidence include official company press releases and SEC filings (e.g., Form 8‑K Item 1.01 by any public company party), with corroboration by wire services and major outlets such as Reuters or the New York Times.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and scope:
- Start: 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC
- Geography/time standard: All dates/times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Resolution:
- Resolve Yes if, between the start and end times above, a signed definitive agreement is publicly announced by at least one principal party (e.g., ByteDance, TikTok, the acquirer/investor consortium, or a public-company party via a Form 8‑K Item 1.01) that satisfies all conditions below. Otherwise resolve No.

Conditions that must all be satisfied:
1) Definitive agreement signed: There is a written, legally binding, fully executed agreement to consummate the transaction (e.g., stock purchase agreement, asset purchase agreement, merger agreement, or equivalent). Non‑binding term sheets, memoranda of understanding (MOUs), or letters of intent (LOIs) do not qualify. If any public company is a party, an Item 1.01 Form 8‑K would typically be filed within four business days of entry and can serve as evidence.

2) Transfer of the right to operate TikTok’s U.S. service: The agreement (or the accompanying official announcement/SEC filing) assigns, conveys, or otherwise grants to a U.S.-organized entity (as defined below) the exclusive right to operate the TikTok app for users located in the United States and exclusive control over U.S. user data and the content-recommendation operations for the U.S. service, whether via ownership or exclusive license. Wording consistent with reported policy goals—i.e., the algorithm is secured/retrained/operated in the U.S. outside ByteDance’s control—meets this criterion if stated in the agreement or official filing/press release.

3) U.S.-organized entity: The entity that will hold the rights in (2) is organized under the laws of the United States, a U.S. state, or the District of Columbia (i.e., a domestic corporation or LLC).

4) ByteDance ownership threshold: The agreement (or accompanying official announcement/SEC filing) explicitly states that ByteDance and its affiliates will collectively own strictly less than 20.000% of the equity of the entity identified in (3) as of the closing contemplated by that agreement, measured on a fully diluted, as‑converted basis (including all outstanding and reserved shares, options, warrants, convertible securities, and similar instruments). Ownership includes both direct and indirect holdings by ByteDance and its “affiliates.” “Affiliate” and “control” are as defined in SEC Rule 405 (affiliate means a person that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with the specified person; control means the power to direct management and policies through ownership, contract, or otherwise).

Evidence required and acceptable sources:
- Primary evidence can be: (a) an SEC Form 8‑K (Item 1.01) by any public-company party describing entry into the material definitive agreement, including the required summary of material terms; and/or (b) an official press release or transaction announcement posted on a principal party’s website that clearly states all relevant points for conditions (2)-(4).
- If the exact percentage ownership or rights are not stated in the agreement text publicly available but are specified in an Item 1.01 8‑K summary or official press release, that is sufficient. In the absence of these, corroboration by at least two reputable outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, WSJ, NYT) reporting the signed definitive agreement and the <20% ByteDance stake and U.S. control arrangements will be accepted, provided their reporting is consistent with any available primary disclosures.

Clarifications and edge cases:
- Multiple-entity structures: If a layered structure is used (e.g., one entity for U.S. operations, a separate JV for data/algorithm), the relevant entity for measuring the <20% threshold is the U.S.-organized entity that, per the agreement/official disclosure, will hold the exclusive rights in condition (2)—i.e., exclusive right to operate TikTok’s U.S. app, exclusive control over U.S. user data, and control/operation of the U.S. recommendation algorithm.
- Announcement timing: The signing must be publicly announced (via SEC filing and/or official press release) within the resolution window. Agreements signed but not publicly announced within the window do not count.
- Amendments: If an agreement is signed within the window but later amended, the initial signing counts for timing. However, to resolve Yes, the version signed within the window must already satisfy conditions (2)-(4).
- Non-qualifying disclosures: LOIs, term sheets, framework agreements, or conditional government approvals without a binding, signed transaction agreement do not qualify.

Context references (for forecasters):
- Ownership threshold and U.S. control elements have been publicly described in late Sept 2025 reporting. Some reporting suggests alternative structures with ByteDance at or near 20% in certain JVs and substantial licensing economics, underscoring uncertainty about meeting the strict <20% criterion by year-end.

question: Will U.S. core PCE inflation (YoY) for November 2025 be at or below 2.8% in the BEA’s December 19, 2025 Personal Income and Outlays release?
background:
Overview and current status (as of 2025-10-01)
- What is being measured: The “core PCE price index” is the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index excluding food and energy. BEA describes this as a measure that removes two categories with more volatile price swings to better show underlying inflation; it is released monthly as part of Personal Income and Outlays. BEA’s tables label the 12‑month rate as “Change From Month One Year Ago”.
- When/where it is reported: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) lists a news release titled “Personal Income and Outlays, November 2025” scheduled for December 19, 2025 (release code BEA 25-55).
- Recent values: BEA reports the YoY core PCE (“excluding food and energy”) at +2.9% for August 2025 in both the August news release and the BEA data page; June–August 2025 values are 2.8%, 2.9%, and 2.9%, respectively.

Definitions and links for forecasters
- Core PCE price index (PCE excluding food and energy): BEA’s definition and recent YoY values are here: https://www.bea.gov/data/personal-consumption-expenditures-price-index-excluding-food-and-energy.
- Year-over-year (YoY) as used by BEA: the 12‑month percent change, labeled in BEA materials as “Change From Month One Year Ago”.
- Resolution source: BEA’s news post for “Personal Income and Outlays, November 2025” (release code BEA 25-55).

Why this threshold: The latest YoY core readings have hovered near the high‑2% range (2.8%–2.9% in June–August 2025), making 2.8% a plausible and uncertain cutoff for the November figure.
resolution_criteria:
What counts
- Target statistic: The 12‑month percent change in the PCE price index excluding food and energy (core PCE), for November 2025, as reported by BEA in its “Personal Income and Outlays, November 2025” news release (release code BEA 25-55) published on December 19, 2025.
- Acceptable fields/sources within the release: Use the YoY figure appearing in the news release text (e.g., the sentence of the form “Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index increased X percent from one year ago,” as exemplified in BEA’s August 2025 release). If that explicit sentence is absent, use the accompanying BEA table value for “Change From Month One Year Ago” for “PCE price index excluding food and energy” for November 2025 (same measure shown on BEA’s core PCE data page). Do not recalculate from index levels.

Resolution rule
- YES if the BEA-reported YoY core PCE for November 2025 is less than or equal to 2.8% as stated in the December 19, 2025 news release; NO if it is greater than 2.8%.

Timing, updates, and rounding
- Timing: This market resolves upon publication of the BEA news release dated December 19, 2025 (regardless of the exact posting time that day). All dates and times in this question are interpreted in UTC when relevant; however, only the content of that specific BEA release determines resolution.
- Rounding: Use the value as BEA reports it (typically to one decimal place). Do not attempt to infer additional precision beyond what BEA publishes in the release/tables.
- Revisions: Only the initially published values in the December 19, 2025 BEA release count for resolution. Any later revisions (e.g., in subsequent releases) are ignored.

Direct links for resolution (when available)
- BEA news index entry referencing the scheduled release and code: https://www.bea.gov/node/41776 
- BEA core PCE definition and recent YoY values (for context on the measurement used): https://www.bea.gov/data/personal-consumption-expenditures-price-index-excluding-food-and-energy 
- Example of how BEA states the YoY core PCE in a monthly release (August 2025): https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/personal-income-and-outlays-august-2025

question: Will the Bank of England change Bank Rate at its 6 November 2025 MPC meeting?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- What is Bank Rate: Bank Rate (also called the Official Bank Rate) is the United Kingdom’s core policy interest rate set by the Bank of England. It is the rate of interest the Bank of England pays on overnight deposits (reserves) placed with it by eligible banks and financial institutions, and is the primary tool used to influence other interest rates in the economy. See the Bank of England explainer: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/the-interest-rate-bank-rate.
- MPC meeting and publication date: The Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has a confirmed announcement and minutes publication date of Thursday 6 November 2025. The specific November 2025 Monetary Policy Summary (MPS) and minutes page exists and is scheduled “to be published at 12pm” (UK time) on that date: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-summary-and-minutes/2025/november-2025.
- Current Bank Rate and recent decisions: The MPC maintained Bank Rate at 4.00% at its meeting ending on 17 September 2025. The official Bank Rate database shows the most recent change prior to that was a reduction to 4.00% effective 7 August 2025.
- Inflation backdrop: The UK Consumer Prices Index (CPI) rose 3.8% in the 12 months to August 2025, unchanged from July 2025. See ONS bulletin: https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/consumerpriceinflation/august2025.
- Market expectations for the 6 November 2025 decision: In the Bank of England’s Market Participants Survey (September 2025), respondents’ mean probabilities for Bank Rate after the 6 November 2025 meeting were 57.8% for 4.00% and 38.7% for 3.75% (with very low probabilities elsewhere), indicating material uncertainty about whether a cut occurs at that meeting. See survey results: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/markets/market-intelligence/survey-results/2025/market-participants-survey-results-september-2025.
Definitions and links:
- Bank Rate/Official Bank Rate: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/the-interest-rate-bank-rate ; official history: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/Bank-Rate.asp.
- Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting dates: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/news/2024/september/monetary-policy-committee-dates-for-2025.
- November 2025 MPS and minutes landing page (resolution source): https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-summary-and-minutes/2025/november-2025.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves on the content of the Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Summary (MPS) and minutes page for November 2025.

- Event window: This question concerns the MPC decision whose MPS and minutes are published on 6 November 2025 (scheduled for 12:00 UK time). All times referenced are UK local time.
- Key term – “Bank Rate”: The United Kingdom’s Official Bank Rate set by the Bank of England (see BoE explainer and official history).
- Key term – “change Bank Rate”: Any decision by the MPC at that meeting to set Bank Rate at a numeric level different from its immediately previous level (increase or decrease). The immediately previous level is the last published Bank Rate prior to 6 November 2025, as recorded in the Bank of England’s official Bank Rate database  and/or the prior meeting’s MPS.

Resolution steps:
1) Access the November 2025 MPS and minutes page: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-summary-and-minutes/2025/november-2025.
2) Determine the MPC’s decision text. Resolve “Yes” if the MPS states the MPC decided to change Bank Rate (e.g., “the Committee voted to reduce/increase Bank Rate to X%”). Resolve “No” if the MPS states the MPC voted to maintain Bank Rate at its previous level (e.g., “voted to maintain Bank Rate at 4%”).
3) If the November 2025 MPS page is unavailable or the wording is ambiguous (unlikely), use the official Bank Rate database to verify whether the Bank Rate changed on 6 November 2025 relative to the prior level. If the database shows a new effective date and rate on 6 November 2025 differing from the prior rate, resolve “Yes”; if it shows no change on that date, resolve “No”.

Primary source of truth: The Bank of England’s November 2025 MPS and minutes page. Fallback source: Bank of England Official Bank Rate history database. Confirmation of meeting/publication date: BoE MPC dates for 2025.

question: Will the ECB lower its deposit facility rate at its 18 December 2025 monetary policy meeting?
background:
Context as of 1 Oct 2025:
- Meeting and communications cadence: The ECB Governing Council is scheduled to hold a monetary policy meeting in Frankfurt on 18 December 2025, followed by a press conference. ECB monetary policy decisions are communicated via a same-day press release, and the President comments at a press conference; for example, the 11 September 2025 release states the press conference starts at 14:45 CET, and the decisions page notes decisions are published on the day of the meeting.
- What is the “deposit facility rate”? It is the interest rate banks receive when they deposit money with the central bank overnight; it is one of the ECB’s three key interest rates.
- Status quo of key rates: On 11 September 2025, the ECB kept its three key interest rates unchanged at: deposit facility 2.00%, main refinancing operations 2.15%, marginal lending facility 2.40%. Earlier in the year (6 March 2025), the ECB lowered the three key rates by 25 basis points, illustrating standard phrasing used when rates change.
- Market context: As of 11 September 2025, Reuters reported that ECB policymakers viewed the 18 December meeting as the more likely date to debate a reduction in borrowing costs, while emphasizing that the decision would depend on incoming data and projections.
- Where the decision will be published: The authoritative record is the ECB’s “Monetary policy decisions” press release for the meeting date, with details on the three key interest rates. The ECB’s “Key ECB interest rates” page documents definitions and current/past values of the three key rates.
resolution_criteria:
What will be judged
- This question concerns the ECB Governing Council’s monetary policy decision announced on 18 December 2025 (Frankfurt local time, CET).

Primary resolution rule
