- Resolve Yes if the ECB’s official “Monetary policy decisions” press release published on 18 December 2025 states that the interest rate on the deposit facility is being lowered relative to its level immediately before the announcement. This can be evidenced by language such as “The Governing Council today decided to lower the three key ECB interest rates …” or “the interest rate on the deposit facility will be decreased to X% …”.
- Resolve No if that press release states the deposit facility rate is unchanged or higher, e.g., “decided to keep the three key ECB interest rates unchanged”.

Definitions and sources
- “Deposit facility rate” means the interest rate banks receive when they deposit money with the Eurosystem overnight, one of the ECB’s three key interest rates.
- “Lowered” means the new deposit facility rate set in the 18 December 2025 decision is strictly less than the rate in force immediately before the announcement. If a numerical comparison is needed, the prior rate can be established from the ECB’s “Key ECB interest rates” page as it appeared immediately prior to the 18 December decision or from the most recent prior monetary policy press release.
- The effective date of any change (e.g., “with effect from [date]”) does not affect resolution; if the decision sets a lower value, it counts as lowered regardless of when it takes effect.

Timing window and scope
- Eligible announcements for this question must occur between 00:00 on 15 October 2025 and 23:59 on 31 December 2025, Frankfurt local time (CET). In practice, the relevant announcement is expected on 18 December 2025, when a monetary policy meeting followed by a press conference is scheduled.

Authoritative sources for resolution
- Primary: ECB “Monetary policy decisions” press release for 18 December 2025 (published on ecb.europa.eu).
- Secondary (only if the primary is unavailable on the day): the ECB introductory statement/press conference text for 18 December 2025; if neither ECB source is accessible by end of day, resolve based on concordant reporting by major wire services (e.g., Reuters).

Edge cases
- If the ECB does not hold a monetary policy meeting on 18 December 2025 and no “Monetary policy decisions” press release is published that day, resolve No. This condition ensures the question remains unambiguously resolvable on or before 31 December 2025.

question: Will the UK government launch a public pilot of a digital driving licence via GOV.UK Wallet by December 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- The UK government has publicly stated that GOV.UK Wallet will launch “later this year” and will include “a pilot digital driving licence,” following the summer 2025 trial launch of the GOV.UK App. A separate January 2025 announcement said a digital driving licence is “coming this year,” with an early version to be piloted later in 2025, as part of the GOV.UK Wallet ecosystem.
- Official GOV.UK Wallet guidance describes the Wallet as an app that will let users save government documents (including, in future, their driving licence) to their phone. It notes that Wallet is not ready to use yet for the general public, and that One Login is required to access it.
- Government guidance for departments and the digital identity sector indicates a staged rollout: Wallet will first hold the HM Armed Forces Veteran Card from summer 2025, followed by the full driving licence as one of the first documents to be added.
- DVLA’s 2024–25 Annual Report states discovery is complete and development is about to commence “with the aim to add a digital driving licence to the GOV.UK Wallet by the end of 2025”.
- The Data (Use and Access) Act received Royal Assent on June 19, 2025, formalising Digital Verification Services and supporting the broader digital identity ecosystem within which GOV.UK Wallet operates.

Why this question is non-trivial: Large public IT projects often slip; while multiple official statements signal a 2025 pilot, actual launch could be delayed. The resolution depends on real-world delivery milestones and official announcements, creating meaningful uncertainty.

Key definitions and links:
- Digital driving licence (DDL): A government-issued digital credential representing an individual’s UK driving licence (issued by DVLA) that can be stored and presented via the GOV.UK Wallet app. Government materials describe Wallet as enabling users to save and use government documents like the full driving licence on their phone. See GOV.UK Wallet overview: https://www.gov.uk/wallet.
- GOV.UK Wallet: A UK government app and platform that will allow people (via GOV.UK One Login) to save and use government-issued documents on their phone, starting with selected credentials and expanding over time.
- UK driving licence (general concept): The official authorisation to drive vehicles in Great Britain, issued by the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA). Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_licence_in_the_United_Kingdom (link provided for general definition; not used for resolution).
- GOV.UK One Login: The government identity and login service required to access Wallet. Overview: https://www.gov.uk/using-your-gov-uk-one-login.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, an official UK government source announces and evidences that a public pilot of a digital driving licence (DDL) via GOV.UK Wallet has launched and is live for some members of the public (outside internal testing), as defined below. Otherwise it resolves No.

Definitions for resolution:
- Public pilot: A government-run limited release intended to test the DDL with members of the public who are not part of internal government testing. The pilot is considered “launched” when eligible members of the public (e.g., drivers in a defined cohort, region, or invite list) can enroll and add a DDL to their GOV.UK Wallet and use it in real-world contexts. Platform limitations (e.g., iOS-only) or cohort restrictions are acceptable; internal closed tests limited to civil servants or contractors do not count.
- Digital driving licence (DDL): A digital version of the UK driving licence issued under DVLA authority, stored and presented via GOV.UK Wallet. It must be the driving licence credential, not other documents (e.g., the HM Armed Forces Veteran Card). Government guidance indicates the full driving licence is planned as one of the first Wallet documents.
- Official UK government source: A page or publication under the gov.uk domain (including GOV.UK News releases, DVLA pages, Cabinet Office/GDS or DSIT publications), or the live GOV.UK Wallet user-facing page/app instructions. Primary resolution sources include:
  • GOV.UK News (“Government news and communications”): https://www.gov.uk/government/news 
  • GOV.UK Wallet overview and guidance pages: https://www.gov.uk/wallet; https://www.gov.uk/guidance/using-govuk-wallet-in-government; https://www.gov.uk/guidance/using-govuk-wallet-in-the-digital-identity-sector 
  • DVLA pages and publications on gov.uk (for example, DVLA press releases and updates) 

What counts as sufficient evidence:
Any one of the following published between the start and end timestamps will resolve the question Yes:
1) A GOV.UK News post or DVLA/GDS/DSIT gov.uk page explicitly stating that a pilot digital driving licence has launched and is now available for eligible members of the public to use (e.g., “pilot digital driving licence launched today…”), or
2) The GOV.UK Wallet user-facing page or app instructions updated to state that users in a defined cohort can now add their driving licence to Wallet (e.g., “You can now save your driving licence to GOV.UK Wallet…”), or
3) An official gov.uk page providing a live sign-up or enrollment pathway clearly open to non-government participants to obtain and use a DDL during the pilot.

Exclusions:
- Announcements that only state intention (e.g., “will launch later this year”) without stating that the pilot is live do not count.
- Pilots or releases involving other documents (e.g., HM Armed Forces Veteran Card) do not count toward this question.
- Reporting by third parties without an official gov.uk source does not count.

If sources conflict:
- Prefer the most recent official gov.uk publication. If ambiguity remains, the GOV.UK Wallet user-facing page and the relevant GOV.UK News post will be decisive.

Notes and context for resolvers:
- Government statements indicate intent to pilot the DDL later in 2025 and to add the full driving licence to Wallet after the Veteran Card, with DVLA aiming for end-of-2025 availability. The legislative foundation for digital verification services was established in June 2025.

question: By December 31, 2025, will the United States reduce or suspend the additional 25% ad valorem duty on products of India imposed under Executive Order 14329?
background:
Status quo as of September 30, 2025:
- On August 6, 2025, the President issued Executive Order 14329 (“Addressing Threats to the United States by the Government of the Russian Federation”) imposing an additional ad valorem duty of 25% on imports of articles of India. The order’s duty becomes effective 21 days after the order’s date for goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, with specified transit exceptions.
- U.S. Customs and Border Protection implemented the measure via a Federal Register Notice on August 27, 2025. The notice establishes HTSUS heading 9903.01.84 for “products of India,” sets the additional duty at 25%, provides the effective time (12:01 a.m. EDT on August 27, 2025), and details exceptions (e.g., certain in-transit shipments, specified iron/steel and aluminum articles, passenger vehicles and parts, humanitarian donations, informational materials). It explicitly states this additional duty is in addition to duties under Executive Order 14257 (reciprocal tariffs) unless otherwise specified.
- Separately, under the July 31, 2025 presidential action “Further Modifying the Reciprocal Tariff Rates,” India’s baseline reciprocal tariff rate was set at 25% effective August 7, 2025, which stacks with the EO 14329 duty where applicable. In practice, this means many Indian-origin goods face combined duties of approximately 50% before other exceptions or sector-specific measures, as the EO 14329 duty is “in addition to” applicable reciprocal tariffs.
- As context, U.S. officials have stated that curbing India’s purchases of Russian oil is crucial to reducing India’s tariff rate and advancing a trade deal. Reporting indicates the extra 25% duty was imposed to pressure India to halt discounted Russian crude purchases and that tariff relief has been linked to India’s actions on Russian oil.

Key definitions and references forecasters may use:
- “Ad valorem duty” refers to a duty calculated as a percentage of the value of the goods. See general definition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_valorem_tax.
- “Federal Register” is the official journal of the U.S. federal government where rules, notices, and presidential documents are published: https://www.federalregister.gov.
- “Products of India” means articles for which India is the country of origin under U.S. Customs rules; in the EO 14329 implementation, these are covered by HTSUS heading 9903.01.84 (with enumerated exceptions).

Why this question is non-trivial:
- The policy is explicitly tied to geopolitical and trade negotiations. Actions that reduce or suspend the additional duty could occur via a new executive order or an implementing/terminating notice in the Federal Register. The linkage to India’s Russian oil purchases and ongoing trade talks adds genuine uncertainty.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on official U.S. government publications between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive.

Operational question:
- Will the United States reduce or suspend the additional 25% ad valorem duty on products of India imposed under Executive Order 14329 and implemented in HTSUS heading 9903.01.84?

Definitions (for resolution purposes):
- “Additional 25% ad valorem duty on products of India” means the duty established by Executive Order 14329 (August 6, 2025) and implemented for HTSUS heading 9903.01.84 in the Federal Register Notice of August 27, 2025.
- “Reduce” means any official action that modifies HTSUS heading 9903.01.84 to set the additional ad valorem rate below 25% (but above 0%) for products of India on a general basis (i.e., a change to the heading’s rate, not merely adding or adjusting product-specific exceptions).
- “Suspend” means any official action that sets the HTSUS heading 9903.01.84 additional ad valorem rate to 0% or removes the heading such that the EO 14329 duty no longer applies to products of India on a general basis (again, not limited to product-specific exceptions).
- “Official action” means one of:
  1) A Presidential Action or Executive Order published on whitehouse.gov that explicitly reduces or suspends the EO 14329 additional duty for products of India (general application), or
  2) A Federal Register notice that modifies or removes HTSUS heading 9903.01.84 to reduce or suspend the duty (general application).
- “General basis” excludes changes that only add or alter exceptions for specific products or subheadings (e.g., carving out a particular sector under HTSUS heading 9903.01.87). Such product-specific exceptions do not count as a reduction or suspension for this question.

Resolution:
- Yes: If, within the resolution window, an official action (as defined above) is published that reduces the rate below 25% or suspends it to 0% for HTSUS heading 9903.01.84 covering products of India. The effective date of the change may be after December 31, 2025; publication within the window is sufficient.
- No: If no such official action is published within the resolution window.

Primary sources of truth:
- Federal Register (e.g., the August 27, 2025 “Notice of Implementation of Additional Duties on Products of India” establishing HTSUS 9903.01.84).
- White House Presidential Actions page for any Executive Orders or Presidential documents that modify or terminate EO 14329’s duty.

Notes for resolvers:
- Use the publication timestamp/date as shown on federalregister.gov or whitehouse.gov. If only a date is shown, treat publication as occurring on that date (UTC). If both sites publish relevant actions, the existence of either suffices for “Yes,” provided it unambiguously reduces or suspends the general duty as defined.

question: Will U.S. headline CPI-U (12‑month percent change, “all items,” U.S. city average) for November 2025 be at least 3.1%?
background:
Context and definitions
- What is being measured: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI‑U) measures the average change over time in prices paid by urban consumers for a market basket of goods and services and covers over 90% of the U.S. population. The “all items” index is the broadest, most widely used CPI‑U aggregate (often called “headline CPI”) and includes all consumer expenditure categories in the U.S. city average; taxes directly associated with purchase/use (e.g., sales and excise taxes) are included in prices.
- The statistic in question: The “12‑month percent change” (year‑over‑year, YoY) compares the index level for a given month to the same month a year earlier. Per BLS, compute it by subtracting the earlier index value from the later index value, dividing by the earlier index value, and multiplying by 100. In BLS CPI news releases, this is the rate typically summarized as “The all items index rose X percent for the 12 months ending [Month]”.
- Status quo: In the most recent published CPI release as of September 11, 2025 (covering August 2025), the all‑items CPI‑U 12‑month change was 2.9%.
- Timing and source: The November 2025 CPI (reference month) is scheduled for release on December 10, 2025 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time (ET) on the BLS site; the BLS schedule explicitly notes that all calendar times are Eastern Time. The corresponding “Consumer Price Index Summary” news release page (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.nr0.htm) will contain the official November 2025 all‑items CPI‑U 12‑month percent change used for resolution.

Why this is forecastable now
- Inflation remained near 3% YoY in late 2025 (2.9% in August), and plausible paths for September–November could move the November YoY either above or below 3.1%, making the 3.1% threshold a non‑trivial target.

Key term clarifications (used in the resolution)
- “CPI‑U”: CPI for All Urban Consumers, the broadest CPI population group.
- “All items, U.S. city average”: The headline CPI‑U aggregate across urban areas; includes all categories, with taxes directly tied to purchases included.
- “12‑month percent change”: The percent change between the index value for November 2025 and November 2024, as defined by BLS.
- Release date/time: December 10, 2025, 08:30 a.m. ET (13:30 UTC); BLS calendar notes all times are Eastern Time.
resolution_criteria:
Binary resolution (Yes/No)
- Question: Will the U.S. headline CPI‑U (12‑month percent change, “all items,” U.S. city average) for November 2025 be at least 3.1%?
- Resolve YES if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Price Index news release (“Consumer Price Index Summary”) published on December 10, 2025 reports the all‑items CPI‑U 12‑month percent change for November 2025 as greater than or equal to 3.1%; resolve NO otherwise.

What exactly to read
- Primary source: BLS “Consumer Price Index Summary” page at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.nr0.htm for the December 10, 2025 release (reference month: November 2025). Use the all‑items CPI‑U “12‑month percent change” value for the U.S. city average shown in the news release (commonly stated in the opening paragraph as “The all items index rose X percent for the 12 months ending November”) and/or in the accompanying table for the “All items” line.

Precision and tie‑breakers
- Use the 12‑month percent change value as presented by BLS in the news release. If multiple places present the value, prefer the value in the release’s tables for “All items, U.S. city average” CPI‑U if there is any discrepancy; otherwise use the figure stated in the text.
- If BLS issues a correction or erratum to the November 2025 CPI news release on or before December 31, 2025, 23:59 UTC, resolve using the corrected value; otherwise, resolve using the initially published news release value.

Scope and timing
- Event window: This question concerns only the single statistic described above for November 2025.
- Resolution timing: Resolve upon publication of the BLS release on December 10, 2025 at 08:30 a.m. ET (13:30 UTC), or upon any BLS correction/erratum issued by December 31, 2025, 23:59 UTC.

Definitions and references
- CPI and CPI‑U overview and coverage: BLS CPI FAQ and Handbook of Methods.
- Inclusion of taxes/fees in “all items”: BLS CPI technical notes.
- 12‑month percent change calculation: BLS CPI factsheet on calculating percent changes.
- Latest baseline (August 2025 YoY = 2.9%): BLS Consumer Price Index Summary for August 2025.
- Release schedule confirming December 10, 2025 at 08:30 a.m. ET for the November 2025 CPI: BLS release calendar (note: all times Eastern Time).

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the U.S. and India jointly announce a framework bilateral trade agreement that explicitly includes at least one quantified tariff reduction on goods?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Strategic intent to reach a 2025 deal: On 2025-02-13, the United States and India issued a Joint Leaders’ Statement that set “Mission 500” (aiming to grow bilateral trade to $500B by 2030) and announced plans to negotiate the first tranche of a mutually beneficial, multi‑sector Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) by fall 2025. The statement said both sides would work toward increasing market access and “reducing tariff and non‑tariff barriers.” 
- Linkage to Russian oil purchases and leverage via U.S. tariffs: As of 2025-09-26, Reuters reported U.S. negotiators told India that curbing purchases of Russian oil was “crucial to reducing [India’s] tariff rate and sealing a trade deal,” and that the U.S. imposed an extra 25% tariff on imports from India, bringing total punitive duties to around 50%, which has complicated talks described as “on a positive track” but needing more work. 
- Recent incremental tariff actions (context/base rates): In September 2023 the United States and India resolved a WTO poultry dispute; India agreed to reduce tariffs on several U.S. products, including frozen turkey/duck and various forms of blueberries and cranberries, alongside other tariff adjustments connected to the termination of multiple WTO disputes (e.g., almonds, walnuts, apples). 
  In April 2024, USTR highlighted that India further reduced its tariffs on frozen turkey, frozen duck, and fresh/frozen/dried/processed blueberries and cranberries. 
- Trade policy forum machinery: The 14th Ministerial-level India–U.S. Trade Policy Forum (TPF) in January 2024 agreed to establish a Joint Facilitative Mechanism to mitigate non-tariff barriers and to pursue a roadmap for enhanced cooperation (e.g., critical minerals, customs/trade facilitation, high-tech trade). This indicates active institutional channels for a framework arrangement. 

Key definitions for forecasters:
- Tariff: A customs duty/tax imposed by a government on imports of goods (occasionally exports). It is paid by the importer (for imports) and is typically expressed as an ad valorem rate (%) or a specific amount per unit. 
- Harmonized System (HS) code: The Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System is a standardized product classification maintained by the World Customs Organization and used by customs authorities as a basis for tariff schedules and trade statistics. HS codes are globally standardized at 6 digits, with countries allowed to add national subdivisions beyond 6 digits. 

Why this question is non-trivial now: The White House set an explicit 2025 timeline to negotiate a first tranche of a BTA with tariff reduction goals, but reporting in late September 2025 indicates U.S. demands linking trade progress and tariff relief to India’s curbing of Russian oil purchases, alongside high U.S. punitive tariffs—factors that could either catalyze concessions or derail any joint announcement before year-end.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and outcome:
- Event window: From 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
- Resolve Yes if, within the event window, the United States and India issue a joint announcement of a framework bilateral trade agreement that explicitly includes at least one quantified tariff reduction on goods, as defined below. Otherwise resolve No.

What counts as a “joint announcement” and acceptable sources:
- Joint announcement means any of the following issued within a 24-hour span that clearly reference the same agreement: (a) a single co‑branded joint statement/press release; or (b) matching statements on official government websites of both countries, each referencing the other party and the same agreement text/terms.
- Acceptable official U.S. sources include: whitehouse.gov, ustr.gov. Acceptable official Indian sources include: pib.gov.in (Press Information Bureau) and commerce.gov.in (Ministry of Commerce & Industry). If an official site is temporarily unavailable, credible wire services (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg) explicitly quoting the joint announcement are acceptable as secondary sources. 

What qualifies as a “framework bilateral trade agreement” for this market:
- A bilateral, government‑to‑government arrangement concerning trade in goods and/or services that is described in the joint announcement as one of the following or equivalent: “framework agreement,” “framework trade agreement,” “first tranche” of a Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA), “agreement in principle” on a bilateral trade deal, or a “framework”/“BTA” that the parties state they have agreed to or concluded (as opposed to merely launching, planning, or continuing negotiations). Announcements that only express an intention to negotiate or to explore an agreement do not qualify. 

Required content on tariff reductions (to qualify as “includes tariff reductions”):
- The joint announcement must contain an explicit, binding commitment by at least one party to reduce a customs duty (tariff) on imports of at least one identified good originating in the other party. It must specify the reduction in a way that is objectively verifiable, such as:
  - stating the current and new ad valorem rate (e.g., from X% to Y%) or the amount of reduction;
  - stating elimination of the tariff on a named product(s);
  - or providing a schedule/table of tariff lines (HS at 6-digit or more detailed national level) with new rates.
- The goods must be identifiable either by HS code(s) or by common product name(s) that unambiguously map to HS lines. Reductions may be unilateral or reciprocal, but they must be framed as commitments under the announced framework agreement (not merely general MFN changes unrelated to the framework). 

What does NOT qualify:
- Announcements that only include aspirations (e.g., “aim to,” “seek to”) without a definite commitment to reduce a tariff rate.
- Announcements limited to non‑tariff measures (e.g., standards cooperation, customs facilitation) with no tariff rate reduction commitment. 
- Announcements outside the event window, or leaked reports without official confirmation as defined above.

Edge cases and clarifications:
- Tariff-rate quotas (TRQs) or temporary duty suspensions count only if the announcement specifies a reduced in-quota rate or a zero rate for identified goods and ties the measure to the framework agreement; general administrative or case-by-case duty remission, export subsidies, or duty drawback do not count. 
- If multiple announcements occur, the earliest qualifying one in the event window determines resolution.
- Time is measured in UTC based on the timestamp of the official publication; if not timestamped, the earliest credible wire report timestamp in UTC citing the official announcement will be used. 

How to verify at resolution:
- Primary source: A joint statement or two matching statements on the specified official websites that include the agreement characterization (framework/BTA/first tranche/agreement in principle) and an explicit, quantified tariff reduction commitment as defined above. 
- Secondary corroboration (if official sites are inaccessible): Credible wire services (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg) quoting and linking to the joint announcement. 

Informational notes for forecasters (non‑binding examples):
- Prior, limited tariff reductions (e.g., poultry and berry products) illustrate feasible product‑level cuts but were not part of a broader bilateral framework trade deal. 
- Institutional mechanisms (TPF/JFM) may facilitate non‑tariff progress, but do not by themselves meet this question’s bar without explicit tariff cut commitments in a framework announcement. 
- The February 2025 Joint Leaders’ Statement established both the ambition (BTA by fall 2025) and the intention to reduce tariffs, raising the prospect of a qualifying announcement within the window.

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will at least €5.0 billion of principal cash derived from immobilised Russian central bank assets be transferred out of Euroclear to an EU/G7‑controlled vehicle for a Ukraine loan instrument?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- Scale and composition of the immobilised assets at Euroclear: As of June 30, 2025, Euroclear reported about €194 billion of Russian sanctioned assets on its balance sheet [13bcdc; 94adbe]. Reuters reporting and official briefings indicate that a large share of these immobilised assets have matured and become cash, with officials putting the cash share at roughly €170 billion (about 90%) by September 2025 [35c49f; 0fc4e2].
- Windfall profits (interest) vs. principal: The EU has been using windfall profits (interest/extraordinary revenues) generated by the immobilised balances to support Ukraine. In H1 2025, interest arising on cash balances from Russian‑sanctioned assets totaled about €2.7 billion, which Euroclear reports separately from principal. The EU made a first transfer of €1.5 billion of such proceeds on July 26, 2024, channelled via the European Peace Facility and the Ukraine Facility; these proceeds are explicitly described as windfall profits/extraordinary revenues, not principal. Separately, Ukraine received the first €3 billion tranche of the G7’s roughly $50 billion loan in January 2025; that loan is backed by earnings from the frozen assets, not by transfers of principal.
- Policy debate on moving principal: Belgium’s prime minister has publicly warned against moving or seizing principal, while deeming use of income acceptable, citing legal immunity and systemic risk concerns (statement of Aug 26, 2025). Meanwhile, the European Commission has floated an EU “reparations loan” concept that could involve replacing the assets at Euroclear with EU zero‑coupon bonds and placing the cash into a special‑purpose vehicle (SPV) owned by participating governments; officials argue moving the assets away from Euroclear would allow greater investment flexibility and potentially higher returns. The Commission is consulting the IMF on sizing, and press reporting in September 2025 references potential volumes up to roughly €130 billion, after accounting for obligations to the G7 loan [eddda0; 8d6501; 35c49f].

Why this question: The transfer of principal cash out of Euroclear to a designated public vehicle is a concrete event distinct from the already‑ongoing transfers of windfall profits. It is legally and politically contentious but under active discussion as of late September 2025, making both “Yes” and “No” outcomes plausible within the remainder of 2025 [d5a443; eddda0; 8d6501].

References for key facts above: Euroclear holdings and interest figures [13bcdc; 94adbe]; share now in cash [35c49f; 0fc4e2]; EU proceeds transfer July 2024 ; G7 loan first tranche Jan 2025 ; Belgian opposition ; EU/SPV proposal and rationale [eddda0; 8d6501].
resolution_criteria:
Time window and unit:
- Eligible transfers must settle between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. Amounts are measured in euros; if any qualifying transfer settles in another currency, convert to EUR at the ECB euro foreign exchange reference rate for the settlement date.

What counts (operational definitions):
- Euroclear: Euroclear Bank SA/NV, the Belgium‑based central securities depository and international central securities depository. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euroclear.
- Immobilised Russian central bank assets: Assets of the Central Bank of Russia (or other Russian sovereign monetary authorities) that were immobilised/frozen under EU sanctions from 2022 onward and are or were held via Euroclear. For the purposes of this question, “principal cash” means the cash balances arising from maturities, redemptions, and principal repayments on those immobilised assets and held on Euroclear’s balance sheet, explicitly excluding any investment income/windfall profits/extraordinary revenues generated by investing those cash balances [13bcdc; 35c49f; 94adbe].
- EU/G7‑controlled vehicle: A legal entity (e.g., an SPV) that is majority‑owned or otherwise controlled (≥50% voting/control) by: (a) an EU institution (e.g., the European Commission) or EU Member State(s), or (b) any G7 government(s) (Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States) or their designated public financial entities. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_of_Seven.
- Ukraine loan instrument: A publicly announced lending program to Ukraine in which the vehicle’s mandate explicitly references the use or management of immobilised Russian principal as collateral or source of funds (e.g., an EU “reparations loan” SPV as described by the European Commission in September 2025 press reporting) or other G7/EU‑backed loan structures if they are explicitly funded by immobilised principal (not merely backed by windfall profits) [eddda0; 8d6501].
- Transfer (for this question): A cash movement that (i) reduces Euroclear Bank’s cash balances attributable to immobilised Russian principal, and (ii) credits cash to the account(s) of an EU/G7‑controlled vehicle as defined above. Purely internal reclassifications at Euroclear or book‑entry substitutions (e.g., Euroclear receiving EU bonds while retaining the cash) do not count unless accompanied by an actual cash outflow from Euroclear to the vehicle’s accounts.

Threshold and aggregation:
- Resolve “Yes” if, in aggregate across one or more qualifying transfers within the window, the cumulative principal cash moved from Euroclear to eligible vehicle(s) is at least €5,000,000,000. Otherwise, resolve “No”. Partial transfers are summed.

Exclusions (do not count toward the threshold):
- Transfers of windfall profits, extraordinary revenues, or net profits generated from immobilised assets (e.g., the July 2024 €1.5 billion proceeds transfer) [e38420; 94adbe].
- Payments to private investors or non‑public entities; tax payments; litigation escrows; collateral postings; or any movement that leaves the cash within Euroclear while substituting securities (e.g., issuance of EU zero‑coupon bonds to Euroclear without an accompanying cash outflow).

Evidence required to resolve:
- Primary confirmation that specifies amount, timing, nature of the funds (principal derived from immobilised Russian assets), and the receiving vehicle, from at least one of: (a) European Commission/Council Press corner releases or legal acts; (b) Euroclear press releases or financial statements; (c) official statements or filings by the receiving vehicle or participating governments. Examples of typical sources include the European Commission press releases announcing proceeds transfers  and Euroclear’s periodic disclosures of sanctioned‑asset‑related figures.
- Plus corroboration by at least one reputable international wire service (e.g., Reuters). See recent Reuters explainer/coverage for context on holdings and proposals [13bcdc; eddda0; 8d6501; 35c49f].

If sources disagree, prioritize primary official documents and Euroclear disclosures; resolve “No” unless there is clear, explicit evidence meeting the above requirements.

question: Will the UK PIPR 12-month change reported in the ONS “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” bulletin be at least 5.6%?
background:
What is being forecast: This question asks whether the Office for National Statistics (ONS) will report a United Kingdom (UK) year-over-year (YoY) increase in average monthly private rents of at least 5.6% in the “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” statistical bulletin.

Key definitions and references:
- United Kingdom (UK): The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, comprising England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
- Price Index of Private Rents (PIPR): An ONS official statistic in development that measures the change in the price of renting residential property from private landlords. It is a monthly “stock” measure intended to reflect price changes across all privately rented properties, including both new and existing tenancies, and is compiled using administrative rental data (VOA, Scottish Government, Welsh Government, NIHE) with a hedonic double imputation methodology.
- 12-month change as used in ONS bulletins: In the monthly bulletin, ONS states the annual percentage change with wording such as “Average UK monthly private rents increased by X% in the 12 months to [month] (provisional estimate).” For example, the September 2025 bulletin states, “Average UK monthly private rents increased by 5.7% … in the 12 months to August 2025 (provisional estimate)”. This question will use that exact UK percentage as published in the November 2025 bulletin (which should refer to “the 12 months to October 2025”).
- Revisions: Because Northern Ireland rental data are delivered with a two‑month lag, the UK series imputes the two most recent months and revises them when data arrive; ONS expects these UK revisions to be minor. Every month ONS revises the two most recent UK estimates.
- Time standard: All dates/times in this question refer to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Recent context (status quo as of 2025-09-30):
- Mar 2025: ONS reported “Average UK monthly private rents increased by 7.7% … in the 12 months to March 2025 (provisional estimate)”.
- May 2025: “7.0% … in the 12 months to May 2025 (provisional estimate)”.
- Jul 2025: “5.9% … in the 12 months to July 2025 (provisional estimate)”.
- Aug 2025: “5.7% … in the 12 months to August 2025 (provisional estimate)”.
- Release cadence example: The September 2025 bulletin was released on 17 September 2025, and noted the next release date as 22 October 2025.

Why this is forecastable and non-trivial: PIPR is a timely national measure of private rent inflation that has been decelerating through 2025, but remains elevated versus pre‑2022 norms. The November 2025 bulletin will reflect the “12 months to October 2025” reading, which is plausibly near the current 5–6% range, making a 5.6% threshold a high‑entropy target given recent momentum and revision practices.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will the UK PIPR 12-month change reported in the ONS “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” bulletin be at least 5.6%?

Operationalization:
- Metric to extract: The percentage value appearing in the sentence within the November 2025 ONS bulletin that states the UK annual change, in the style “Average UK monthly private rents increased by X% … in the 12 months to October 2025 (provisional estimate).” The UK value (not England, not Great Britain) is the target. This wording and placement are consistent with prior bulletins.
- Threshold test: Resolve YES if X ≥ 5.6%; resolve NO if X < 5.6%.
- Rounding: Use the percentage exactly as published in that sentence (ONS typically presents one decimal place). Do not adjust for any implied additional precision.
- Revisions: Use the first value published in the initial release of the “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” bulletin. If, and only if, ONS issues a formal correction/erratum to that bulletin before 23:59:59 UTC on 31 December 2025, use the corrected value. Regular month‑to‑month revisions to the two most recent UK estimates due to Northern Ireland data lags are expected and documented by ONS, but for the purposes of this market, only the value in the initial November 2025 bulletin (or its official correction, if any) will be used.
- Source of truth: The ONS statistical bulletin “Private rent and house prices, UK: November 2025” on ons.gov.uk. Recent bulletins and phrasing examples are visible in the August and September 2025 releases. If the November 2025 bulletin is published on a different URL structure, the most directly comparable ONS page bearing that bulletin title will be used.
- Timing: Resolution will occur upon publication of that bulletin (initial release) and in any case no later than 23:59:59 UTC on 31 December 2025. All times UTC.

Outcomes:
- YES if the extracted UK annual percentage (12 months to October 2025) is ≥ 5.6%.
- NO if the extracted UK annual percentage is < 5.6%.

Notes for verifiers:
- Examples of the exact sentence structure and UK figures appear in: April 2025 (7.7%; 12 months to March) ; June 2025 (7.0%; 12 months to May) ; August 2025 (5.9%; 12 months to July) ; September 2025 (5.7%; 12 months to August; released 17 Sep 2025; next release 22 Oct 2025). These provide the template for locating the November 2025 UK value.
- Definition and revision practices for PIPR are documented in the PIPR QMI.

question: Will Blue Origin’s New Glenn launch NASA’s ESCAPADE mission between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Summary of status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- Vehicle status: Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket conducted its maiden flight (NG-1) on January 16, 2025, lifting off at 2:03 a.m. EST (0703 UTC) from Space Launch Complex 36 (SLC-36) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and reaching orbit.
- Mission overview: NASA’s ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) is a twin-spacecraft heliophysics mission to study how the solar wind interacts with Mars’ magnetic environment, managed by UC Berkeley’s Space Sciences Laboratory with NASA partners; it will use two identical spacecraft for simultaneous observations.
- Current launch plan for NG-2/ESCAPADE: As of late September 2025, NASA and Blue Origin state that New Glenn’s second mission (NG-2) carrying ESCAPADE is targeted for “later this fall” from SLC-36, Cape Canaveral. NASA’s ESCAPADE blog reported the spacecraft returned to Florida in September 2025 to prepare for launch, scheduled no earlier than this fall on New Glenn. Independent reporting indicates the launch is now expected in late October or early November 2025, with NASA’s Launch Services Program citing “very late in October, maybe the first week in November,” and noting trajectory flexibility that allows ESCAPADE to launch virtually any day in 2025 before heading to Mars in 2026. Space.com further reports Blue Origin is targeting mid-October for NG-2, with pre-launch milestones including vehicle movement and a hotfire test anticipated mid-month.
Why this is non-trivial: New Glenn has flown once, and NG-2 involves interplanetary payload integration and pre-launch testing that commonly slip. The publicly stated windows span mid-October through early November 2025, leaving meaningful uncertainty about whether liftoff will occur within the specified forecasting window.
Key references a forecaster may monitor:
- NASA ESCAPADE mission page and blog for schedule/status updates.
- NASA news releases regarding ESCAPADE launch media accreditation and date targeting.
- Blue Origin’s official New Glenn mission pages and press releases (e.g., NG-1 precedent).
- Reputable industry reporting on schedule updates (SpaceNews, Space.com).
resolution_criteria:
Outcome determination window: Events must occur between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.
Definitions and scope:
- “New Glenn” refers to Blue Origin’s orbital-class heavy-lift launch vehicle operating from SLC-36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station; it successfully flew NG-1 on January 16, 2025.
- “ESCAPADE mission” refers to NASA’s twin-spacecraft heliophysics mission to study Mars’ magnetic environment and solar wind interaction, as described by NASA Science.
- “Launch” (for resolution) means liftoff: the moment the New Glenn rocket carrying the ESCAPADE payload leaves the launch pad under its own power. Static fire tests, wet dress rehearsals, rollouts, or scrubs do not count. An abort after liftoff still counts as a launch for the purposes of this question. Blue Origin’s NG-1 press materials exemplify how liftoff times are recorded and publicly reported (e.g., “engines ignited at 2:03 a.m. EST”).
- “Carrying the ESCAPADE payload” means the launched New Glenn vehicle has the ESCAPADE spacecraft integrated and manifested for the mission, as confirmed by NASA or Blue Origin. The mission is widely described as New Glenn’s second flight (NG-2).
Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if an officially confirmed liftoff of New Glenn with the ESCAPADE payload occurs within the window defined above.
- Resolve No if no such liftoff occurs within the window.
Accepted resolution sources:
- Primary: Official confirmation from NASA (e.g., NASA Science ESCAPADE blog/mission page or NASA news releases) and/or Blue Origin’s official press releases/news posts.
- Secondary (if primary is unavailable or delayed): Reputable, independent reporting with live coverage or post-event confirmation (e.g., SpaceNews, Space.com, Reuters).
How to verify quickly on resolution date:
- Check NASA’s ESCAPADE blog/mission page for a launch update or post.
- Check Blue Origin’s newsroom for an NG-2 launch press release (NG-1 precedent shows timely publication).
- Cross-check timing within UTC window using the timestamp provided by NASA/Blue Origin or corroborated by reputable outlets.

question: By December 31, 2025 (UTC), will ACEA EU‑27 data show Tesla’s new passenger car registrations for January–November 2025 at least 30% lower than January–November 2024?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01: ACEA (the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association) publishes monthly press releases on “New passenger car registrations in Europe,” with EU‑27 figures and breakdowns that include manufacturer-level data; August 2025’s release demonstrates the cadence of these monthly, year-to-date updates, and ACEA states it provides registrations broken down by country, fuel type, and manufacturer. Reuters reported that for January–August 2025, Tesla’s sales (i.e., new registrations) in the European Union were down 42.9% year-over-year, and down 32.6% in Europe as a whole, indicating a substantial decline through late summer even as some individual markets began to show monthly rebounds. ACEA’s statistics press release calendar lists the publication date for the November 2025 passenger car registrations release (which will include January–November cumulative data) as Tuesday, 23 December 2025, ensuring availability before year-end.

Key definitions and scope:
- European Union (EU‑27): The 27 member states of the European Union; see EU entry for country list and membership. Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union (reference link only; scope in this question follows ACEA’s EU‑27 usage in its passenger-car registrations releases) [concept; ACEA monthly EU scope indicated in 4eb73f].
- New passenger car registration: The first-time registration of a new passenger vehicle, corresponding to EU vehicle category M1 (vehicles designed and constructed for the carriage of passengers, with no more than eight seats in addition to the driver’s seat). Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_classification#European_Union (reference link). In ACEA statistics, “passenger car registrations” refer to new passenger car registrations and exclude commercial vehicles; ACEA publishes these monthly for the EU.
- Tesla: The automotive marque of Tesla, Inc., as reported in ACEA’s by‑manufacturer registration tables. Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc (reference link).
- Periods compared: “January–November 2025” means registrations with registration dates from 2025‑01‑01 00:00:00 to 2025‑11‑30 23:59:59 (calendar months Jan through Nov); “January–November 2024” means registrations from 2024‑01‑01 00:00:00 to 2024‑11‑30 23:59:59. Times are expressed in UTC for clarity; ACEA aggregates by calendar month.
- Europe vs EU: This question uses EU‑27 only (ACEA’s EU scope). Figures that include EFTA and/or the UK (“Europe as a whole”) are out of scope.

Why this threshold and timing: Through Jan–Aug 2025, Tesla’s EU registrations were down 42.9% YoY, but late‑year performance (Sep–Nov) could narrow the gap, leaving realistic uncertainty around whether the full Jan–Nov decline will be ≥30%. Using Jan–Nov avoids year‑end lags in full‑year publications while capturing most of the annual cycle. The ACEA calendar shows the November release will be published on 23 December 2025, allowing resolution before year‑end.
resolution_criteria:
Yes if ACEA’s EU‑27 cumulative Tesla new passenger car registrations for January–November 2025 are at least 30% lower than the ACEA EU‑27 cumulative Tesla new passenger car registrations for January–November 2024; No otherwise.

Operationalization:
- Source of truth: The ACEA “New passenger car registrations in Europe” press release for November 2025 (published 23 December 2025 per ACEA’s calendar), together with its accompanying ‘by manufacturer’ EU‑27 table or annex, will be used to extract Tesla’s EU‑27 brand totals for Jan–Nov 2025 and Jan–Nov 2024. The monthly press releases and their YTD framing (e.g., the August 2025 release) establish the reporting cadence and EU scope.
- Computation: Let R2025 be Tesla’s EU‑27 new passenger car registrations cumulative for Jan–Nov 2025 and R2024 be Tesla’s EU‑27 cumulative for Jan–Nov 2024, as reported in ACEA’s by‑manufacturer EU‑27 table. Compute percentage change as (R2025 − R2024) / R2024. Resolve Yes if this is ≤ −30.0%; resolve No otherwise. Equivalently, Yes if R2025 ≤ 0.70 × R2024.
- Scope constraints: Use EU‑27 totals only; exclude non‑EU countries (e.g., EFTA, UK). Use passenger cars only; exclude commercial vehicles (LCVs, trucks, buses), consistent with ACEA’s passenger‑car statistics. Use Tesla brand totals; do not include other marques.
- Timing: Resolution occurs upon publication of November 2025 ACEA passenger‑car registrations (EU‑27) and its by‑manufacturer table, expected on 2025‑12‑23 per ACEA’s press release calendar; in any case, resolution will be made using the latest available ACEA November 2025 EU‑27 passenger‑car registrations data as of 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC.

Notes on validation: Background context on the 2025 YTD decline comes from Reuters’ report citing January–August 2025 declines for Tesla in the EU and Europe as a whole; this context is for forecasting background only and is not used directly in resolution. ACEA’s reliable statistics page affirms availability of manufacturer‑level registration breakdowns, and the August 2025 press release demonstrates monthly YTD reporting and EU scope.

question: Will Ulta Beauty report Q3 FY2025 comparable sales growth of at least 5.0%?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- Metric and definition: Ulta Beauty reports “comparable sales” as a key operating metric. In recent press releases, Ulta defines comparable sales as “sales for stores open at least 14 months and e-commerce sales”. Ulta’s 2025 Form 10-K further clarifies that comparable sales include retail sales, salon services, and e-commerce; stores are included beginning on the first day of the 14th month of operation; remodeled stores remain in the comp base unless closed for part of the period; and in 53-week fiscal years the 53rd week is included, with the following year’s comparison shifted by one week to align comparable calendar weeks. Ulta’s fiscal year consists of 52 or 53 weeks ending on the Saturday closest to January 31. For additional general context, same-store/comparable sales in retail refers to the revenue change of existing outlets over a period compared to the same period a year earlier, excluding new or closed outlets.
- Latest results: In Q2 FY2025 (thirteen weeks ended August 2, 2025), Ulta reported comparable sales growth of 6.7% year-over-year and raised its full-year FY2025 comparable sales guidance to 2.5%–3.5%.
- Disclosure timing: Ulta’s IR calendar lists a “Q3 2025 Ulta Beauty Earnings Conference Call” on December 4, 2025, indicating Q3 FY2025 results will be released and discussed on or around that date.
Why this is interesting: Q2 comps were robust (+6.7%), but the full-year guide (2.5%–3.5%) implies more modest run-rate growth, and Q3 spans early holiday activity where promotional intensity and demand can swing outcomes. This makes a 5.0% threshold plausibly uncertain for Q3 FY2025.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve Yes if Ulta’s Q3 FY2025 press release states that comparable sales for the quarter increased by at least 5.0% year-over-year; resolve No if it states a figure below 5.0%.

Key definitions and rules:
- “Comparable sales” means Ulta’s company-reported comparable sales metric, which includes retail, salon services, and e-commerce; stores enter the comp base on the first day of the 14th month of operation; remodeled stores remain unless closed for part of the period; 52/53-week rules apply as described in Ulta’s filings. Ulta press releases describe this as “sales for stores open at least 14 months and e-commerce sales”.
- “Q3 FY2025” refers to Ulta’s third fiscal quarter of FY2025 as defined by the company’s fiscal calendar (a 52/53-week fiscal year ending on the Saturday closest to January 31).
- “At least 5.0%” means greater than or equal to 5.0%. The determination will use the percentage exactly as presented in the source document. If Ulta reports the figure to one decimal place, that displayed rounded figure governs. If a more precise figure is presented (e.g., in tables), that precise figure governs if it clearly refers to the overall company comparable sales for the quarter.
- If multiple comparable-sales-related figures are given (e.g., by channel, transactions, ticket), only the overall company “comparable sales” percentage for the quarter is used. Do not use year-to-date figures.
- Corrections: If Ulta issues an official correction to the press release or filing by 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, the corrected figure governs.

Primary source of truth:
- Ulta Beauty’s Q3 FY2025 earnings press release posted on the company’s Investor Relations website on or around December 4, 2025.

Fallback sources (used only if the press release is not available or is ambiguous by 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025):
1) Ulta’s Form 10-Q for Q3 FY2025 filed with the U.S. SEC (EDGAR), using the overall company comparable sales percentage for the quarter as defined above.
2) If neither the press release nor the 10-Q is available by the resolution deadline, use credible mainstream reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, WSJ) that directly quotes Ulta’s reported Q3 FY2025 comparable sales percentage.

Timing and timezone:
- The question resolves upon the first eligible source’s publication, with any corrections through 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025 considered. All dates/times are in UTC.

Notes to forecasters:
- As of Q2 FY2025, comparable sales growth was 6.7%, and full-year FY2025 comparable sales guidance was 2.5%–3.5%. Q3 FY2025 results are scheduled to be discussed on December 4, 2025 per Ulta’s IR calendar.

question: By 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, will the FOMC’s target federal funds rate midpoint be at least 75 basis points lower than on September 22, 2025?
background:
Context and definitions a forecaster should know:
- Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC): the policy-setting body of the U.S. Federal Reserve System that sets the target range for the federal funds rate. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Open_Market_Committee
- Federal funds rate (target range): since December 2008 the FOMC has typically expressed policy as a target range (lower limit and upper limit) for the federal funds rate, and announces changes via official press releases on the Federal Reserve Board’s website under News & Events → Press Releases → Monetary Policy (FOMC statements). See: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases.htm (select Monetary Policy/FOMC statements for 2025)
- Basis point (bp or bps): for purposes of this question, 1 basis point = 0.01 percentage point. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basis_point
- Midpoint (of the target range): defined here as the arithmetic average of the upper and lower limits of the target range, i.e., midpoint = (upper limit + lower limit) / 2.

Status quo as of 2025-09-22:
- The FOMC communicates and updates the target range by statement; intermeeting actions are possible. Forecasters should track the latest FOMC statements (Monetary Policy press releases) on the Federal Reserve Board’s site (see link above). For convenient daily series indicating the upper and lower limits, see the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED) series “Federal Funds Target Range – Upper Limit” (DFEDTARU) and “Federal Funds Target Range – Lower Limit” (DFEDTARL):
  - DFEDTARU: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFEDTARU
  - DFEDTARL: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFEDTARL

Why this has forecasting value:
- The magnitude of cumulative cuts through year-end 2025 is uncertain and depends on inflation, growth, and labor-market data, as well as the FOMC’s reaction function. A 75 bp threshold is large enough to be economically meaningful while plausibly achievable or not, yielding non-trivial disagreement among informed forecasters.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and evaluation instants:
- Start date/time: 2025-09-22 00:00:00 UTC.
- End date/time: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Definitions for this market:
- “Target range” means the FOMC’s stated range for the federal funds rate (lower limit and upper limit) as officially announced by the FOMC in press releases on the Federal Reserve Board’s website under News & Events → Press Releases → Monetary Policy (FOMC statements): https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases.htm (filter by Monetary Policy/FOMC statements).
- “Midpoint” means the arithmetic average of the target range’s upper and lower limits, computed as midpoint = (upper limit + lower limit) / 2.
- “Basis point (bp/bps)” is defined as 0.01 percentage point; 75 bps = 0.75 percentage points.

What is being measured:
- Let M0 be the midpoint of the FOMC target range “in effect” at 2025-09-22 00:00:00 UTC.
- Let M1 be the midpoint of the FOMC target range “in effect” at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
- Resolve YES if M1 ≤ (M0 − 0.75 percentage points). Resolve NO otherwise. Exactly 75 bps of cumulative reduction qualifies as YES.

Primary resolution source and procedure:
1) Identify, on the Federal Reserve Board’s official website, the FOMC statement(s) establishing the target range in effect at each evaluation instant (M0 and M1). Use the most recent FOMC statement whose effective date/time precedes or equals the evaluation instant. The authoritative page is the Board’s News & Events → Press Releases (Monetary Policy/FOMC statements): https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases.htm
2) From the identified statement, extract the stated target range (e.g., “X to Y percent”). Compute the midpoint as defined above.

Secondary sources and tie-breakers:
- As a convenience cross-check, the FRED daily series DFEDTARU (upper limit) and DFEDTARL (lower limit) may be used to corroborate the range that is in effect on the evaluation dates:
  - DFEDTARU: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFEDTARU
  - DFEDTARL: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFEDTARL
- If there is any discrepancy between FRED and the Federal Reserve Board’s official FOMC statements, the Federal Reserve Board’s statements prevail.

Edge cases and clarifications:
- Intermeeting actions: If the FOMC changes the target range between meetings, the change counts if it is in effect at the evaluation instant.
- Single-point target contingency: If, at either evaluation instant, the FOMC expresses policy as a single-point target (not a range), interpret the lower limit = upper limit = that target; the midpoint equals that target.
- Time zone: All times in this question are UTC. Only the target range “in effect” at the exact evaluation instants (as above) is used; the path taken during the interval is irrelevant.

question: UK Online Safety enforcement: Will Ofcom publish a confirmation decision imposing a financial penalty on 4chan’s provider by 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Status quo as of October 1, 2025: Ofcom opened a formal investigation into the provider of 4chan (4chan Community Support LLC) on June 10, 2025, regarding compliance with duties to protect users from illegal content and with statutory information requests under the UK Online Safety Act 2023. In August 2025, BBC reporting noted that Ofcom issued 4chan a provisional notice of contravention for failing to comply with two information requests, and that counsel for 4chan stated it would refuse to pay proposed fines (including an initial £20,000 and daily penalties thereafter). Ofcom’s enforcement guidance explains the process from a provisional notice of contravention to a confirmation decision, including imposing financial penalties and the possibility of daily penalties when contraventions continue. Ofcom typically publishes a non-confidential version of final decisions imposing penalties on its official website; for example, its "Final Decision" in the MintStars case details a contravention and financial penalty and is published as a PDF on ofcom.org.uk.

Definitions and context a forecaster should know:
- Ofcom: The UK communications regulator (Office of Communications). For general reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ofcom
- Online Safety Act 2023 (OSA): UK law regulating online services’ safety duties. For the statute: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/50/contents/enacted
- Provider of 4chan: The legal entity identified by Ofcom as providing the 4chan service; currently 4chan Community Support LLC per Ofcom’s investigation page.
- Provisional notice of contravention: A notice issued by Ofcom under OSA s.130 when it has reasonable grounds to believe a provider has failed/is failing to comply with enforceable requirements; it sets out provisional findings, may include a provisional penalty determination, and invites representations.
- Confirmation decision: A final decision issued by Ofcom under OSA s.132 after considering representations, confirming findings of contravention and specifying any requirements and/or financial penalties; publication of a non-confidential version on Ofcom’s website follows closure of the investigation.
- Financial penalty (monetary penalty): A penalty Ofcom may impose up to the higher of £18 million or 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue; penalties may be single or daily (continuing) and are detailed in the decision/penalty notice.

Key sources to track:
- Ofcom’s 4chan investigation page: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/online-safety/illegal-and-harmful-content/investigation-into-4chan-and-its-compliance-with-duties-to-protect-its-users-from-illegal-content 
- Ofcom Online Safety Enforcement Guidance (definitions/process): https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/online-safety/information-for-industry/illegal-harms/online-safety-enforcement-guidance.pdf 
- Example publication format for final decisions (MintStars): https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/online-safety/enforcement/final-decision-investigation-into-mintstars-ltd-compliance-with-rules-to-protect-children-from-restricted-material.pdf 
- August 2025 BBC report on 4chan’s stance and Ofcom’s provisional action: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cq68j5g2nr1o 

Why this is high-entropy: The existence of a provisional notice and stated intent to resist paying, plus potential litigation and extraterritorial issues, make the timing and likelihood of a 2025 confirmation decision imposing a penalty uncertain. Ofcom’s process requires consideration of representations and then issuance of a decision; the pace and outcome are not predetermined.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone: Eligible events must occur between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025. Resolution will occur shortly after the end of this window.

Question resolves Yes if all of the following are true by 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025:
1) Ofcom publishes on its official website (ofcom.org.uk) a non-confidential, final decision document that:
   a) Is a confirmation decision under OSA s.132 (or an equivalent final penalty notice under the Act) concerning the 4chan service’s provider; and
   b) Explicitly imposes a financial penalty (any amount > £0), either as a single amount and/or a daily (continuing) penalty, on the provider identified by Ofcom as operating 4chan (currently 4chan Community Support LLC).
2) The published document clearly identifies the contravention(s) under the Online Safety Act and states the penalty imposed, consistent with Ofcom’s enforcement guidance and publication practices (e.g., a non-confidential "Final Decision" PDF or equivalent page).

Question resolves No if:
- No such confirmation decision (or final penalty notice) imposing a financial penalty on the provider of 4chan is published by Ofcom on its official website by the deadline; or
- Only a provisional notice of contravention is in place without a final decision imposing a penalty.

Scope clarifications:
- "Publish" means Ofcom has made publicly available on ofcom.org.uk a non-confidential version of the decision/penalty document. Ofcom’s enforcement guidance states it publishes non-confidential versions after closing investigations.
- "Provider of 4chan" means the entity Ofcom names as the provider for the 4chan service in the investigation/decision. As of today, this is 4chan Community Support LLC. If Ofcom identifies a successor provider in the decision, that will count.
- Press reports, social media posts, or third-party commentary do not by themselves constitute publication; the source of truth is Ofcom’s official website.
- Business disruption measures, directions without a financial penalty, or criminal actions are out of scope for a Yes.

Primary resolution sources:
- Ofcom’s 4chan investigation page and Online Safety enforcement pages on ofcom.org.uk (for publication of provisional and final decisions).
- Example of how a final decision imposing a penalty is typically formatted and published: Ofcom’s MintStars Final Decision.

Context claims and sources: Investigation opening date and provider name ; provisional notice in August and refusal to pay ; enforcement process and publication practices ; example final decision publication.

question: Between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025 (UTC), will the U.S. FDA approve Novo Nordisk’s oral semaglutide for a chronic weight management indication?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30: Novo Nordisk submitted a New Drug Application (NDA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for an investigational, once-daily, 25 mg oral formulation of semaglutide (described as an oral version of Wegovy) for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight (with comorbidities), and for reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in adults with overweight/obesity and established cardiovascular disease. The FDA accepted this NDA on May 2, 2025, with the sponsor stating the FDA’s action date is in Q4 2025. Novo Nordisk confirmed the submission in company materials, indicating oral semaglutide 25 mg for obesity was filed for U.S. regulatory review. Coverage by BioPharma Dive and FiercePharma reported the submission occurred in April 2025. Efficacy data published in the New England Journal of Medicine reported mean body weight loss of −13.6% over 64 weeks versus −2.2% for placebo with oral semaglutide 25 mg, along with improvements in BMI, waist circumference, and physical function scores. As context, semaglutide is a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist marketed as Wegovy for weight management (injectable), Ozempic and Rybelsus for diabetes (Rybelsus is an oral formulation at lower doses than those proposed for obesity).

Definitions and sources: 
- FDA approval and NDA: An NDA is the formal proposal to request approval to market a new drug in the U.S.; FDA approval signifies the agency has determined the drug is safe and effective for proposed use(s), labeling is appropriate, and manufacturing controls are adequate. 
- Drugs@FDA database: FDA’s Drugs@FDA is the authoritative database of drug products approved since 1939 and includes labels, approval letters, reviews, and approval histories; it is updated daily and will be used as a primary resolution source. 
- Semaglutide: A GLP-1 receptor agonist used for diabetes and obesity under brands Ozempic, Rybelsus (oral), and Wegovy (injectable). 

Why this is forecastable now: The FDA’s target decision window is Q4 2025, which overlaps the resolution window for this question; outcomes include approval, a Complete Response Letter (non-approval), or an extension past year-end. Approval is not guaranteed, creating meaningful uncertainty.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone: Eligible events must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive).

Question subject: The NDA accepted by FDA on May 2, 2025 for an oral semaglutide product submitted by Novo Nordisk for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight (with one or more comorbid conditions), and reduction of MACE in adults with overweight/obesity and established cardiovascular disease.

Key term definitions: 
- “FDA approval”: A final approval decision by FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) on the relevant NDA, as evidenced by FDA records (approval letter/approval history) or official FDA news communication. FDA approval of an NDA indicates the drug is safe and effective for the proposed use(s), labeling is appropriate, and manufacturing controls are adequate. 
- “Oral semaglutide product”: A drug product whose active ingredient is semaglutide and whose labeled route of administration is oral (e.g., tablet). 
- “Chronic weight management indication”: Labeling that includes use for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, consistent with how Wegovy injection is labeled for weight management; the precise wording may vary, but must clearly indicate weight management in adults with obesity or overweight (not solely cardiovascular risk reduction).

Resolution rule (Yes/No): 
- Resolve Yes if, within the time window, FDA grants approval to Novo Nordisk’s oral semaglutide NDA and the approved labeling includes a chronic weight management indication for adults with obesity or overweight. 
- Resolve No if, by the end of the time window, FDA has not issued such an approval (e.g., issues a Complete Response Letter/non-approval, extends the review beyond December 31, 2025 UTC, or approves only a cardiovascular risk reduction indication without a chronic weight management indication).

Primary resolution sources: 
1) FDA’s Drugs@FDA database entry/approval history for the relevant oral semaglutide NDA (access via https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/), showing an approval date within the window and labeling that includes a chronic weight management indication. 
2) Alternatively, an official FDA press announcement (newsroom) on fda.gov indicating approval within the window with clear reference to an oral semaglutide product for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight.

Non-sources and exclusions: 
- Sponsor or third-party press releases (e.g., Novo Nordisk, Reuters, or trade publications) are insufficient on their own. Use FDA sources above for resolution. 
- Approvals or announcements outside the time window; approvals in other jurisdictions (e.g., EMA) do not count.

Operational notes: 
- If FDA approves both weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction indications together, this counts as Yes (weight management present). If FDA approves only the cardiovascular risk reduction indication without weight management within the window, resolve No. 
- If FDA approves under a different proprietary name than “Wegovy” but meets the criteria (oral semaglutide, Novo Nordisk, weight management indication), resolve Yes.

question: October 2025 U.S. CPI (headline YoY) ≥ 3.0%
background:
Definition and scope. For this market, “headline CPI YoY” means the 12‑month percent change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI‑U), U.S. city average, All Items, 1982–84=100, not seasonally adjusted, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) in its national Consumer Price Index Summary news release. Headline inflation refers to the aggregate CPI including volatile components such as food and energy. BLS commonly phrases this figure as “Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased X percent before seasonal adjustment” in the national CPI news release.

Status quo as of 2025‑09‑30. The latest published national CPI news release (August 2025 data, released September 11, 2025) reports: “Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 2.9 percent before seasonal adjustment”. The same release states that “The Consumer Price Index for September 2025 is scheduled to be released on Wednesday, October 15, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. (ET)”.

Release timing for October 2025 CPI. The BLS “Schedule of Selected Releases” lists the October 2025 CPI news release for Thursday, November 13, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time (13:30 UTC). The calendar notes that all listed times are Eastern Time.

Why this is non‑trivial. The 12‑month headline CPI outcome reflects multiple moving components (e.g., energy, food, shelter, core goods/services), and forecasters may incorporate data such as commodity moves, housing measures, and monthly CPI sub‑index trends. The threshold (3.0%) is close to the latest reading (2.9% for August 2025), creating genuine uncertainty around whether October 2025’s 12‑month change rounds to ≥3.0%.
resolution_criteria:
Yes if the BLS national Consumer Price Index Summary (news release) for October 2025, published on bls.gov, reports the headline CPI 12‑month percent change (U.S. city average CPI‑U, All Items, 1982–84=100, not seasonally adjusted) as at least 3.0%; No otherwise.

Operational details:
- Source of truth: the BLS national CPI news release webpage (“Consumer Price Index Summary”) for October 2025 on bls.gov. The figure will be taken from the sentence of the form “Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased X percent before seasonal adjustment,” consistent with BLS phrasing used in recent releases.
- Release timing: Scheduled for Thursday, November 13, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time (13:30 UTC). Resolution occurs upon publication of the October 2025 CPI news release or any official correction posted by BLS by December 31, 2025.
- Measurement specifics: Use the 12‑month percent change for the U.S. city average CPI‑U, All Items, not seasonally adjusted, as explicitly defined by BLS. The decision threshold is based on the percent figure as reported by BLS; no independent recalculation or alternative data series will be used.
- Revisions and corrections: If BLS issues an erratum or correction to the October 2025 CPI news release by December 31, 2025, the corrected figure will be used. Any revisions or methodological changes posted after December 31, 2025, will not affect resolution.
- Time window: The question concerns the October 2025 CPI YoY figure and resolves no later than December 31, 2025, based on the BLS publication schedule.

question: Will the FOMC change the federal funds rate target range at its October 28–29, 2025 meeting?
background:
Status quo and context as of 2025-09-30:
- Meeting schedule and timing: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has a regularly scheduled two‑day meeting on October 28–29, 2025, with a policy statement customarily released at 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the second day and a press conference thereafter. The Federal Reserve’s October 2025 calendar lists “FOMC Meeting – Two-day meeting, October 28–October 29” and notes a press conference on the 29th.
- Current target range: At its September 16–17, 2025 meeting, the FOMC decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4 to 4‑1/4 percent, as stated in the post‑meeting statement. The accompanying Implementation Note directs operations to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4 to 4‑1/4 percent, effective September 18, 2025.

Key definitions and notes for forecasters:
- Federal funds rate target range: For the purposes of this question, this is the numeric lower and upper bounds (in percent) for the federal funds rate targeted by the FOMC, as stated in the FOMC post‑meeting statement and/or accompanying Implementation Note published on FederalReserve.gov. Examples of this phrasing and format are shown in the September 17, 2025 statement and Implementation Note.
- FOMC post‑meeting statement: The Federal Reserve press release titled “Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement,” posted on FederalReserve.gov for each meeting (see, e.g., the September 17, 2025 statement).
- Meeting identification: The meeting at issue is the regularly scheduled FOMC meeting that begins on October 28, 2025, as listed on the Federal Reserve’s calendar.

Why this is forecastable: The October 28–29 meeting falls within the resolution window and follows a recent policy move (September 2025), making a further change plausible but uncertain. The Fed publishes authoritative statements on its website that allow for unambiguous verification.
resolution_criteria:
Outcome: Resolve “Yes” if the FOMC post‑meeting statement on FederalReserve.gov for the October 28–29, 2025 meeting announces a federal funds rate target range whose lower or upper bound differs from the target range announced in the post‑meeting statement for the immediately preceding regularly scheduled meeting (September 16–17, 2025). Otherwise, resolve “No”.

What to compare:
- Prior reference value: The target range announced in the September 17, 2025 post‑meeting statement (and, if needed to confirm numeric bounds, its Implementation Note) serves as the baseline for comparison; as of that meeting, the range was 4 to 4‑1/4 percent.
- Target meeting value: The target range as stated in the October 28–29, 2025 meeting’s post‑meeting statement (and/or its Implementation Note, if needed for numeric precision). The statement is customarily released on day two of the meeting; the Federal Reserve’s tentative schedule notes a 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time release for these statements.

Definitions for resolution:
- “Different” means any change in either the lower or upper bound of the stated target range (numeric inequality at either bound suffices).
- “FOMC post‑meeting statement” refers to the Federal Reserve press release titled “Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement” for the relevant meeting, as posted on FederalReserve.gov (see the September 17, 2025 example).
- “Federal funds rate target range” refers to the numeric bounds for the target range specified by the FOMC, as published in the statement and/or the Implementation Note (see examples from September 17–18, 2025).

Scope and edge cases:
- Intermeeting actions: Any intermeeting change prior to October 28, 2025 does not, by itself, determine resolution. Only the range announced in the October 28–29, 2025 post‑meeting statement is compared to the September 16–17, 2025 statement for the purpose of this question.
- Schedule changes: If no FOMC post‑meeting statement is published for a meeting that begins on October 28, 2025 (e.g., due to cancellation), resolve “No.” The identification of the meeting date comes from the Federal Reserve’s published calendar.

Source(s) of truth to check on resolution date:
- FederalReserve.gov page for the October 28–29, 2025 “Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement.” If needed to verify the numeric bounds, use the accompanying Implementation Note. The prior‑meeting baseline is the September 17, 2025 statement and Implementation Note.
- For meeting timing context, consult the FOMC’s tentative schedule announcement and the October 2025 calendar on FederalReserve.gov.

question: Will the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season end with at least 15 named storms?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01 (UTC):
- NOAA’s seasonal outlook (May 22, 2025) forecast 13–19 total named storms (maximum sustained winds ≥39 mph), with a 60% chance of an above-normal season, 30% near-normal, and 10% below-normal. The season runs June 1–November 30.
- NOAA’s August 7 update revised the expected range to 13–18 named storms and noted the ranges are inclusive of storms that had already formed by that date.
