- Through the morning of Sept. 29, 2025, nine named storms and three hurricanes had formed; this was one named storm and two hurricanes below the average pace through the end of September, according to the National Hurricane Center (NHC) as reported by Weather.com. The New York Times also reported Imelda as the ninth named storm by Oct. 1, 2025. The NHC 2025 advisory archive lists the named Atlantic systems to date (Andrea, Barry, Chantal, Dexter, Erin, Fernand, Gabrielle, Humberto, Imelda). The NHC’s season summary page likewise showed nine named storms and three hurricanes through Sept. 30, 2025.

Key definitions and scope:
- Named storm (Atlantic): A tropical or subtropical cyclone in the Atlantic basin that the NHC officially assigns a name from World Meteorological Organization (WMO) lists. Tropical storms (34–63 kt; 39–73 mph) and hurricanes (≥64 kt; ≥74 mph) are named; subtropical storms (≥34 kt) are also named. NHC uses 1-minute average sustained winds for intensity. See: NHC Glossary definitions for Tropical Storm and Hurricane , Subtropical Cyclone/Storm , and NHC explanation of WMO-maintained name lists.
- Atlantic hurricane season: Officially runs from June 1 to November 30, though named storms can occur outside these dates; the NHC’s final season total for 2025 is the authoritative count for this question.

Why this is forecast-relevant now: With nine named storms recorded by Sept. 29 and NOAA’s updated range at 13–18, whether the final 2025 total reaches ≥15 remains plausibly above or below the threshold given variability in late-season activity.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve “Yes” if the National Hurricane Center’s final 2025 North Atlantic season total lists 15 or more named storms; otherwise resolve “No.”

Primary source of truth:
- NHC “North Atlantic Tropical Weather Summary (2025)” on the NHC Tropical Cyclone Reports index (nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/). The final “Named Storms” total reported for the 2025 Atlantic season on this page will be used for resolution.

Fallback if the primary source is not finalized by 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025:
- Use the NHC 2025 Atlantic Tropical Cyclone Advisory Archive (nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2025/) to count the number of named Atlantic systems listed for 2025. Count each system that the archive lists under the Atlantic basin with an assigned name (e.g., Andrea, Barry, …), regardless of whether it was tropical or subtropical, and regardless of subsequent transitions (post-tropical, extratropical), consistent with NHC naming practice and intensity thresholds (Tropical Storm: 34–63 kt; Hurricane: ≥64 kt; Subtropical Storm: ≥34 kt). If the count is ≥15, resolve “Yes”; otherwise, “No.”

Additional rules:
- In the event of discrepancy between sources, the NHC season summary page  supersedes the archive count.
- All dates/times are in UTC.
- This question concerns the Atlantic basin totals as defined and reported by the NHC; no other basin’s activity is relevant.

question: Will any candidate be elected on the first count in Ireland’s 2025 presidential election?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- Polling day and times: The 2025 Irish presidential election will be held on Friday, 24 October 2025, with polling from 7:00 to 22:00 local time, as set by the Presidential Election Order made by the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage on 3 September 2025. RTÉ likewise notes polling on Friday 24 October, with counting beginning at 09:00 the following day (Saturday, 25 October).
- Official results publication: The Presidential Returning Officer’s official site states that results will be available on Saturday, 25 October 2025 at https://www.presidentialelection.ie/election-results/index.html. That results section includes fields for the national “Quota,” “Valid Poll,” first count “1st preference votes,” and first count status, indicating it will publish the first-count totals and the quota used to determine a first-count election.
- Voting system and what the first count means: The election uses preferential voting (PR–STV) for a single office; voters rank candidates 1, 2, 3…. After polling, ballot papers are sorted by first preferences and the number of first-preference votes for each candidate is reported to the Presidential Returning Officer; this is the “first count”. The Presidential Returning Officer calculates the “quota,” and in a single-seat presidential contest a candidate who receives a number of votes equal to or greater than fifty percent of valid votes plus one is declared elected; if no one reaches the quota on the first count, the lowest candidate is excluded and votes are transferred until a candidate reaches the quota.
- Field of candidates (as of close of nominations): The official Notice of Poll lists three candidates on the ballot: CATHERINE MARTINA ANN CONNOLLY (Independent TD), JIM GAVIN, and HEATHER HUMPHREYS. With three candidates, a first-count win is plausible but not assured.
Key definitions and where to find them on official sources:
- Presidential Returning Officer (PRO): The official who ascertains and declares the result based on reports from local returning officers and publishes results on the official site.
- First count: The initial national aggregation of first-preference votes (the ‘1’ rankings) reported to the PRO after ballots are sorted by first preferences.
- Valid votes / Valid Poll: Ballots deemed valid under Irish electoral rules and counted toward the result; the official results page displays “Valid Poll” and “Invalid Ballot Papers,” which the PRO uses to compute the quota.
- Quota: The number of votes necessary for election; for this single-winner election it is defined as fifty percent of valid votes plus one, as calculated and applied by the PRO.
Primary sources for resolution include: the PRO’s results page and any associated official notices/declarations on https://www.presidentialelection.ie/. RTÉ provides an authoritative procedural overview and timing of count commencement (09:00 on 25 October).
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will any candidate be elected on the first count in Ireland’s 2025 presidential election between 00:00 UTC on 15 October 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on 31 December 2025?

Operational definitions:
- Presidential Returning Officer (PRO): The official in charge of ascertaining and declaring the result of the presidential election based on constituency reports, as described in official guidance. For the 2025 election, the PRO publishes results at https://www.presidentialelection.ie/election-results/index.html.
- First count: The initial tally of first-preference votes (the ‘1’ rankings) for each candidate, aggregated nationally after local counts and reported to the PRO; this is the first published count on the PRO site.
- First-preference vote: A vote marked with the numeral ‘1’ beside a candidate’s name under Ireland’s preferential PR–STV system.
- Valid votes / Valid Poll: Ballots judged valid and included in the “Valid Poll” figure displayed on the PRO’s results page; invalid ballot papers are excluded.
- Quota (for this election): The number of votes necessary for election in a single-winner contest, defined as fifty percent of valid votes plus one and calculated by the PRO; the PRO will display the official “Quota” on the results page.

Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if, according to the final official national first-count results published by the PRO, at least one candidate’s first-preference total is equal to or greater than the official Quota on the first count (i.e., the candidate is declared elected on the first count). Otherwise resolve No.

Source of truth and where to look:
- Primary source: The PRO’s official results page for the 2025 election at https://www.presidentialelection.ie/election-results/index.html and any associated official notices/declarations on the same site. Use the final figures as they stand after any recounts concluded before resolution (see below).

Timing and contingencies:
- Event window: Only outcomes determined and published between 00:00 UTC on 2025-10-15 and 23:59:59 UTC on 2025-12-31 are eligible for resolution.
- Recounts: If there is a recount or re-examination that alters the first-count totals or quota before the declaration, use the final official figures at the time the PRO declares the result; recount procedures exist under Irish election rules. If a recount is ordered and not concluded by 2025-12-31, postpone resolution until completion or resolve N/A if no definitive first-count figures are available by that date.
- Publication delay/backup: If the PRO website is unavailable for more than 72 hours after the declaration, resolve based on consistent, credible reporting from mainstream outlets (e.g., RTÉ, BBC, Reuters, AP) explicitly stating whether a candidate was elected on the first count, and corroborate when the PRO site becomes available again.

Notes for resolvers:
- The candidates on the 2025 ballot (per the official Notice of Poll) are Catherine Connolly, Jim Gavin, and Heather Humphreys. The official results page indicates it will publish the first count, the Valid Poll, and the Quota, which are the only figures needed to apply this criterion.

question: Between October 15 and December 31, 2025 (UTC), will Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. and Paramount, a Skydance Corporation, publicly disclose that they have entered into a binding definitive agreement to merge or for one to acquire the other?
background:
Status quo as of October 1, 2025:
- Paramount Global and Skydance Media completed their merger on August 7, 2025, creating the combined parent company "Paramount, a Skydance Corporation" (also referenced in SEC filings as "Paramount Skydance Corporation"). The company’s press releases and investor relations materials confirm the new name and that Class B shares trade on Nasdaq under the ticker PSKY. The SEC Form 8-K filed on August 7, 2025 details the closing mechanics and uses the registrant name Paramount Skydance Corporation.
- Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) announced on June 9, 2025 plans to separate into two publicly traded companies by mid-2026—“Streaming & Studios” and “Global Networks”—including component lists and leadership roles, via its investor relations press release. WBD maintains a Financial News section on its IR website where such press releases are published.
- Media reporting in September 2025 indicates that Paramount, a Skydance Corporation, is exploring or preparing a majority-cash bid to acquire WBD; these reports describe an exploratory stage, not a signed agreement, and note that neither company commented at that time. The New York Times coverage provides additional market context, including WBD’s approximate valuation (~$41B) and debt (~$35B) and notes the strategic implications of any potential deal.

Key definitions and data sources forecasters may rely on:
- Merger and acquisition: A merger is the legal consolidation of two business entities into one; an acquisition occurs when one entity takes ownership of another’s share capital, equity interests, or assets.
- Material Definitive Agreement disclosures: U.S. public companies disclose entry into certain material, binding agreements not made in the ordinary course of business via Form 8-K Item 1.01; this is the standard mechanism by which definitive M&A agreements are publicly disclosed.
- Official press releases: Paramount, a Skydance Corporation publishes press releases on its IR site (e.g., its August 7, 2025 merger completion release) , and WBD publishes press releases on its IR site.

Why this question has non-trivial uncertainty:
- Industry consolidation remains plausible following Paramount’s recent merger and WBD’s stated plan to separate businesses by mid-2026, creating potential transaction structures (e.g., agreements contingent on the separation).
- Reputable reporting in September 2025 suggests active exploration by Paramount, but no binding agreement had been announced as of those reports.

Time window:
- Eligible announcements must occur between October 15, 2025 00:00:00 UTC and December 31, 2025 23:59:59 UTC.
resolution_criteria:
Resolve YES if, between October 15, 2025 00:00:00 UTC and December 31, 2025 23:59:59 UTC, either of the following public disclosures occurs, clearly stating that Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. (WBD) and Paramount, a Skydance Corporation (also referenced as Paramount Skydance Corporation in SEC filings) have entered into a binding definitive agreement to merge or for one to acquire the other:

- A joint press release, or separate press releases issued by both WBD and Paramount, published on their official corporate newsroom or investor relations websites, explicitly announcing that a definitive agreement has been signed (e.g., merger agreement, stock purchase agreement) under which either (a) the companies will legally merge into one parent entity, or (b) one company will acquire the other such that the acquirer will become the legal parent controlling the target.

OR

- A Form 8-K filed on EDGAR by either WBD or Paramount that discloses entry into a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01 establishing a merger or acquisition between the two companies as defined above. The 8-K must name the counterparty as Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. or Paramount (Paramount Skydance Corporation) and describe a merger or acquisition, not merely exploratory talks or non-binding documents.

Definitions for resolution:
- "Definitive agreement": A legally binding contract that sets out agreed terms for a merger or acquisition. For U.S. public companies, such agreements are typically disclosed via Form 8-K Item 1.01, which requires reporting entry into material binding agreements not made in the ordinary course.
- "Merger": Legal consolidation of two business entities into one.
- "Acquisition": One entity takes ownership of another entity’s share capital, equity interests, or assets such that the acquirer becomes the controlling parent of the target.
- "Announce": Publish an official press release on the company’s newsroom or investor relations website, or file a Form 8-K that discloses entry into a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01.
- "Paramount, a Skydance Corporation" vs "Paramount Skydance Corporation": The combined company formed by the merger of Paramount Global and Skydance Media on August 7, 2025 is branded as "Paramount, a Skydance Corporation" in press materials; SEC filings reference the registrant as "Paramount Skydance Corporation". Both refer to the same parent entity for purposes of this question.

What does NOT count:
- Non-binding documents such as letters of intent, term sheets, MOUs, exclusivity agreements, or announcements of talks/interest without a signed definitive agreement.
- Agreements limited to asset purchases or licensing that do not result in one company becoming the legal parent controlling the other (i.e., no change of corporate control of the parent entity).
- Agreements with third parties where WBD and Paramount are not counterparties to a merger or acquisition between themselves.

Sources of truth to be checked at resolution:
- Warner Bros. Discovery investor relations Financial News page (for press releases): https://ir.wbd.com/news-and-events/financial-news/.
- Warner Bros. Discovery Newsroom: https://www.wbd.com/newsroom/ (for press releases; no claim cited here).
- Paramount investor relations press releases: https://ir.paramount.com/press-releases (e.g., merger completion press release confirming this is the official outlet).
- SEC EDGAR for Form 8-K filings (Item 1.01): https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/#/category/form-8-k. For illustration, Paramount’s Aug 7, 2025 8-K documents the prior merger closing mechanics under the registrant name "Paramount Skydance Corporation".

Resolution timing:
- YES resolves at the timestamp of the first qualifying disclosure within the window.
- NO resolves at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC if no qualifying disclosure occurred within the window.

question: By December 31, 2025 (UTC), will the FOMC’s federal funds rate target range midpoint be at least 50 basis points lower than on September 22, 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Context: Interest rates materially affect insurers’ portfolio yields and investment income. The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets a target range for the federal funds rate, influencing broader interest rates. A basis point (bp) is one hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%).
Status quo (as of 2025-09-22): The FOMC lowered the federal funds target range to 4.00%–4.25%, effective 2025-09-18. FRED’s upper-limit series (DFEDTARU) shows 4.25% on 2025-09-18 onward, down from 4.50% on 2025-09-17. Therefore, the baseline midpoint on 2025-09-22 is (4.25% + 4.00%) / 2 = 4.125%.
Relevance: Additional cuts (e.g., cumulative ≥50 bps vs. baseline) would further lower fixed-income yields’ discount rates yet may reprice portfolios and new money yields, affecting insurers’ investment income and profitability. Forecasters can track DFEDTARU and DFEDTARL on FRED for ongoing policy changes.
resolution_criteria:
Definitions:
- Federal funds rate target range: The range for the overnight federal funds rate set by the FOMC. We use the lower and upper limits as reported by FRED series DFEDTARL (lower limit) and DFEDTARU (upper limit). The midpoint is defined as (upper limit + lower limit) / 2.
- Basis point (bp): 0.01 percentage point.
Timeframe and baseline:
- Start date/time: 2025-09-22 00:00:00 UTC.
- Baseline midpoint: Computed from DFEDTARU and DFEDTARL values for 2025-09-22 (which reflect the effective 4.00%–4.25% range established 2025-09-18), yielding 4.125%.
Primary resolution:
- On 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve using the FRED daily values labeled 2025-12-31 for DFEDTARU and DFEDTARL. Compute the midpoint.
- YES if the midpoint on 2025-12-31 is at least 0.50 percentage points (≥50 bps) lower than the baseline midpoint (≤3.625%). NO otherwise.
Data sources:
- Primary: FRED DFEDTARU (upper limit) and DFEDTARL (lower limit) daily series.
- Backup (if FRED is unavailable on resolution): Official Federal Reserve releases indicating the target range in effect on 2025-12-31; for method and precedent, see the Implementation Note language confirming target ranges and effective dates.
Edge cases:
- If DFEDTARU/DFEDTARL show no entry for 2025-12-31, use the latest available daily values on or before 2025-12-31.
- “At least 50 bps” includes exactly 50 bps (i.e., a 0.500 percentage point reduction).

question: DMA enforcement: Will the European Commission publish at least one additional non-compliance decision against a gatekeeper between Oct 15 and Dec 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- The EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) is Regulation (EU) 2022/1925; official text and overview are on EUR-Lex (see: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/1925/oj/eng). Gatekeepers designated under the DMA currently include Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft, and Booking (European Commission’s official gatekeepers page).
- On 25 March 2024, the European Commission opened five non-compliance investigations under the DMA concerning Alphabet (steering in Google Play, self-preferencing in Search), Apple (steering in the App Store, web browser choice screen design), and Meta (“pay or consent” model). The Commission stated it intended to conclude these proceedings within 12 months.
- On 23 April 2025, the Commission adopted non-compliance decisions finding Apple and Meta in breach of the DMA. Apple was found to have breached its anti-steering obligation; Meta’s “consent or pay” model was found non-compliant. The Commission imposed fines of €500 million (Apple) and €200 million (Meta).
- The Commission regularly publishes DMA enforcement news via its “Press Corner” and the dedicated DMA “Latest news” page (example entries include the 23 April 2025 non-compliance decisions).

Why this question:
- Additional non-compliance decisions in late 2025 are plausible but not guaranteed, given ongoing proceedings and the 12-month conclusion intention originally stated for the March 2024 cases. The timeframe from 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-31 captures a period when further decisions could realistically appear, producing meaningful uncertainty for forecasters.
resolution_criteria:
Yes/No resolution with strict definitions and sources.

Question:
Resolve “Yes” if, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the European Commission publishes at least one additional formal non-compliance decision under the DMA against any gatekeeper; resolve “No” otherwise.

Definitions (with links and examples):
- Digital Markets Act (DMA): EU Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 on contestable and fair digital markets. See EUR-Lex: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/1925/oj/eng (link provided for reference).
- Gatekeeper: A company designated by the European Commission under the DMA; the Commission’s consolidated list currently includes Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft, and Booking. See the official EU page “DMA designated Gatekeepers”. For the purpose of resolution, “gatekeeper” refers to any company that is designated at the time of the decision’s publication.
- Non-compliance decision (for this question): An official decision by the European Commission that explicitly finds a gatekeeper to be in breach of the DMA (also termed “non-compliance decision” or described by the Commission as “finds [Company] in breach of the DMA”). For example, the Commission’s 23 April 2025 actions against Apple and Meta are described as non-compliance decisions and state those gatekeepers “breached”/“are not compliant with” DMA obligations.
- Publish/published: The decision is made public on an official European Commission web property, either: (a) the Commission’s Press Corner press release/news page for the decision; or (b) the official Digital Markets Act website’s “Latest news” page (digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/latest-news_en). The Commission uses these venues to announce DMA non-compliance decisions (e.g., Apple/Meta on 23 April 2025). The publication time is the timestamp shown on the relevant Commission page.
- Additional: Excludes non-compliance decisions published prior to the start of the resolution window. Specifically, it excludes the two non-compliance decisions concerning Apple and Meta published on 23 April 2025. Any qualifying decision published within the resolution window counts, even if concerning the same companies again.

Inclusions:
- Any Commission decision that the Commission itself describes as a non-compliance decision under the DMA, or that the Commission’s official announcement states “found [gatekeeper] in breach of the Digital Markets Act,” where the announcement is published on the Commission’s Press Corner or the DMA Latest news page.

Exclusions:
- Openings of investigations, statements of objections, preliminary findings, specification proceedings, commitments decisions, or workshop/consultation notices do not count unless the Commission explicitly states the adoption of a “non-compliance decision” finding a breach of the DMA.
- Decisions or actions published after 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, even if adopted earlier, do not count. Publication date/time controls.
- Publications outside official Commission web properties do not count for resolution.

Resolution process:
1) On or after 2026-01-01 00:00:01 UTC, check:
   - European Commission Press Corner for any press releases or news pages dated within the resolution window and explicitly announcing a non-compliance decision under the DMA against a gatekeeper.
   - The official DMA “Latest news” page (digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/latest-news_en) for entries in the window with the same explicit content.
2) If at least one qualifying announcement is found, resolve “Yes”; otherwise resolve “No”.
3) If both sources exist for the same decision, use the earliest Commission publication timestamp within the window.

Notes:
- The March 25, 2024 investigations and 12-month intention , and the April 23, 2025 Apple/Meta decisions and fines , are provided as context only and do not themselves determine resolution.
- Appeals, subsequent modifications, or later annulments do not affect resolution, which is based solely on the Commission’s publication within the specified window.

question: IAEA–Iran: Will the IAEA publish a verified, quantified figure for Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched to up to 60% U‑235 in Q4 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01:
- Latest verified baseline before Q4 2025: In a Board of Governors report (GOV/2025/50) circulated on 2025-09-03, the IAEA stated that as of 2025-06-13 Iran’s stockpile included 440.9 kg of uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235, and noted that 432.9 kg of this was verified in the form of UF6 enriched up to 60% U‑235. The report details that since 2025-06-13 the Agency lost access to safeguarded facilities (except BNPP), withdrew inspectors for safety by end-June, and Iran enacted a law on 2025-07-02 suspending cooperation; consequently, the Agency lost continuity of knowledge and could not quantify the stockpile with previous confidence until resumption of in‑field verification.
- Director General statements: On 2025-09-08, the IAEA Director General reiterated loss of access since 2025-06-13, inspector withdrawal by end‑June, Iran’s 2025-07-02 law suspending cooperation, and the need to conclude modalities to resume full inspections; he noted verification of high‑enriched uranium was overdue without access.
- Prospects of resuming inspections: Credible reporting indicates that on 2025-09-09, the IAEA and Iran announced agreement “on practical modalities to resume inspection activities,” with both sides describing it as a step toward full resumption following June attacks; no firm operational timeline was disclosed at that press event.
- Where such stockpile figures appear: The IAEA typically publishes quantified enriched‑uranium stockpile figures in Director General reports to the Board of Governors (GOV/ documents) and occasionally references them in DG statements posted on iaea.org. The IAEA maintains an official page aggregating Iran‑related Board reports with links and dates (e.g., GOV/2025/25, GOV/2025/24, GOV/2025/10), updated through 2025.

Key definitions and terms:
- Uranium‑235 (U‑235): A fissile isotope of uranium; enrichment percentage denotes the fraction of U‑235 in uranium. Weapons‑grade uranium is commonly defined as ≥85% U‑235; HEU is ≥20% U‑235.
- Uranium hexafluoride (UF6): Volatile compound used in uranium enrichment processes. IAEA reporting of “kgU in UF6” refers to the mass of uranium contained in the UF6, not the total compound mass; IAEA reports explicitly specify figures as “kg of uranium in the form of UF6”.
- “Uranium enriched to up to 60% U‑235”: For this question, this refers to the IAEA’s stockpile category in GOV reports that explicitly labels uranium enriched “up to 60% U‑235” (near‑bomb‑grade) and provides mass in kilograms of uranium (kgU) in UF6 form.
- “Publish”: Release on official IAEA channels (iaea.org), including Director General reports to the Board of Governors (GOV/ series) or formal DG statements/news releases.
- “Verified, quantified figure”: A single number (not a range) in kilograms of uranium (kgU) for the “up to 60% U‑235” stockpile that the IAEA explicitly characterizes as based on its verification activities (e.g., uses terms like “verified,” “based on verification activities,” or indicates that in‑field verification enabling that figure has occurred).

Why this has uncertainty: Access and cooperation were suspended in mid‑2025, creating verification gaps; while a September 2025 announcement suggested modalities to resume inspections, implementation details remain unclear, making it uncertain whether the IAEA will regain sufficient access and publish a newly verified figure within Q4 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Event window and time zone:
- Eligible publications must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Resolution:
- This resolves YES if, within the event window, the IAEA publishes on iaea.org either:
  1) a Director General report to the Board of Governors (GOV/ document), or
  2) a formal Director General statement or IAEA news release,
  that contains a newly verified, quantified figure for Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched to up to 60% U‑235, expressed in kilograms of uranium (kgU), and the publication explicitly attributes the figure to the Agency’s verification activities. The figure must pertain to a reference date on or after 2025-10-15 or be explicitly described as newly verified during the event window.

- This resolves NO if no such publication appears within the event window, or if any number published during the window lacks explicit attribution to IAEA verification (e.g., is presented solely as an unverified estimate based on declarations without in‑field verification, or repeats the pre‑Q4 figure without new verification).

Scope clarifications:
- Acceptable phrasing indicating verification includes: “verified,” “based on verification activities,” “following resumption of in‑field verification,” or equivalent language establishing that the Agency’s verification activities underpin the figure.
- The figure must correspond specifically to the IAEA’s “enriched up to 60% U‑235” category reported in kgU in UF6 form; figures for different enrichment bands or without clear categorization do not count. If presented for total HEU without the 60% band delineated, it does not count.
- Ranges or qualitative descriptions (e.g., “around X kg” without a single quantitative value) do not count. Multiple figures for different dates are acceptable as long as at least one meets the criteria above.

Primary resolution sources:
- IAEA “IAEA and Iran – IAEA Board Reports” aggregation page (for GOV/ documents and dates): https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/focus/iran/iaea-and-iran-iaea-board-reports.
- Relevant GOV/ reports (e.g., GOV/2025/50 as an example of format and categorization) and DG statements on iaea.org.

Definitions references:
- Uranium‑235 and enrichment thresholds: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uranium-235.
- Uranium hexafluoride (UF6): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uranium_hexafluoride.

Adjudication notes:
- If needed to confirm publication timing or content, use the IAEA page above to access the specific GOV/ document or DG statement; resolution should be achievable within ~10 minutes by checking Q4 2025 entries.
- If IAEA and Iran implement modalities announced on 2025-09-09 and inspections resume, verification language may appear in Q4 documents; however, adjudication relies only on IAEA official publications, not third‑party reporting.

question: Will New York City’s Central Business District Tolling Program (congestion pricing) be active and collecting tolls at 11:59 pm ET on December 31, 2025?
background:
Overview and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Definition and geography. The Central Business District Tolling Program (CBDTP) charges a toll for vehicles entering Manhattan’s Congestion Relief Zone (CRZ). The CRZ is defined by the MTA as the area of Manhattan south of and including 60th Street, excluding the FDR Drive, West Side Highway/Route 9A, and the Hugh L. Carey Tunnel connections to West Street. Entering the CRZ means moving from outside the CRZ onto local streets and avenues within the CRZ. Travel exclusively along excluded roadways (e.g., FDR Drive or West Street/West Side Highway) without exiting to local streets does not incur a toll; the MTA provides concrete examples of tolled and untolled movements, including specific connections among FDR Drive, the Brooklyn and Manhattan bridges, the Hugh L. Carey Tunnel, Queens Midtown Tunnel, Queensboro Bridge, Lincoln Tunnel, and Holland Tunnel.
- Launch and ongoing operation. The MTA’s press release states the program launched on Sunday, January 5, 2025 at 12:00:01 a.m. ET, charging a toll for motorists to enter Manhattan below 60th Street (the CBD/CRZ). The MTA’s CBDTP project page describes the program as active, stating: “Since January 5, 2025, vehicles entering the Congestion Relief Zone in Manhattan … are being charged a toll”.
- Hours/rates context (for what “collecting tolls” entails). The official toll schedule shows tolling is continuous, with differentiated rates by time: peak periods are 5 a.m.–9 p.m. on weekdays and 9 a.m.–9 p.m. on weekends; overnight rates (off-peak) are 75% lower, confirming toll collection continues overnight at reduced rates.
- Recent developments and risk context. On February 19, 2025, the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Federal Highway Administration announced termination of federal approval for New York City’s cordon pricing plan under the Value Pricing Pilot Program, citing program scope and revenue-setting concerns. Despite this, MTA communications indicated ongoing operation later in 2025; a September 2025 MTA press release stated, “Congestion pricing is working, it is legal, and the cameras are staying on,” and presented 2025 operational metrics (e.g., reductions in zone entries and travel time improvements). These dynamics create policy/legal risk relevant to the forecast while establishing that, as of early fall 2025, tolling remained in effect.

Key references for forecasters:
- MTA CBDTP project page: https://www.mta.info/project/CBDTP 
- MTA CRZ FAQs and tolling information (definitions, examples): https://congestionreliefzone.mta.info/faqs; https://congestionreliefzone.mta.info/tolling 
- MTA press releases: Launch (Jan 5, 2025) and subsequent updates: https://www.mta.info/press-release/new-york-joins-world-cities-launch-of-first-nation-program-deliver-cleaner-air-less; September 2025 status update: https://www.mta.info/press-release/icymi-less-traffic-safer-streets-summer-comes-end-governor-hochul-highlights 
- USDOT/FHWA announcement (Feb 19, 2025) terminating federal approval: https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/us-department-transportation-terminates-tolling-approval-new-york-citys-cordon
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on the program’s status at precisely 2025-12-31 11:59:59 pm Eastern Time (ET).

Definitions (for this market):
- Central Business District Tolling Program (CBDTP): The Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) program that charges tolls to vehicles entering the CRZ in Manhattan.
- Congestion Relief Zone (CRZ): The area of Manhattan south of and including 60th Street, excluding the FDR Drive, West Side Highway/Route 9A, and the Hugh L. Carey Tunnel connections to West Street. Travel solely on excluded roadways without exiting to local streets does not incur a toll; the MTA’s FAQs provide concrete examples of tolled/untolled routes and how detection points determine whether a vehicle remained on excluded roadways.
- Active and collecting tolls: For this resolution, “active” means that the MTA is charging tolls for vehicles entering the CRZ at the time of resolution (i.e., toll collection is in effect, whether at peak or overnight rates). The CBDTP toll schedule indicates tolling is continuous with peak and overnight time windows; thus, tolling is considered “active” so long as entries to the CRZ are tolled according to the schedule in effect.
- Suspension/termination: “Suspended” means the MTA has officially announced a halt to toll collection for entries into the CRZ. “Terminated” means the MTA (or its TBTA subsidiary) has officially ended the program.

Resolution sources and hierarchy:
- Resolve YES if, as of the resolution timestamp, the MTA indicates that the CBDTP is in effect—i.e., that vehicles entering the CRZ are being charged a toll—on any of the following official sources: the CBDTP project page, the MTA’s Congestion Relief Zone/tolling site, an MTA press release, or an MTA service/customer notice.
- Resolve NO if the MTA has officially suspended or terminated toll collection for CRZ entries on or before the resolution timestamp (evidenced by an MTA press release, service/customer notice, or an explicit announcement on the CBDTP project page or CRZ site).
- In the event of conflicting information across MTA sources, prioritize a dated MTA press release or service/customer notice over undated website copy. If official MTA web properties are unavailable at resolution, use credible media reports (e.g., AP, Reuters, NYT) that directly cite an official MTA announcement.

Date range and timezone:
- This question concerns the program’s status at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 ET. All times are Eastern Time. Historical information prior to that timestamp is provided only for context and does not by itself determine resolution.

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the European Commission announce a Digital Markets Act (DMA) fine against any designated gatekeeper?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30:
- What the DMA is and how fines work: The EU’s Digital Markets Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/1925) empowers the European Commission to fine designated “gatekeepers” for non-compliance. The Commission can impose fines up to 10% of a company’s total worldwide annual turnover, rising to 20% for repeated infringements, and can impose periodic penalty payments up to 5% of average daily worldwide turnover.
- First DMA non-compliance fines (April 2025): On 23 April 2025, the European Commission announced non-compliance decisions under the DMA against Apple and Meta, imposing fines of €500 million and €200 million, respectively. These announcements were made via an official press release and the Commission’s Digital Strategy website. An Official Journal summary notes the legal basis for Apple’s fine as Article 30(1) DMA, explicitly referencing articles 29(1)(a), 30(1)(a), and 31(1)(h) of Regulation (EU) 2022/1925.
- Gatekeepers (who can be fined under the DMA): As of the latest official gatekeepers page, the Commission lists Alphabet, Amazon, Apple (including for iPadOS), ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft, and Booking (for Booking.com) as designated gatekeepers.
- Enforcement pipeline (illustrative of ongoing scrutiny): On 25 March 2024, the Commission opened DMA non-compliance investigations into Alphabet, Apple, and Meta, noting that infringements can lead to fines up to 10% of worldwide turnover (20% for repeat cases).

Why this should be uncertain (and interesting): The Commission has demonstrated willingness to fine under the DMA but the timing and targets of any additional fines remain contingent on evolving investigations and compliance measures. The Q4 2025 window follows the first wave of decisions and leaves open the possibility of further enforcement actions, without certainty they will occur precisely in that period.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive), will the European Commission publicly announce that it has imposed a monetary fine under the Digital Markets Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/1925) on any designated gatekeeper?

Definitions
- Digital Markets Act (DMA): Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 governing “gatekeepers” and their “core platform services,” including enforcement via fines and periodic penalty payments.
- Gatekeeper: An undertaking designated by the European Commission as a gatekeeper under the DMA. For practical purposes, any entity listed on the Commission’s official “DMA Gatekeepers” page at the time of the announcement qualifies (e.g., Alphabet, Amazon, Apple (incl. iPadOS), ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft, Booking).
- DMA fine (what counts): A monetary penalty that the Commission states it has imposed for non-compliance with the DMA (Regulation (EU) 2022/1925). This includes fines adopted pursuant to Article 30 of the DMA; EU documentation for earlier decisions explicitly references Article 30(1) for such fines. Fines under other legal bases (e.g., TFEU Articles 101/102 or the Digital Services Act) do NOT count.
- Periodic penalty payments: Recurring penalties intended to compel compliance; these are distinct from fines and do NOT count toward resolving this question.
- Publicly announce / announcement: Publication by the European Commission of an official press release or news item stating that the Commission “has fined” (or equivalent wording indicating an imposed fine) a gatekeeper for breaching the DMA. Acceptable outlets are: (a) the Commission’s Press Corner (official press releases), or (b) the Commission’s Digital Strategy/DMA news pages. Examples of past acceptable announcement venues include the April 23, 2025 press release and Digital Strategy news page for the Apple and Meta fines. Media reports, leaks, interviews, social media posts, or company statements do not count as announcements for the purposes of this market.

Time window and time zone
- Eligible announcements must be published between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive.
- If the Commission source displays only a publication date (no time), the date shown is considered authoritative; if a time is displayed, compare it using UTC.

Inclusions
- Any single qualifying announcement during the window resolves YES, regardless of the fine amount or which gatekeeper is fined.
- Multiple fines announced in the window still resolve the question as a single YES.

Exclusions and edge cases
- Announcements of investigations, statements of objections, commitments, warning letters, or intents to fine do not count.
- Imposition of periodic penalty payments (Article 31) alone does not count.
- Fines not explicitly tied to the DMA (e.g., antitrust or DSA fines) do not count.

Source(s) of truth for resolution
- Primary: European Commission Press Corner press releases and/or Commission Digital Strategy/DMA news pages for the relevant announcement(s).
- Where needed for legal basis confirmation, an Official Journal summary citing Article 30(1) DMA may be used, though the press release/news item within the window is sufficient for timing of the announcement.

question: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will the IAEA publicly report Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched up to 60% U-235 at or below 396.8 kg (U mass)?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) reported that as of 13 June 2025, Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235 totaled 440.9 kg of uranium (U mass) in the form of UF6, an increase of 32.3 kg from the previous report. The same IAEA Director General report (GOV/2025/50, published 3 September 2025) describes major verification challenges since 13 June 2025, including the Agency’s loss of continuity of knowledge regarding inventories of nuclear material, withdrawal of inspectors for safety reasons, and Iran’s subsequent suspension of cooperation, leaving the IAEA unable to conduct in-field verification and unable to quantify changes to the stockpile with prior confidence. Contemporary news coverage also cited the 440.9 kg figure and contextualized it as a slight increase before the mid-June attacks on nuclear facilities, noting the IAEA as source. Definitions and terms: 
- Uranium enrichment: The process of increasing the concentration of uranium‑235 (U‑235) in uranium through isotope separation; enrichment percentage (e.g., 60%) refers to the fraction of U‑235 by mass in the uranium.
- Uranium‑235 (U‑235): A fissile isotope of uranium with natural abundance ~0.72% in unprocessed uranium; enrichment increases its proportion.
- Uranium hexafluoride (UF6): A volatile compound used in gaseous diffusion and gas centrifuge enrichment; IAEA reporting commonly distinguishes “kg of uranium (U mass)” contained in UF6 from total UF6 mass.
- “U mass”: For this question, “U mass” means kilograms of uranium content, not kilograms of UF6. The baseline 440.9 kg is explicitly reported by the IAEA as kg of uranium (in the form of UF6) enriched up to 60% U‑235.
- “Enriched up to 60% U‑235”: For this question, this category follows IAEA usage and refers to uranium material whose U‑235 assay is within the IAEA’s “up to 60%” inventory category, i.e., material at or near 60% U‑235 assay as reported by the IAEA.
Source documents and cadence: The principal source is IAEA Director General reports to the Board of Governors (e.g., GOV/2025/50, derestricted and posted on iaea.org) and any IAEA Director General public statements on iaea.org that include quantitative stockpile figures. The September 3, 2025 GOV/2025/50 report is the latest public, authoritative stockpile figure as of this writing. Reuters and AP articles corroborate the same figure and provide context but are secondary sources.
resolution_criteria:
Baseline and threshold: Baseline is 440.9 kg of uranium (U mass) enriched up to 60% U‑235, as of 13 June 2025, per IAEA GOV/2025/50. The threshold for resolution is 396.8 kg (i.e., a decrease of at least 10% relative to the baseline).
Event window and time zone: Eligible publications are those publicly posted between 2025‑10‑15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025‑12‑31 23:59:59 UTC (UTC) on iaea.org.
What counts as “IAEA publicly report”: Any of the following, provided they are publicly accessible on iaea.org:
- A derestricted IAEA Director General report to the Board of Governors that includes a numerical figure for Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235, expressed as kilograms of uranium (U mass), as of a stated date.
- An official IAEA “Statement” or “News Center” item by the Director General that includes a numerical figure for Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235, expressed as kilograms of uranium (U mass), as of a stated date.
Primary metric and units: The primary metric for resolution is the IAEA‑reported kilograms of uranium (U mass) in the “enriched up to 60% U‑235” category. If both U mass and UF6 mass are provided, U mass governs. Figures reported only in UF6 mass will not be converted and will not count toward resolution unless the document itself states the corresponding U mass for the 60% category.
Yes/No rules:
- Resolve Yes if any eligible IAEA public document (as defined above) published within the event window explicitly reports the 60% stockpile at or below 396.8 kg (U mass) as of its stated measurement date.
- Resolve No if, by the end of the event window, no eligible IAEA public document reports a numerical U mass figure at or below 396.8 kg for the 60% category, including the case where no quantitative update is published.
Document precedence and conflicts: If multiple eligible IAEA documents are published within the window, use the most recent publication time (UTC). If figures conflict, the most recently published eligible IAEA document supersedes earlier ones for resolution.
Exclusions: Media reports not posted on iaea.org (e.g., wire services citing confidential reports) do not count as “publicly reported” for resolution, though they informed the background.
Verification steps: A resolver will visit iaea.org’s Document Library and News Center to locate any derestricted Director General reports or statements published in the event window and verify whether a numerical U mass figure for uranium enriched up to 60% U‑235 is at or below 396.8 kg.

question: Will a binding, definitive agreement transferring control of TikTok’s U.S. operations be publicly announced between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of September 30, 2025:
- The Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (Public Law 118-50; often referred to as H.R. 7521) prohibits distribution, maintenance, or updates of certain foreign adversary–controlled apps in the U.S., with relief if a “qualified divestiture” is executed. The Act defines both “foreign adversary controlled application” and “qualified divestiture,” including requirements that U.S. operations no longer be controlled by a foreign adversary and that operational relationships (e.g., algorithm cooperation, data sharing) with formerly affiliated foreign adversary–controlled entities be precluded.
- On September 16, 2025, the White House issued “Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay,” extending the enforcement delay under prior executive actions to December 16, 2025, and instructing the Attorney General to defend exclusive federal authority to enforce the Act.
- On September 25, 2025, the White House published “Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security,” stating the President has determined a proposed TikTok U.S. divestiture plan would constitute a qualified divestiture under the Act and directing the Attorney General not to enforce the Act for 120 days from that date to permit completion of the divestiture.
- DOJ/AG guidance applied the Act’s prohibitions to TikTok as effective January 19, 2025, and described temporary non-enforcement periods to allow assessment and potential resolution strategies.

Why this matters for forecasting: The combination of statutory prohibitions, executive delays, and an identified proposed divestiture framework creates real uncertainty about whether a binding, definitive agreement will be publicly announced before year-end 2025. A definitive agreement is often evidenced by SEC Form 8-K Item 1.01 filings (for public registrants) or formal press releases; Item 1.01 defines “material definitive agreement” as one that provides for obligations material to and enforceable against the registrant (or rights enforceable by the registrant), whether or not subject to conditions.

Key definitions and references forecasters may consult:
- TikTok: A short-form video platform operated by TikTok (ByteDance) offering services globally, including in the U.S. (general reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok).
- ByteDance: Parent company of TikTok (general reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ByteDance).
- “Material definitive agreement”: As defined by SEC Form 8-K Item 1.01(b), an agreement with obligations or rights that are material and enforceable (commonly used to delineate binding definitive deals and distinguish them from non-binding term sheets, LOIs, or MOUs).
- “Qualified divestiture”: As defined in Section 2(g)(6) of the Act; the President’s determination is through an interagency process and must result in U.S. operations not being controlled by a foreign adversary and preclude operational relationships with such entities.

Status quo suggests multiple pathways to a publicly verifiable announcement before year-end (company press releases, SEC filings, or formal U.S. Government statements). However, completion (closing) is different from announcement/entry into a definitive agreement; this question concerns the latter.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, there is a public announcement evidencing that ByteDance/TikTok and a buyer (or consortium) have entered into a binding, definitive agreement that transfers control of TikTok’s U.S. operations, or an equivalent corporate arrangement that clearly meets the Act’s “qualified divestiture” criteria.

To count, the announcement must meet all of the following:
1) Announcement type: At least one of the following publicly accessible sources must clearly evidence entry into a binding, definitive agreement:
   - An SEC Form 8-K filing by a U.S.-listed party to the agreement disclosing “Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement” under Item 1.01 ;
   - An official press release posted on the corporate website or official newsroom of ByteDance Ltd., TikTok, or a buyer/consortium member party to the agreement;
   - A formal public statement or Presidential action posted on whitehouse.gov or an official U.S. Government website indicating the agreement has been executed and constitutes a qualified divestiture under the Act.

2) Definitive agreement requirement: The agreement must be legally binding and definitive (not a letter of intent, memorandum of understanding, term sheet, or other non-binding framework). For public registrants, the SEC’s Item 1.01 definition of “material definitive agreement” is the standard: an agreement providing obligations material to and enforceable against the registrant or rights enforceable by the registrant. For private companies, the press release or official statement must clearly indicate a signed, binding purchase, merger, asset transfer, joint venture formation, or similar definitive agreement, not a preliminary or non-binding arrangement.

3) Scope: The agreement must explicitly cover TikTok’s U.S. operations such that control of U.S. operations is transferred to an entity not controlled by ByteDance or TikTok, or must be formally recognized by the U.S. Government as a “qualified divestiture” under Section 2(g)(6) of the Act. Evidence that the arrangement satisfies a qualified divestiture (via a formal White House or DOJ/AG statement) is sufficient to meet the scope requirement. Closing of the transaction is not required; entry into the agreement is sufficient.

4) Timing: The public announcement must occur within the inclusive window from 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 to 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.

Exclusions:
- Non-binding documents (LOIs, MOUs, term sheets) do not count.
- Internal or leaked documents without official public release do not count.
- Agreements signed before October 15, 2025 or announced after December 31, 2025 do not count.

Resolution procedure:
- A human resolver will verify the announcement via the specified sources. If multiple announcements exist, the earliest qualifying public announcement within the window will be used for resolution.
- If no qualifying public announcement is found, resolve No.

Primary authoritative references for verification include: the relevant White House executive actions (Sept 16 extension to Dec 16, 2025; Sept 25 order identifying a proposed qualified divestiture and directing 120 days of non-enforcement) , the Act’s definitions and divestiture criteria , and SEC Form 8-K Item 1.01 for the definition of “material definitive agreement”. DOJ/AG published application of the Act to TikTok provides background on effective dates and non-enforcement periods.

question: Will the Bank of England’s MPC reduce Bank Rate at its December 2025 meeting?
background:
Definitions and scope:
- Bank Rate: the UK’s core policy interest rate, i.e., the rate the Bank of England pays on reserves held by banks/building societies and the rate it charges on certain lending to them.
- MPC refers to the Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee (see Bank of England website for MPC information). This question concerns the MPC’s December 2025 policy decision, as formally announced in the Bank of England’s “Monetary Policy Summary and minutes” for December 2025.
- Time window: This question resolves based on outcomes announced between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. The December 2025 MPC announcement is scheduled for 18 December 2025; the Bank of England’s December Monetary Policy Summary page indicates it will be published at 12:00 (UK local time).

Status quo as of late September 2025 (context for forecasters):
- At the MPC meeting ending 17 September 2025, Bank Rate was maintained at 4.0%. The vote was 7–2 to hold, with two members preferring a 25 bp cut to 3.75%. The MPC reiterated that monetary policy is “not on a pre-set path” and that it would remain responsive to data. The Committee also expected CPI inflation to rise slightly around September before falling back towards target thereafter.
- UK CPI inflation (ONS headline CPI, 12-month rate) was 3.8% in August 2025, unchanged from July 2025, according to the latest ONS bulletin at the time.

Primary resolution source:
- Bank of England “Monetary Policy Summary and minutes – December 2025” page (official source-of-truth; to be published by the Bank at the stated time).

Why this is forecastable: There is plausible uncertainty between a cut vs. hold/increase given recent inflation dynamics, prior vote splits, and MPC guidance emphasizing data dependence rather than a preset path.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will the Bank of England’s MPC reduce Bank Rate at its December 2025 meeting?

Resolution event and timing:
- This question resolves upon publication of the Bank of England’s “Monetary Policy Summary and minutes – December 2025,” expected on 18 December 2025 at 12:00 UK local time, and in any case no later than 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. All times in this question are UTC unless otherwise specified.

Operational definitions for adjudication:
- “Bank Rate” means the UK’s official policy rate as defined by the Bank of England.
- “Reduce” / “cut” means the MPC sets Bank Rate to a level strictly lower than the level in effect immediately prior to the December 2025 decision. Evidence of a cut will typically be clear in the official communication (e.g., headline language such as “Bank Rate reduced to X%”) and/or by comparing the newly announced Bank Rate to the previously effective rate.

How to resolve:
- Use the Bank of England’s December 2025 Monetary Policy Summary and minutes page as the sole source-of-truth to determine the decision.
- Resolve “Yes” if the December 2025 Monetary Policy Summary/minutes states that Bank Rate was reduced relative to its level immediately prior to the meeting (i.e., the decision is a cut). Resolve “No” if Bank Rate was maintained or increased.

Edge cases and clarifications:
- If the Bank of England does not publish the December 2025 Monetary Policy Summary/minutes by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve “No.”
- If the December 2025 meeting is rescheduled but the Monetary Policy Summary/minutes for that meeting are still published by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve based on that publication.
- If multiple versions or updates are posted on the publication date, resolve based on the latest official version available on the Bank of England website as of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
- Media reports, third-party data providers, and press conferences do not override the official Monetary Policy Summary/minutes page for resolution.

Start date for eligible outcomes: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC. End date: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

question: Will ACMA impose a monetary enforcement action on Optus related to the 18 September 2025 Triple Zero outage by December 31, 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Incident: On 18 September 2025, Optus experienced an outage that prevented some customers from connecting to Australia’s Triple Zero (000) emergency number. Government and media reporting indicate about 600 failed Triple Zero calls and multiple deaths linked to the outage. The incident has been described as stemming from a network firewall upgrade in which established processes were not followed. Less than two weeks later, a fresh outage affecting emergency call services occurred, intensifying scrutiny.
- Regulator action: The Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) announced on 22 September 2025 that it had commenced an investigation into Optus’s compliance with emergency call service regulations and related obligations, and stated it will make its findings public once concluded.
- Enforcement toolkit and precedent: ACMA’s compliance and enforcement policy includes monetary instruments such as infringement notices (specified penalties payable if accepted) and civil penalties (pecuniary penalty orders via the Federal Court). As precedent, ACMA reported Optus paid three infringement notices totalling $12,000,420 for breaches related to the November 2023 Triple Zero outage.

Key definitions and links for forecasters:
- ACMA: Australia’s communications regulator; investigation page and media releases are published at acma.gov.au.
- Optus: For this question, “Optus” means Singtel Optus Pty Limited or any Australian subsidiary (e.g., Optus Mobile Pty Ltd, Optus Networks Pty Ltd) that ACMA treats as part of the Optus group for enforcement in relation to the specified incident.
- Triple Zero (000): Australia’s primary emergency number; general background: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_zero (link provided for definition/reference only).

Why this is forecastable: ACMA has an open investigation with stated intent to publish findings , monetary penalties are within its enforcement toolkit , and Optus has previously received (and paid) significant ACMA penalties for emergency call service breaches. Whether ACMA will impose a monetary enforcement action tied specifically to the 18 September 2025 outage by year-end is plausible yet uncertain, and will be publicly verifiable.

Notes on data sources for resolution: ACMA typically announces enforcement outcomes via articles/media releases on acma.gov.au and periodic compliance reports. Major wire services and national outlets (e.g., Reuters, ABC) also cover significant ACMA enforcement actions and can serve as secondary confirmation.
resolution_criteria:
Question: Will ACMA impose a monetary enforcement action on Optus related to the 18 September 2025 Triple Zero outage between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive)?

Operational definitions:
- Monetary enforcement action (for this question) means either of the following, provided it explicitly relates to the 18 September 2025 Triple Zero outage:
  1) ACMA issues an infringement notice to Optus that specifies a monetary penalty amount (payment to the Commonwealth) for contraventions under relevant legislation or instruments (e.g., the Telecommunications Act), as described in ACMA’s compliance and enforcement policy ; or
  2) An Australian court makes a civil penalty (pecuniary penalty) order against Optus in proceedings brought by (or on the application of) ACMA for contraventions relating to the outage.

- Explicit relation to the 18 September 2025 Triple Zero outage means the ACMA publication (or the court order) directly references “Triple Zero”/“000” and the date or factual description that uniquely identifies the 18 September 2025 incident (e.g., “18 September 2025”, “September 2025 outage causing ~600 failed Triple Zero calls”).
- Optus means Singtel Optus Pty Limited or any Australian subsidiary within the Optus group that ACMA names in relation to this incident.

Start and end of eligibility window:
- Start: 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC
- End: 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC

Resolution rules:
- Resolve YES if, within the eligibility window, ACMA publishes on acma.gov.au that it has issued an infringement notice to Optus that explicitly ties the notice to the 18 September 2025 Triple Zero outage; or if an Australian court publishes an order within the window imposing a pecuniary penalty on Optus in ACMA-initiated proceedings explicitly tied to that outage. Payment of an infringement notice is not required for YES; issuance by ACMA suffices, provided the issuance is publicly announced on acma.gov.au within the window. If both occur, resolve YES.
- Resolve NO if, by the end of the window, neither of the above has occurred; or if ACMA only announces non-monetary actions (e.g., remedial directions, warnings, code directions, or acceptance of an enforceable undertaking without any specified monetary penalty), or actions/penalties that do not explicitly relate to the 18 September 2025 outage.

Primary resolution sources (in order of preference):
1) ACMA website publications (articles/media releases, enforcement pages) on acma.gov.au that announce issuance of infringement notices or other enforcement outcomes, or periodic reports summarizing such outcomes.
2) If applicable, an Australian court order imposing a pecuniary penalty (e.g., the Federal Court of Australia online registry/judgments). If a court order is used, it must explicitly reference the 18 September 2025 outage.
3) Secondary confirmation only if needed for clarity: major credible outlets (e.g., Reuters, ABC) reporting and linking to the ACMA notice or court order.

Tiebreakers and edge cases:
- If ACMA announces that it has commenced civil penalty proceedings but no court order imposing a penalty is made within the window, do NOT count this as monetary enforcement (resolve NO absent other eligible actions).
- If ACMA issues multiple enforcement instruments, at least one must be a monetary one (as defined above) explicitly tied to the 18 September 2025 Triple Zero outage for YES.
- If an ACMA publication or court document references the September 2025 outage but is ambiguous as to the date, use explicit mention of “18 September 2025” or the contemporaneous description (e.g., ~600 failed Triple Zero calls) to confirm eligibility.
- The date for timeliness is the publication date shown on the ACMA page or the date of the court order. If only a date (not time) is shown, treat it as occurring on that date; ensure it is on or before 2025-12-31 when interpreted against the UTC cutoff.

Supporting context for forecasters:
- ACMA has publicly stated it commenced an investigation into the 18 September 2025 outage and will publish findings.
- Media and official timelines report around 600 failed Triple Zero calls and multiple deaths linked to the 18 September 2025 outage.
- ACMA has previously imposed a large monetary penalty on Optus for Triple Zero-related breaches tied to the November 2023 outage (three infringement notices totalling $12,000,420).

question: By 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, will the United States lower the Section 232 additional duty rate applied to steel articles of EU origin below 50% ad valorem (including via an EU-specific tariff-rate quota)?
background:
Status quo as of October 1, 2025: On June 3, 2025, a presidential action increased the Section 232 tariffs on steel articles and derivative steel articles from 25% to 50% ad valorem, effective 12:01 a.m. ET on June 4, 2025, and applicable to imports from all countries except the United Kingdom, which remained at 25%. Subsequent Federal Register implementation notices adjusted HTSUS notes for derivative steel articles and confirmed effective dates and coverage for these duties. On August 21, 2025, the EU and U.S. published a joint statement setting out a broader trade framework: it committed the U.S. to apply only MFN tariffs to certain EU products as of September 1, 2025, and stated that for steel and aluminum the parties would consider cooperation, including potential tariff‑rate quota (TRQ) solutions; however, it did not announce a reduction of the 50% Section 232 rate on EU steel. Industry commentary the same day highlighted that a 50% U.S. import tariff on EU steel continues under the current regime and urged work toward a TRQ. The September 25, 2025 Federal Register notice implementing elements of the framework applied MFN‑only treatment to specified EU products and exempted aircraft and aircraft parts from certain tariffs, but did not reduce Section 232 steel tariffs for the EU.

Definitions and scope:
- Section 232 additional duty rate: The ad valorem duty imposed under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 on steel articles and derivative steel articles, as set by presidential proclamations and implemented in the HTSUS (currently 50% ad valorem for most countries) [1b957e; ff6dc7].
- Steel articles and derivative steel articles: The categories as defined in the relevant presidential actions and HTSUS Chapter 99 notes implementing Section 232 steel measures [1b957e; ff6dc7].
- EU origin: For this question, “EU origin” means goods for which the country of origin declared to U.S. Customs and Border Protection is a European Union Member State, using U.S. customs rules of origin.
- Tariff‑rate quota (TRQ): A trade policy instrument under which a specified quantity of imports is subject to a lower in‑quota tariff rate, with higher tariffs applied to quantities above the quota. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff-rate_quota.
- Most‑favored‑nation (MFN) tariff: The non‑preferential base tariff rate applied to WTO members under MFN treatment. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_favoured_nation.

Why this is a non‑trivial, high‑entropy forecast: The policy baseline is a 50% Section 232 rate on EU steel, but the August 21 framework explicitly contemplates TRQ cooperation for steel and aluminum, and the Administration has been actively modifying tariff instruments through proclamations and HTSUS notices throughout 2025 [1b957e; ff6dc7; e1f985; c05883]. That creates plausible paths to a year‑end adjustment (across‑the‑board or in‑quota via a TRQ), while industry signals suggest continued uncertainty.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and time zone: Eligible actions must take effect between 00:00 UTC on October 1, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025. The question resolves at 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025.

What resolves YES:
- An official U.S. action in effect by the resolution time that sets the applicable Section 232 additional duty rate on entries of steel articles of EU origin (and/or derivative steel articles of EU origin) to any rate strictly less than 50.00% ad valorem. Qualifying actions include:
  - A Presidential Proclamation adjusting imports of steel under Section 232 and published on whitehouse.gov, increasing or decreasing rates, that explicitly sets a lower rate for EU products; and/or
  - A Federal Register notice that amends the HTSUS (e.g., Chapter 99 notes) to implement an EU‑specific rate below 50% for steel articles or derivative steel articles; and/or
  - Establishment of an EU‑specific tariff‑rate quota (TRQ) for steel (and/or derivative steel) under Section 232 where the in‑quota Section 232 additional duty rate is below 50% ad valorem.

What does not count as YES:
- Importer‑specific or product‑specific exclusions that do not change the general EU‑wide rate structure, aircraft‑specific exemptions, or changes outside Section 232 (e.g., only MFN base rates without altering the Section 232 additional duty) [c05883; ff6dc7].

What resolves NO:
- If no qualifying official action is in effect by the resolution time, such that the applicable Section 232 additional duty rate remains 50% ad valorem for EU‑origin steel articles (and derivative steel articles) [1b957e; ff6dc7; 68ed4d; c05883].

Primary resolution sources to check at resolution time:
- Presidential actions page (whitehouse.gov) for proclamations adjusting steel tariffs (e.g., the June 3, 2025 action increasing to 50%).
- Federal Register notices implementing Section 232 tariff adjustments and HTSUS amendments (e.g., the June 16, 2025 implementation and the September 25, 2025 framework notice) [ff6dc7; c05883].
- If needed, credible wires (Reuters, AP, Bloomberg) that report on new proclamations or Federal Register notices and cite the official documents. For context about EU‑U.S. framework intentions, refer to the August 21, 2025 joint statement  and EUROFER’s press release noting the continued 50% rate.

question: Between October 15 and December 31, 2025 (UTC), will Iran and at least one of the E3 (France, Germany, United Kingdom) or the United States publicly announce the initiation of formal talks on Iran’s nuclear program?
background:
Status quo as of September 30, 2025: On August 28, 2025, the E3 (France, Germany, and the United Kingdom) notified the UN Security Council that Iran was in significant non-performance of its commitments under the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), thereby initiating the snapback process under UNSC Resolution 2231. A draft resolution led by China and Russia to delay the snapback failed at the Security Council on September 26, 2025. The United States confirmed that UN sanctions were reimposed the evening of September 27, 2025 (8:00 p.m. EDT), concluding the snapback process initiated by the E3 on August 28 , and the EU Council detailed the restrictive measures reimposed on September 29, 2025. Reuters contemporaneous reporting also describes the snapback taking effect at 0000 GMT on Sunday, September 28, 2025, and notes Western intentions to return to a mixture of pressure and dialogue going forward.

In July–September 2025, the E3 publicly offered Iran a limited, one-time extension to delay snapback conditioned on concrete steps, including resuming direct and unconditional negotiations with the United States, restoring IAEA access, and accounting for Iran’s high-enriched uranium stockpile; the E3 emphasized that reimposed UN sanctions are not the end of diplomacy. As of mid–September 2025, statements at the IAEA Board and by European officials indicated Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile was far above JCPOA limits (overall stockpile at 48× the JCPOA cap; >440 kg enriched up to 60%), and that the IAEA lacked continuity of knowledge and access to comprehensively verify stocks and activities. On September 23, 2025, Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei publicly ruled out negotiations with the United States on the nuclear program, calling US demands a “diktat,” while Iranian and European officials held discussions on the margins of UNGA. Statements from US and European representatives at the UN underscored that snapback does not preclude a diplomatic resolution in the future.

Why this question: Despite heightened pressure, both Western actors and Iran’s interlocutors have signaled that diplomacy remains possible, creating plausible room for movement in Q4 2025. The event—publicly announced initiation of formal nuclear talks—would be a clear, binary signal with non-trivial uncertainty.

Key concepts and references forecasters may find useful:
- JCPOA (2015 Iran nuclear deal): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Comprehensive_Plan_of_Action
- UNSC Resolution 2231: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_2231
- IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Atomic_Energy_Agency
- Iran’s nuclear program overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_program_of_Iran
- Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (official English name and role): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Iran) 

Typical official sources for announcements/readouts:
- Iran MFA: https://www.mfa.gov.ir (English portal commonly available at https://en.mfa.ir)
- US Department of State: https://www.state.gov (Press releases/readouts: https://www.state.gov/press-releases/)
- UK FCDO: https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/foreign-commonwealth-development-office (News: https://www.gov.uk/government/announcements)
- French MFA (MEAE): https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/en/ (Country file/news pages host Iran-related statements)
- German Federal Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt): https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en/newsroom
- Credible wire services (fallback if primary sources are temporarily inaccessible): Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), AFP (https://www.afp.com)
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves to Yes if, between October 15, 2025, 00:00:00 UTC and December 31, 2025, 23:59:59 UTC, BOTH of the following occur:

1) Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) issues a public, official announcement stating that formal talks/negotiations on Iran’s nuclear program have begun, or are scheduled to begin on a specified date on or before December 31, 2025 (UTC). The announcement must be published either on an official Iranian government web domain (e.g., mfa.gov.ir) or on an official, verified social media account of the Iran MFA or the Foreign Minister.

2) At least one of the following counterparts issues a public, official announcement, either jointly or reciprocally, describing the same initiation of formal talks/negotiations (as in 1) on Iran’s nuclear program: the US Department of State, the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE), or the German Federal Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt). The announcement must be published on the counterpart’s official web domain or an official, verified social media account.

Definitions and clarifications:
- Formal talks/negotiations on Iran’s nuclear program: A structured, official negotiation process between state representatives concerning Iran’s nuclear activities, safeguards, enrichment, the JCPOA, UNSCR 2231, and/or related nuclear terms. The announcement must use terms such as “formal talks,” “negotiations,” “a negotiating round,” or “talks will begin,” and explicitly reference the nuclear program (or widely used synonyms such as “nuclear issue,” “nuclear file,” “JCPOA,” “IAEA safeguards,” or “Resolution 2231”). Track II/backchannel or purely unofficial meetings do not count.
- Joint announcement: A single statement co-issued by Iran’s MFA and at least one counterpart ministry/department listed above, posted on at least one of their official domains or official verified accounts.
- Reciprocal announcement: Separate statements from Iran’s MFA and the counterpart ministry/department listed above, referencing the same initiation of talks/negotiations, issued within 168 hours (7 days) of each other.
- Publicly announce: Publication on an official government website or an official, verified account on major platforms (e.g., X/Twitter, Facebook, YouTube), where the issuing entity is clearly identified as Iran’s MFA or the specified counterpart ministry/department. Media reports alone do not count unless used as a fallback per Evidence below.
- Eligible counterparts: US Department of State, UK FCDO, French MEAE, German Auswärtiges Amt. Iran’s MFA official English name and role: “Ministry of Foreign Affairs” of the Islamic Republic of Iran.
- Date/time: All timing is in UTC. Only announcements within the window October 15, 2025, 00:00:00 UTC through December 31, 2025, 23:59:59 UTC are considered.
- Scheduling versus occurrence: Announcements that “will begin” count if the specified first session date is on or before December 31, 2025 (UTC). If, by December 31, 2025 (UTC), an official cancellation of the scheduled first session is announced by either party, the initiation does not count.
- Exclusions: Announcements solely about humanitarian exchanges, regional security talks unrelated to the nuclear file, technical IAEA meetings without negotiation between Iran and the E3/US, or generalized statements of willingness to talk absent a concrete initiation or scheduled negotiating round.

Evidence required to resolve Yes:
- URLs to the qualifying announcements on the official website(s) and/or posts on official, verified social media accounts of Iran’s MFA and the relevant counterpart. If official sites are temporarily inaccessible at resolution time, credible wire service reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP) that directly quotes or captures the official announcements may be accepted, provided it clearly identifies the issuing entity and the content of the announcement.

Resolution sources and verification approach:
- Primary: Official government press releases/statements/readouts on the sites listed in Background and in the Definitions above. The resolver will verify language explicitly initiating formal nuclear talks and the timing (UTC) of publication.
- Secondary (fallback, if needed): Credible wire services (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP) that reproduce or quote the official announcement text.

Outcome determination:
- Yes if both 1) and 2) occur as defined within the stated window.
- No if the criteria are not met by December 31, 2025, 23:59:59 UTC.

Context sources for the status quo and diplomatic posture: E3 snapback initiation and conditions for delay ; UNSC vote failure to extend sanctions relief and member statements on diplomacy ; US confirmation of snapback completion and statement that diplomacy remains an option ; EU Council description of reimposed measures ; Reuters analysis on timing and the mix of pressure and dialogue ; IAEA-related stockpile and access context ; Khamenei statement ruling out US talks.
