Examples listed in recent IAEA reporting include: Fordow Fuel Enrichment Plant (FFEP), Natanz Fuel Enrichment Plant (FEP) and Pilot FEP (PFEP), Uranium Conversion Facility (UCF), Fuel Manufacturing Plant (FMP), Fuel Plate Fabrication Plant (FPFP), Enriched UO2 Powder Plant (EUPP), Khondab/Arak Heavy Water Research Reactor (KHRR), Heavy Water Production Plant (HWPP), Tehran Research Reactor (TRR), Jaber Ibn Hayan Multipurpose Laboratory (JHL), and the Molybdenum, Iodine and Xenon Radioisotope Production facility (MIX), among others; BNPP (Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant) is explicitly excluded by the question wording.

Resolution sources context
- The IAEA’s “Monitoring and Verification in Iran” topic page aggregates relevant Iran safeguards reports, statements, and news and can serve as a discovery hub. The IAEA’s “IAEA and Iran – IAEA Board Reports” page aggregates Board/DG reports on Iran by year. Director General statements are published on iaea.org (e.g., the Sept 8, 2025 Board statement). These official iaea.org sources will be used for resolution.

Why this is forecastable
- As of early September 2025, only limited activity at BNPP had occurred, while broader in-field verification remained halted; subsequent developments could plausibly lead either to partial resumption at another facility or continued suspension through year-end, leaving meaningful uncertainty for forecasters.
resolution_criteria:
Question
- Resolve whether, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, the IAEA publicly reports that its inspectors conducted any in-field verification at an Iranian safeguarded nuclear facility other than the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant (BNPP).

Start and end dates (UTC)
- Eligible publication window: 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

What counts as a qualifying report
- A qualifying “public report” must be an official IAEA publication on iaea.org published within the window, specifically one of the following:
  1) An IAEA Board of Governors report (GOV/… document) or Director General report posted on the IAEA’s “IAEA and Iran – IAEA Board Reports” page ; or
  2) A Director General statement posted on iaea.org (News Center > Statements) ; or
  3) An IAEA News/Press release or article posted under the IAEA’s Iran “Monitoring and Verification in Iran” topic page.

Event that must be reported
- The qualifying IAEA publication must explicitly state that IAEA inspectors conducted in-field verification (see definitions below) at at least one Iranian safeguarded nuclear facility other than BNPP. The publication must either:
  a) Name at least one such non-BNPP facility (e.g., FFEP, Natanz FEP/PFEP, UCF, FMP, FPFP, EUPP, KHRR/Arak, HWPP, TRR, JHL, MIX, etc.) ; or
  b) State unambiguously that inspections/in-field verification occurred at a safeguarded nuclear facility other than BNPP (e.g., wording that clearly excludes BNPP).

Definitions to apply
- “In-field verification” (counts): on-site safeguards verification activities by IAEA inspectors at a facility, including inspections (ad hoc, routine, special), design information verification (DIV), physical inventory verification (PIV), nuclear material accountancy checks, application of containment/surveillance, and environmental sampling performed at the facility.
- “Not in-field verification” (does not count): remote monitoring with data transmitted off-site, analysis of commercial satellite imagery, or other open-source assessments without inspector presence at the facility.
- “Iranian safeguarded nuclear facility”: a nuclear facility in Iran that the IAEA treats as a facility under Iran’s NPT Comprehensive Safeguards Agreement in its official reports (examples listed above). BNPP is excluded by the question wording.

What does NOT qualify
- Any activity solely at BNPP (Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant) does not qualify.
- References to “inspections” or “monitoring” that do not clearly indicate inspector presence on-site at a safeguarded nuclear facility (e.g., remote monitoring, satellite analysis) do not qualify.
- Third-party media reports or statements by non-IAEA officials do not qualify unless they are IAEA publications on iaea.org as specified above.

Resolution
- YES if at least one qualifying IAEA publication (as defined) is posted on iaea.org within the publication window and explicitly indicates that in-field verification by IAEA inspectors occurred at any Iranian safeguarded nuclear facility other than BNPP on or after 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC.
- NO if no such qualifying IAEA publication is posted within the window.

Tie-breaking and conflicts
- If multiple IAEA publications within the window conflict, prefer (in order): Board of Governors GOV reports > Director General reports/statements > IAEA News/Press releases. If conflicts remain, prefer the most recent publication within the window.

Documentation for resolvers
- Use the following IAEA pages to search for qualifying publications: “Monitoring and Verification in Iran” topic page ; “IAEA and Iran – IAEA Board Reports” aggregation page ; and the IAEA News Center Statements section (example of format and hosting shown in the DG’s Sept 8, 2025 statement). Context on the June 2025 halt in in‑field verification, withdrawal of inspectors, Bushehr-only access, and loss of continuity of knowledge is documented in GOV/2025/50 and DG statements.

question: Will UK headline CPI (12‑month rate) for November 2025 be at least 3.5%?
background:
Context as of 2025-09-30: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) schedules its statistical bulletin “Consumer price inflation, UK: November 2025” for publication on 17 December 2025 at 07:00 (UK local time), and notes it is not yet published as of now. The latest published headline Consumer Prices Index (CPI) annual rate is 3.8% for the 12 months to August 2025 (“The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) rose by 3.8% in the 12 months to August 2025, unchanged from July.”). The Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Summary (September 2025) states: “Twelve-month CPI inflation was 3.8% in August, and is expected to increase slightly in September, before falling towards the 2% target thereafter.”.

Definitions and scope:
- Consumer Prices Index (CPI): The UK measure of consumer price inflation published monthly by the ONS. For background and wording conventions, see the ONS bulletin for August 2025.
- 12‑month rate (year-over-year, YoY): The percentage change in the CPI over the 12 months to the specified month, expressed in percent. ONS bulletins phrase this as “The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) rose by X% in the 12 months to [month year]…”.
- Headline CPI: For this question, “headline CPI” means the CPI 12‑month rate (not CPIH, not “core” CPI, and not any seasonally adjusted, trimmed, or alternative measure).
- At least: Greater than or equal to (≥).
- Units and rounding: Resolution uses the CPI 12‑month rate value as reported in the ONS bulletin text and/or headline figures for November 2025, which ONS typically reports to one decimal place. No independent recalculation or alternative rounding is applied.

Why this is non-trivial: As of August 2025, headline CPI is 3.8% , and the Bank of England indicated a near-term uptick in September followed by a decline towards target. Whether November’s YoY CPI prints at or above 3.5% depends on developments in energy, food, administered prices, and base effects, creating plausible uncertainty around the 3.5% threshold within the time frame. 

Key source to monitor: The ONS bulletin page “Consumer price inflation, UK: November 2025” (release scheduled 17 December 2025, 07:00).
resolution_criteria:
- Question: Will the UK headline CPI 12‑month rate for November 2025 be at least 3.5%?
- Start and end for eligibility: This question pertains solely to the CPI 12‑month rate for November 2025. Resolution will occur after the scheduled ONS publication on 2025-12-17.
- Primary resolution source: The ONS statistical bulletin page “Consumer price inflation, UK: November 2025”.
- Measured quantity: The CPI 12‑month rate (YoY) for November 2025, as presented by ONS in the bulletin’s headline figures and/or main points (e.g., phrased as “The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) rose by X% in the 12 months to November 2025”). This phrasing is consistent with ONS conventions.
- Decision rule: If the published CPI 12‑month rate for November 2025 is ≥ 3.5%, resolve Yes; otherwise resolve No.
- Time zone and timing: Resolution will use the value as displayed on the bulletin page on and after publication on 2025-12-17. For avoidance of ambiguity, the check will be performed no later than 2025-12-31 23:59 UTC. If ONS issues an official correction to the November 2025 bulletin before 2025-12-31 23:59 UTC, the corrected value will be used; corrections after that time will be disregarded.
- Exclusions: CPIH, “core” CPI, alternative inflation measures, or any values derived from datasets other than the named bulletin are not considered unless the bulletin is temporarily unavailable; in such a case, the same November 2025 CPI 12‑month rate as reported by ONS on the bulletin page once accessible will be used.

Source-of-truth schedule and current status: ONS indicates the November 2025 CPI bulletin is scheduled for 17 December 2025 at 07:00 and is not yet published as of today. The most recent CPI 12‑month rate published is 3.8% for August 2025 , and the Bank of England expects a slight rise in September followed by a move towards 2% thereafter.

question: Will TikTok’s U.S. divestiture deal formally close between 2025-10-15 and 2025-12-31 (UTC)?
background:
Context and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- U.S. Executive Order and structure: On September 25, 2025, the White House issued the executive order “Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security,” determining that a proposed plan for a “qualified divestiture” would allow Americans to continue using TikTok while addressing national security concerns. The order describes a U.S.-based joint venture to operate TikTok’s U.S. application, majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, with ByteDance and affiliates owning less than 20%. It also directs the Attorney General to delay enforcement of the Act for 120 days to allow time for the divestiture to be completed.
- Deal framing and valuation: Reuters reported the same day that the President signed the order declaring the sale plan ready, with a valuation of about $14 billion and ByteDance to hold less than 20% in the U.S. entity.
- Investor consortium reporting: Prior reporting indicated a U.S. investor consortium led by Oracle and Silver Lake (with other participants reported to include Andreessen Horowitz) controlling roughly 80% of the U.S. TikTok entity. Later Reuters coverage noted expectations that ByteDance would maintain ownership interests but cede control of data, content, and the algorithm to a new U.S. joint venture, raising questions about the extent of divestiture.
- China’s stance: Coverage following the order noted China’s conspicuous public silence about formal approval even as the U.S. President said he had received a green light from China’s President; analysts quoted by CNBC argued China has little incentive to permit a ByteDance divestment. Reuters’ contemporaneous report quoted the U.S. President claiming he told President Xi and “he said go ahead with it,” while also noting Chinese official statements in general terms about market-based negotiations.
- What is “TikTok U.S.” for purposes of this question: TikTok Inc. is an American company incorporated and headquartered in California; its ultimate parent is ByteDance Ltd. (a privately held company with operations in China). TikTok’s proprietary algorithm is owned by ByteDance, and portions of the platform’s source code are developed and maintained in China.

Key definitions and links forecasters may find useful:
- Divestiture: “the partial or full disposal of a company or other entity’s operations or assets through sale, exchange, closure, or bankruptcy.” Investopedia: https://www.investopedia.com/terms/d/divestiture.asp.
- Closing (M&A): the final stage of a sale where all conditions are met, documents executed, and consideration is delivered; distinct from signing. Divestopedia: https://www.divestopedia.com/definition/926/closing.
- Qualified divestiture (as used here): as described and determined in the September 25, 2025 executive order “Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security,” which specifies a U.S.-based entity operating TikTok’s U.S. application, majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, with ByteDance and affiliates owning less than 20%, and with operational control of algorithms, code, content moderation, and U.S. user data under the U.S. entity’s control and monitored by trusted partners.

Why this question is interesting and plausibly uncertain by year-end:
- The deal sits at the intersection of U.S.–China policy, national security reviews, and complex cross-border corporate carve-outs. While the White House order frames a path and extends a non-enforcement window to enable a closing, valuation, ownership, control, and foreign approvals (or non-objection) introduce material execution risk before December 31, 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Binary resolution as of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, for events occurring between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC (all times UTC):

Question: Will the TikTok U.S. divestiture deal formally close in this period?

Definitions for this market:
- TikTok U.S. business: the operation of the TikTok application for users in the United States, currently offered by TikTok Inc., an American company incorporated and headquartered in California, whose ultimate parent is ByteDance Ltd..
- Qualified divestiture: the transaction structure determined and described in the September 25, 2025 executive order “Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security,” involving a U.S.-based entity to operate TikTok’s U.S. application, majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, with ByteDance and affiliates owning less than 20%, and with control of algorithms/code, content moderation, and U.S. user data under that U.S. entity, as specified in the order.
- Close / Closing: consummation of the transaction (distinct from signing) such that all required approvals and conditions precedent are satisfied, transaction documents are executed, and consideration is delivered, effecting transfer of ownership/control as specified in the definitive agreements.

Resolution:
- YES if, between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, there is credible public evidence that the transaction constituting the qualified divestiture of TikTok’s U.S. business has closed. Evidence must satisfy one of the following:
  (A) An official statement/press release from TikTok and/or ByteDance AND an official statement/press release from the buyer/new U.S. entity (or a public filing by a public buyer, such as a Form 8-K), each explicitly stating that the transaction has “closed” or “been completed,” and clearly identifying that this closing covers TikTok’s U.S. business consistent with the qualified divestiture described in the September 25, 2025 executive order; AND corroboration by at least two independent major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, WSJ, FT, Bloomberg, NYT, CNBC) reporting that the deal has closed; or
  (B) An official U.S. government statement (e.g., from the White House or Department of Justice) that the qualified divestiture contemplated by the September 25, 2025 executive order has been completed/closed, thereby satisfying the Act’s requirements.

- NO if no such evidence exists by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, or if public communications indicate only signing, intent, or conditional approvals without closing (e.g., “framework agreement,” “definitive agreement signed,” or “subject to remaining approvals”).

Additional notes:
- Timezone: All dates/times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
- Start date: Only closings that occur on/after 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC count toward a YES outcome.
- Conflicts: If sources conflict, priority is given to official statements by the transaction parties and U.S. government statements. If ambiguity remains, the market resolves NO.
- Name changes: The new U.S. entity’s name may differ from reporting; what matters is that the closing clearly pertains to the qualified divestiture of the TikTok U.S. business as described in the September 25, 2025 executive order.

question: Will Shein’s IPO result in its shares beginning to trade on a public stock exchange by December 31, 2025 (UTC)?
background:
Context and status quo as of early Q4 2025:
- What is Shein? Shein (SHEIN Group) is a global fast-fashion e-commerce company headquartered in Singapore, operating the SHEIN marketplace/brand and related apparel/accessories businesses.
- Definitions you’ll need: An initial public offering (IPO) is the first sale of a company’s shares to the public, typically underwritten by investment banks and accompanied by a listing on a stock exchange (i.e., the first time the shares are offered to public investors). A stock exchange is an organized marketplace where securities such as shares are bought and sold.
- 2025 listing timeline and regulatory posture:
  - April 2025: Shein secured approval from the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) for a planned London IPO, but still needed approval from China’s securities regulator (CSRC) for an offshore listing under Beijing’s rules; as of that date, the IPO had not occurred.
  - May 2025: Reporting indicated the London IPO attempt stalled due to the lack of CSRC approval; Shein began working toward a Hong Kong listing within 2025.
  - July 2025: Shein confidentially filed a draft prospectus with the Hong Kong exchange and sought a CSRC nod, while keeping London as a preference if an FCA-accepted, CSRC-approved prospectus were possible.
  - August 2025: Shein considered relocating its headquarters back to mainland China to improve prospects of obtaining Beijing’s approval for a Hong Kong IPO; discussions were preliminary.
  - Late September 2025: Reuters’ coverage still described Shein as working toward a Hong Kong listing after the proposed London IPO failed to secure CSRC approval.
- Additional headwinds cited in coverage: Allegations and political scrutiny tied to supply chains; U.S. tariff changes affecting Shein’s de minimis import treatment; and broader geopolitical tensions, all potential influences on timing and valuation.

Taken together, public reporting through late September 2025 describes Shein as actively pursuing an IPO with Hong Kong as the most likely venue, while London remained a possibility contingent on CSRC approval; none of these reports indicate that an IPO had already been completed at those times.

Why this question is forecastable now: Multiple regulatory dependencies (CSRC approval, exchange admission), venue uncertainty (HKEX vs. LSE), and political/trade headwinds create genuine uncertainty about whether Shein can complete an IPO and commence trading by year-end 2025.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone:
- Eligible events must occur between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive. All times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

What counts as “Yes”:
- Resolve Yes if all of the following occur within the time window:
  1) Shein conducts an initial public offering (IPO), defined as the company’s first sale of shares to public investors in connection with admission to trading on a stock exchange.
  2) The issuer’s equity securities (ordinary shares or depositary receipts representing such shares) are admitted to trading on a stock exchange (i.e., an organized marketplace where securities are bought and sold).
  3) Trading in those securities “begins” (i.e., the exchange’s official communication indicates admission/commencement of dealings, such as “admission to trading” or “dealing in the shares commences,” and the first trading session opens) within the time window. 

What does not count:
- The following do NOT satisfy this market:
  - A direct listing without a primary share sale (no IPO).
  - A merger with or acquisition by a SPAC (de-SPAC), reverse takeover, or any transaction where the resulting listing is not the result of Shein’s own IPO.
  - A priced IPO where the first day of trading is scheduled outside the time window (e.g., priced on Dec 31 UTC but trading starts Jan 1 UTC).

Who “Shein” refers to:
- “Shein” means SHEIN Group (the corporate parent of the SHEIN fast-fashion business) or any successor holding company identified in the IPO prospectus as the top-level parent that directly or indirectly consolidates substantially all of Shein’s operating business (e.g., the SHEIN e-commerce marketplace and related apparel/accessory operations).

Primary resolution sources (examples):
- Official exchange notices confirming admission and first day of dealings/trading, such as:
  - HKEX New Listing Information (Main Board): https://www2.hkexnews.hk/New-Listings/New-Listing-Information/Main-Board?sc_lang=en
  - HKEX Application Proof/PHIP index (for corroboration of issuer identity and listing documents): https://www1.hkexnews.hk/app/appindex.html
  - London Stock Exchange Regulatory News Service (RNS) admission notices: https://www.londonstockexchange.com/news
- Issuer press releases on SHEIN Group’s newsroom: https://www.sheingroup.com/newsroom/corporate-news/press-releases/
- Corroboration from major wire services (e.g., Reuters), which have extensively covered Shein’s listing process.

How the resolver will decide on Dec 31, 2025:
- The resolver will check whether any official exchange notice (HKEX, LSE, or another recognized stock exchange) shows that trading in Shein’s equity securities commenced within the specified UTC time window, and confirm issuer identity matches the “Who Shein refers to” definition. If such a notice exists, and at least one of the above corroborating sources reports the debut, the market resolves Yes. Otherwise, the market resolves No.

Edge cases and clarifications:
- If trading begins and is subsequently suspended or halted, it still counts as Yes provided trading commenced within the time window per the exchange’s official notice.
- Dual listings: If Shein lists on multiple exchanges, the first date and time trading begins on any one exchange within the window controls.
- Depositary receipts: If the IPO is executed via depositary receipts representing Shein’s equity and those receipts are listed/trading as part of the IPO, it counts.
- If the issuer reorganizes (e.g., inserts a new holding company) solely to facilitate the IPO, it still counts as Yes so long as the post-reorg parent matches the “Who Shein refers to” definition and the transaction otherwise meets the IPO and trading criteria.

question: Will the EU formally endorse and commit to implementing a “Reparations Loan” to Ukraine using immobilised Russian sovereign asset cash balances (via an EU- or G7-backed SPV) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-31 (UTC)?
background:
Summary of the concept and current status as of 2025-10-01:
- The European Commission has outlined a plan often termed a “Reparations Loan” to fund Ukraine in 2026–2027 by leveraging cash balances accrued from immobilised Russian central bank securities held in Europe, particularly at Euroclear in Belgium. Under the plan, cash balances would be transferred to an EU- or G7-owned special purpose vehicle (SPV), while Euroclear would receive EU-backed zero-coupon bonds or a tailored debt instrument to cover legal risk; Ukraine would only repay the loan if Russia pays war reparations in a future settlement.
- Reuters’ detailed explainer reports roughly €210bn of frozen Russian sovereign assets held in Europe, with about €185bn at Euroclear and around €175bn of those having become cash as securities matured; after first covering the existing G7 ERA loan (~€45bn), officials discuss an additional loan capacity of ~€130–€140bn for the new Reparations Loan, subject to an IMF needs assessment for 2026–27. Euronews similarly describes a cash pot of ~€176bn at Euroclear (with ~€10bn expected), a total loan framework up to €185bn (of which ~€140bn would be available after backing the €45bn G7 credit), and the Commission’s concept of a zero-interest loan to Ukraine with repayment contingent on reparations.
- Euroclear’s H1 2025 press release states that as of end-June 2025, €194bn of sanctioned Russian assets were on Euroclear Bank’s balance sheet, and interest on those cash balances was ~€2.7bn in H1 2025. This contextualises the scale of immobilised assets and proceeds.
- As of Oct 1, 2025, major EU leaders have signaled support in principle but highlighted legal and risk-sharing concerns. Reuters reports leaders planned to discuss legal aspects at the European Council meeting on Oct 23–24, with Belgium, France, and Luxembourg insisting on strong guarantees given asset location and litigation risk; Denmark, Sweden, the Netherlands, and Germany expressed varying degrees of support, while the EU’s top diplomat noted not all member states were fully on board; G7 participation in guarantees was to be discussed as well. AP similarly notes a proposed loan size around €140bn, positions from leaders (including caution on international law and guarantees), and that the plan aims to use cash balances without outright confiscation of sovereign assets.
- Politically and legally, multiple reports emphasise the design seeks to avoid confiscation (a red line for many governments and the ECB) while still mobilising cash balances for Ukraine via an SPV, with risks to be collectively guaranteed by EU (and potentially non-EU G7) governments.

Key definitions and helpful references for forecasters:
- European Council: the body of EU heads of state or government. See official overview: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/european-council-and-council-of-the-eu/
- European Council conclusions: the formal document adopted at the end of each European Council meeting stating the Council’s political positions and decisions. See: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/european-council/conclusions/
- European Commission Communication (COM document): an official Commission document published on EUR-Lex and/or the Commission’s “Press corner”, often outlining adopted policy/legislative initiatives. See EUR-Lex document types: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/content/tools/TableOfSectors/types_of_documents_in_eurlex.html
- Special purpose vehicle (SPV): a legally distinct entity used to isolate financial risk. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special-purpose_entity
- Euroclear: a Brussels-based central securities depository. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euroclear
- “Frozen”/“immobilised” Russian sovereign assets: Russian central bank securities and related balances restricted under sanctions; figures and mechanics described in Reuters and Euronews reports above.

Why this is forecastable with non-trivial uncertainty:
- There is momentum and high-level political support to discuss the Reparations Loan in late October 2025, yet significant legal, institutional, and guarantee-sharing hurdles remain, and unanimity issues around sanction renewals could complicate timelines. A formal endorsement (by European Council conclusions) or a Commission commitment via an adopted Communication/Decision is plausible but far from assured by year-end, creating high entropy.
resolution_criteria:
Time window and timezone:
- Eligible actions must occur between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Outcome definition:
- Resolve “Yes” if, within the time window, either of the following is satisfied:
  1) European Council conclusions explicitly endorse proceeding with the EU “Reparations Loan” concept or an equivalent SPV structure that uses cash balances from immobilised/frozen Russian sovereign assets to fund a loan to Ukraine, with Ukraine’s repayment contingent on future war reparations. “Explicitly endorse proceeding” means the conclusions unambiguously support the EU implementing the plan (e.g., by stating that the European Council endorses/supports/mandates/decides to proceed with such a loan/SPV or invites/mandates the Commission to prepare/establish it for financing Ukraine in 2026–27). Mere calls to “explore”, “study”, or “consider” options without endorsing proceeding do NOT count.
  2) The European Commission publishes an adopted Communication (COM document) or an adopted Commission Decision (a formal College adoption), which explicitly commits the Commission to implement the scheme (e.g., establishing the SPV and/or initiating the transfer of cash balances from Euroclear or equivalent custodians, backed by EU guarantees), beyond exploratory or consultation papers. A press release in the Commission “Press corner” stating that “the Commission has adopted” such a Communication/Decision also suffices if it clearly describes the mechanics (loan to Ukraine backed by cash balances from immobilised Russian sovereign assets and repayment contingent on reparations).

What qualifies as “equivalent SPV structure”:
- Any EU- or EU+G7-owned SPV arrangement that: (a) sources funding from cash balances accrued from immobilised/frozen Russian sovereign assets (not outright confiscating the assets); (b) extends an interest-free or zero-interest loan to Ukraine; and (c) specifies that Ukraine’s repayment obligation is contingent upon Russia paying war reparations. This captures the variants reported by Reuters and Euronews.

What does NOT count:
- Council of the EU (ministerial) conclusions, informal statements by individual leaders, speeches, interviews, op-eds, media leaks, non-adopted drafts, feasibility studies, or generic language about “supporting Ukraine” that lacks explicit endorsement to proceed with the Reparations Loan/SPV mechanics described above.

Sources of truth for resolution:
- For European Council conclusions: the official conclusions published on consilium.europa.eu for European Council meetings held in the window (e.g., Oct 23–24 or any subsequent meeting in 2025). See: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/european-council/conclusions/
- For Commission actions: the European Commission “Press corner” and EUR-Lex entries of adopted Commission Communications/Decisions (COM documents and Commission Decisions) in the window. See: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner and https://eur-lex.europa.eu/ (document type overview: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/content/tools/TableOfSectors/types_of_documents_in_eurlex.html)

Context citations supporting the defined mechanics and current status:
- Detailed plan mechanics, asset amounts, cash-balance transfer to an SPV, zero-coupon bonds to Euroclear, loan repayment contingent on reparations: Reuters explainer ; corroborating mechanics and amounts: Euronews.
- Asset scale at Euroclear and interest proceeds: Euroclear H1 2025 press release.
- Leaders’ positions, legal concerns, and planned European Council discussion dates: Reuters Oct 1 status ; summary of positions and legal cautions: AP.

Resolution notes:
- The resolver should locate the relevant European Council conclusions or Commission documents/press releases in the specified window and check for explicit endorsement/commitment that matches the mechanics defined above. If neither criterion is met by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, resolve “No”.

Rationale for this framing:
- The event is significant, plausibly time-bound to late-2025 discussions, and depends on legal/institutional hurdles and cross-national guarantees, making outcomes genuinely uncertain and researchable.

question: Between 2025-09-25 and 2025-12-31 (UTC), will a U.S.-based TikTok joint venture close such that ByteDance and its affiliates own <20% of the U.S. entity that operates TikTok’s U.S. application?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- On 2025-09-25, the White House issued a presidential action describing a framework under which TikTok’s U.S. application would be operated by a new U.S.-based joint venture (the “U.S. TikTok JV”), majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, with ByteDance Ltd. and its affiliates holding less than 20% of the JV upon completion. The action also directed the Attorney General not to enforce the relevant Act for 120 days to permit the contemplated divestiture to be completed. A contemporaneous White House fact sheet likewise states ByteDance will hold less than 20% of the new U.S. joint venture and outlines JV governance and security controls (e.g., Oracle-hosted U.S. data environment).
- Separately, on 2025-09-16, a presidential action further extended the enforcement delay for the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (the “Act”) until 2025-12-16, directing DOJ to take no action to enforce the Act or impose penalties during the specified delay periods.

What forecasters should know:
- The 2025-09-25 presidential action describes a “qualified divestiture” framework, under which implementation agreements are to be executed and the transaction closed so that U.S. persons control the U.S. TikTok JV and ByteDance’s residual stake is <20%.
- A determination or public confirmation by U.S. authorities (e.g., White House/DOJ/CFIUS) that TikTok has undergone a “qualified divestiture” per the 2025-09-25 order would be strong evidence that the JV has closed consistent with the <20% ByteDance ownership condition specified in the presidential materials.

Key definitions and references (for clarity):
- “U.S. TikTok JV”: the new joint-venture company based in the United States that will operate TikTok’s U.S. application as described by the White House on 2025-09-25. See also general joint venture background: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_venture.
- “ByteDance and its affiliates”: ByteDance Ltd. and any “affiliate” of ByteDance (affiliate has the meaning in 17 CFR 240.12b-2: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.12b-2).
- “Owns” / “ownership percentage”: assessed on a beneficial ownership basis consistent with 17 CFR 240.13d-3 (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.13d-3), including any securities exercisable or convertible within 60 days. For this market question, the practical test is what the authoritative closing source (defined below) states regarding ByteDance’s percentage. If both a precise percentage and a clear statement that the stake is below 20% are provided, either suffices.
- “Close,” “closed,” or “completed”: the transaction has been consummated (i.e., all closing conditions satisfied and effectiveness occurred), as evidenced by an official closing announcement or filing by one of the defined authoritative sources below.
- Time zone: All dates/times in this question are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
- Eligible window for events: 2025-09-25 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Context on resolution sources:
- Presidential actions and fact sheets are posted on whitehouse.gov at durable URLs (e.g., the 2025-09-25 presidential action and fact sheet) and will be accepted for determining whether an official “qualified divestiture” determination has been made and/or the transaction has closed consistent with the specified ownership.
- The 2025-09-16 enforcement-delay action remains relevant background regarding DOJ non-enforcement timing through 2025-12-16.
resolution_criteria:
This resolves based on publicly available information posted no later than 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Question: Between 2025-09-25 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, will there be a confirmed closing of the transaction to form and/or transfer operations to a U.S.-based TikTok joint venture such that ByteDance Ltd. and its affiliates own less than 20.00% of the U.S. entity that operates TikTok’s U.S. application?

Resolution rules:
- Resolve “Yes” if, within the eligible window, at least one of the following authoritative sources confirms that the transaction has closed (using language such as “closed,” “completed,” or “consummated”) and that ByteDance’s ownership in the U.S. TikTok JV is strictly less than 20% (i.e., <20.00%):
  1) An official press release or transaction closing announcement posted on the websites of TikTok, ByteDance, or the U.S. TikTok JV (if named/created), or an SEC filing by a public company party to the transaction that discloses closing and ownership percentages (e.g., Form 8-K, 6-K, or similar).
  2) A U.S. Government announcement (e.g., White House presidential action/fact sheet, DOJ or CFIUS public statement) explicitly stating that the transaction has closed consistent with the 2025-09-25 “qualified divestiture” framework under which ByteDance’s ownership is <20%.
  3) Major wire-service reporting (Reuters, AP) or top-tier outlets (e.g., WSJ, Bloomberg, FT) that explicitly cite one of the sources in 1) or 2) above, and relay both the occurrence of closing and the ByteDance <20% ownership.

- Resolve “No” if by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC there is no such confirmation, or if available authoritative sources confirm closing but indicate ByteDance’s ownership is greater than or equal to 20.00% at closing.

Clarifications:
- If the White House/DOJ/CFIUS publicly determines that TikTok has undergone a “qualified divestiture” per the 2025-09-25 presidential action, that will suffice for “Yes,” because the presidential materials specify ByteDance will hold <20% of the U.S. JV under the qualified divestiture framework.
- “Ownership” refers to beneficial ownership and any direct/indirect equity interest, including via instruments exercisable/convertible within 60 days, consistent with 17 CFR 240.13d-3. However, for resolution, the percentage explicitly stated by the authoritative closing source governs.
- The U.S. entity (“U.S. TikTok JV”) is the new U.S.-based joint venture that will operate TikTok’s U.S. application as described by the White House on 2025-09-25.
- Non-binding agreements, letters of intent, partial step completions (e.g., only regulatory approval without closing), or speculative media reports without a qualifying source do not count.

Primary resolution sources (non-exhaustive):
- White House Presidential Actions and Fact Sheets (e.g., “Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security” on 2025-09-25; related fact sheet).
- DOJ or CFIUS public statements or notices.
- Corporate press releases posted on official websites of TikTok, ByteDance, or the U.S. TikTok JV; relevant SEC filings by parties to the transaction.

Edge cases:
- If multiple sources conflict, prefer primary official sources (White House/DOJ/CFIUS; company filings/press releases). If still conflicting, the market administrator will wait up to seven calendar days for clarifying official statements before resolving.
- If the closing occurs within the window but is posted publicly after the deadline, it does not count. Conversely, filings/announcements posted within the window that clearly state closing has occurred within the window do count.

Time zone: All times UTC.

Citations for background claims: presidential action describing the JV structure, <20% ByteDance ownership, and 120-day DOJ non-enforcement (2025-09-25) ; White House fact sheet reiterating <20% ownership and JV governance and security controls ; enforcement delay extension to 2025-12-16 (2025-09-16).

question: OPEC+8: Will the eight-country group announce a net increase in required production for January 2026 by December 31, 2025?
background:
Context as of 2025-10-01 (UTC):
- What is OPEC and OPEC+? The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is an intergovernmental organization of oil-producing nations; “OPEC+” refers to OPEC members plus allied non-OPEC producers that cooperate under the Declaration of Cooperation framework.

- The 2025 eight-country arrangement (“OPEC+8”): In 2025, eight OPEC+ producers — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman — have been issuing monthly decisions on production adjustments, coordinated via OPEC press releases. On September 7, 2025, an OPEC press release stated an adjustment of +137 thousand barrels per day (kbd) to be implemented in October 2025 and identified these eight countries as the participants. A July 5, 2025 OPEC press release described the ongoing monthly-meeting structure and noted that an August 2025 adjustment of +548 kbd (equivalent to four monthly increments) would be implemented from the July 2025 required production level, with flexibility to pause or reverse based on market conditions. Earlier, on April 3, 2025, OPEC announced an increase of +411 kbd for May 2025, described as “equivalent to three monthly increments”.

- Current forward-looking signals: On September 30, 2025, Reuters reported that OPEC+ was considering a larger November increase (indicative ranges included roughly +274–411 kbd, with one source mentioning up to +500 kbd, which OPEC publicly disputed), and that eight OPEC+ members would hold an online meeting on October 5 to decide November output. Separately, the 62nd OPEC Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC) meeting on October 1, 2025 reaffirmed monitoring adherence to the production adjustments decided at the 38th OPEC and non-OPEC Ministerial Meeting (ONOMM), with the next JMMC set for November 30, 2025.

- Where official decisions are published: OPEC and OPEC+ communiqués and press releases are published on the OPEC press releases index page (opec.org).

Key terms used by OPEC in 2025 communications:
- “Required production”: In 2025 OPEC materials, “required production levels” are referenced in the context of the 38th ONOMM baseline and subsequent voluntary adjustments (e.g., UAE’s required production phased increase per the 38th ONOMM). We will rely on the terminology and figures as presented in OPEC’s official releases when calculating any month-to-month changes.

Why this is a live question: The OPEC+8 have been incrementally unwinding prior cuts with month-by-month adjustments through 2025. Reuters coverage indicates that further increases were under active consideration for late 2025 meetings, but it is not yet determined whether an explicit production increase for January 2026 relative to December 2025 will be officially announced by year-end.
resolution_criteria:
Time window for eligible announcements: 00:00 UTC on 2025-10-15 through 23:59 UTC on 2025-12-31.

Operational group definition ("OPEC+8"): For this question, “group-wide” refers specifically to the eight OPEC+ producers that have been issuing monthly adjustments via OPEC press releases in 2025: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman. This narrower definition is used to ensure unambiguous sourcing and calculation from the ongoing 2025 communication format.

Primary source of truth: Official OPEC/OPEC+ press releases or communiqués published on the OPEC press releases index (https://www.opec.org/press-releases.html). Reputable wire services (e.g., Reuters) may be used only to locate/point to the official OPEC release, not as a standalone resolution source.

Definitions and measurement rules:
- “Required production” and “production adjustment” will be interpreted as they are used in OPEC’s official communications tied to the 38th ONOMM baseline and subsequent voluntary adjustments. When OPEC provides per-country “required production” figures and/or an aggregate “production adjustment” (e.g., “+411 kbd for May”), we will use those officially stated numbers for calculation.
- “Aggregate required production of the OPEC+8” in a given month is defined as the sum of the eight countries’ required production levels for that month, if per-country figures are provided in the OPEC release. If OPEC instead provides a single explicit net “production adjustment” for the OPEC+8 for a given month relative to the prior month (e.g., “the eight countries will implement an adjustment of +N kbd in January 2026 from December 2025 required production level”), that explicit aggregate adjustment will be used as the authoritative month-on-month change.

Resolution rule (YES/NO):
- Resolve YES if, by 23:59 UTC on 2025-12-31, there exists an official OPEC release (on the press releases index) that clearly indicates a net increase in the OPEC+8’s output for January 2026 relative to December 2025, as evidenced by either:
  (A) An explicit positive “production adjustment” for January 2026 (vs December 2025) announced for the OPEC+8; or
  (B) Per-country required production values for both December 2025 and January 2026 for the OPEC+8, such that the sum for January exceeds the sum for December.
- Resolve NO if no such qualifying official release exists by the deadline, or if the official release(s) indicate no change or a net decrease for January 2026 vs December 2025.

Additional tie-breakers and edge cases:
- If multiple official releases are published within the window that address January 2026, the most recent OPEC release before the deadline prevails.
- If OPEC publishes both per-country tables and an explicit aggregate adjustment for January, but they conflict due to an obvious erratum, prefer the later corrected/updated version, if any; otherwise, prefer the explicit aggregate adjustment stated in the text of the same release.
- If OPEC uses synonyms (e.g., “quota,” “target,” “required production”) for the month-by-month mandated levels, use the figures as presented to compute the aggregate month-to-month change.
- Announcements that do not pertain to January 2026 or do not specify a January vs December month-on-month change are ineligible for YES.
- Time zone for all cut-offs is UTC.

Citations for definitions and status quo:
- OPEC/OPEC+ definitions:.
- OPEC press release index (canonical publication location):.
- Evidence of 2025 eight-country arrangement and monthly adjustments (participants and examples of +137 kbd for October 2025, +411 kbd for May 2025, +548 kbd for August 2025; monthly meeting cadence):.
- Reuters context on late-2025 prospective increases and October 5 online meeting plan for November output:.
- JMMC oversight reference and next scheduled meeting (Nov 30, 2025):.

question: Between October 15 and December 31, 2025 (UTC), will the IMF Executive Board complete the second review of Pakistan’s Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and approve a disbursement under the EFF?
background:
Summary and status quo as of 2025-10-01:
- Pakistan is under an International Monetary Fund (IMF) Extended Fund Facility (EFF) arrangement. On May 9, 2025, the IMF Executive Board completed the first review of Pakistan’s EFF arrangement and stated this decision allowed for an immediate disbursement of about US$1 billion (SDR 760 million). In the same press release, the Board also approved an arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) for Pakistan.
- On May 23, 2025, an IMF press release stated that “The next mission associated with the next EFF and RSF reviews is expected in the second half of 2025,” indicating timing for subsequent reviews.

Key definitions and references (for forecasters):
- IMF Executive Board: The IMF’s resident decision‑making body that conducts regular Board meetings and takes decisions on member country arrangements. See IMF overview of the Executive Board: https://www.imf.org/en/About/Our-Structure/Executive-Board and Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#Governance.
- Extended Fund Facility (EFF): An IMF lending arrangement to provide assistance to countries experiencing serious balance of payments problems because of structural weaknesses, with longer‑term engagement than stand‑by arrangements. See IMF factsheet: https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/Sheets/2016/08/01/20/56/Extended-Fund-Facility and Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_Fund_Facility.
- Review (in the context of IMF arrangements): Periodic assessments of a program where IMF staff and authorities evaluate performance against quantitative criteria and structural benchmarks; the IMF Executive Board then considers completion of the numbered review. Completion of a review is announced via an IMF press release that typically uses language such as “Executive Board completes the [Nth] review under the Extended Fund Facility arrangement with [country]” and states whether a disbursement (also called a “purchase” under the EFF) was approved/made available. For example, the May 9, 2025 press release explicitly states that completing the first review enabled an immediate disbursement.
- Disbursement under the EFF: The amount (in Special Drawing Rights, SDR, and often translated into US$) that the press release states is approved/made available for the member to draw (“purchase”) under the EFF upon completion of the review. See IMF glossary entry on purchases/disbursements: https://www.imf.org/en/About/Factsheets/IMF-Lending.
- IMF press release: A news item published on imf.org under the News > Press Releases section and bearing a Press Release number (e.g., PR 25/137). Example for Pakistan (May 9, 2025): https://www.imf.org/en/News/Articles/2025/05/09/pr-25137-pakistan-imf-completes-1st-rev-of-eff-arrang-and-approves-req-for-arrang-under-rsf. The IMF country page for Pakistan also aggregates relevant releases and documents: https://www.imf.org/en/Countries/PAK.

Why this is a non‑trivial forecast:
- Whether the second review can be completed by year‑end depends on Pakistan meeting program conditions, macroeconomic developments, and IMF‑Pakistan negotiations. The May statements set expectations for a second‑half‑2025 mission, but the exact timing and outcome of the Executive Board’s consideration are uncertain. Forecasters should monitor IMF press briefings, staff‑level announcements, and Pakistan’s fiscal/monetary policy news for signals of progress toward Board consideration.

What data/source will be used for resolution:
- The IMF’s official press releases (imf.org News > Press Releases) and, secondarily, the IMF’s Pakistan country page (which links to the same releases). The May 2025 press releases establish the format and language used to indicate completion of a review and approval of a disbursement.
resolution_criteria:
Event window and time zone:
- Eligible events are those announced in IMF press releases dated between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, inclusive. The “date” used is the date displayed on the IMF press release page.

Question restated precisely:
- Resolve Yes if, during the event window, there exists an IMF press release that explicitly states all of the following for Pakistan:
  1) The IMF Executive Board completed the second review under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) arrangement with Pakistan (wording such as “completed the Second Review under the EFF” or “completes second review under the EFF arrangement with Pakistan” is acceptable, including “Second” or “2nd”).
  2) A disbursement/purchase under the EFF strictly greater than zero was approved/made available upon completion of that second review (the press release typically specifies an amount in SDR and often in US$ as well). If the press release combines EFF and RSF items, only the EFF disbursement counts for this criterion.
- Resolve No if no such press release satisfying both (1) and (2) is dated within the event window.

Authoritative sources for resolution:
- Primary: IMF News > Press Releases (https://www.imf.org/en/News/Articles) and the IMF Pakistan country page (https://www.imf.org/en/Countries/PAK) linking to the relevant press release(s).

Inclusions and exclusions:
- Included: An IMF press release bearing a Press Release number (e.g., “PR 25/xxx”) that explicitly states Board completion of the second EFF review for Pakistan and an approved/made‑available disbursement under the EFF greater than zero.
- Excluded: Staff‑level agreements, end‑of‑mission statements, staff concluding statements, press briefings, blogs, or social media posts; press releases that do not mention Board completion of the second EFF review; press releases that mention Board completion but do not approve/make available any disbursement under the EFF (i.e., zero EFF disbursement); press releases dated outside the event window.

Edge cases and tie‑breaking:
- If more than one relevant press release is published within the window, any one that satisfies both (1) and (2) is sufficient for a Yes.
- If a press release announces Board completion of the second review after the window (dated in 2026) referring to a Board decision taken in late 2025, this does not count (the press release date governs eligibility).
- If the press release announces completion of a combined review (e.g., EFF second review and RSF review) and only the RSF disbursement is approved while EFF disbursement is zero, resolve No.
- If the ordinary meaning of “second review” is not used but equivalent numbering is unambiguously indicated (e.g., “completion of Review 2 under the EFF”), treat it as the second review.

Verification time budget:
- A resolver should be able to verify the outcome within 10 minutes by searching imf.org press releases for Pakistan and scanning the relevant press release text.

Citations supporting status quo and precedent wording:
- IMF Executive Board completed Pakistan’s first EFF review on May 9, 2025 and allowed an immediate disbursement of about US$1 billion (SDR 760 million).
- IMF stated on May 23, 2025 that the next mission associated with the next EFF and RSF reviews was expected in the second half of 2025.

question: Will the Bank of England change Bank Rate at either the 6 November or 18 December 2025 MPC announcements?
background:
Summary of what forecasters need to know as of 2025-09-30 (UTC):
- What is “Bank Rate”? The Bank of England (BoE) sets Bank Rate, the interest rate it pays on reserves held with it and charges on certain loans to eligible institutions. Bank Rate influences other UK interest rates.
- When are the relevant meetings? The BoE’s 2025 MPC schedule includes meetings/announcement dates on Thursday 6 November 2025 and Thursday 18 December 2025. The Monetary Policy Summary and minutes are published eight times a year, typically at 12 noon on a Thursday. The BoE explainer page also states: “We will announce our next decision on Thursday 6 November 2025”.
- Current status quo: At its meeting ending on 6 August 2025, the MPC voted 5–4 to reduce Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.00%. At its meeting ending on 17 September 2025, the MPC voted 7–2 to maintain Bank Rate at 4.00%. The BoE’s explainer page shows “Current Bank Rate 4%” and references the August 2025 reduction.
- Market expectations (context only): In the September 2025 Market Participants Survey, respondents’ median expected Bank Rate was 4.00% for 6 November 2025 and 3.75% for 18 December 2025; for 6 November, the mean probability mass was concentrated at 4.00% (57.8%) and 3.75% (38.7%).
- Primary sources to watch on the day: The BoE publishes a “Monetary Policy Summary and minutes” page for each meeting (e.g., November 2025 and December 2025 pages are scheduled “to be published at 12pm”). The BoE also maintains an official Bank Rate database with the current and historical Official Bank Rate.

Key definitions and links:
- Bank Rate (a.k.a. Official Bank Rate): The BoE’s policy rate; see BoE explainer.
- MPC announcement: The BoE’s Monetary Policy Summary and minutes publication for the relevant meeting date (links available on the BoE site and “Monetary policy summary and minutes” index page).
- The two relevant dates are fixed by the BoE’s 2025 schedule: 6 November 2025 and 18 December 2025.

Why this is forecastable now: As of late September 2025, Bank Rate is 4.00% following an August cut, and the MPC kept it unchanged in September. There is meaningful uncertainty about whether the MPC will change Bank Rate at one or both late‑2025 meetings, with survey expectations split across 3.75% and 4.00% for November and a 3.75% median for December.
resolution_criteria:
Question and date range:
- Resolve whether the Bank of England changes Bank Rate at either of the MPC announcements on Thursday 6 November 2025 or Thursday 18 December 2025. Eligible events must occur between 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. All times are UTC.

Definitions:
- “Bank Rate” means the Bank of England’s Official Bank Rate, as defined by the BoE (its policy interest rate that influences other UK interest rates).
- “MPC announcement” means the Bank of England’s published “Monetary Policy Summary and minutes” for the relevant meeting date, which the BoE publishes eight times per year, typically at 12 noon on a Thursday. For November and December 2025, the BoE’s schedule specifies announcements on 6 November 2025 and 18 December 2025. The BoE also flags that the next decision announcement is on 6 November 2025.
- “Change (in Bank Rate) at a meeting” is satisfied if the relevant Monetary Policy Summary explicitly states that the MPC voted to set Bank Rate to a level different from the level in effect immediately prior to that announcement (e.g., “voted to reduce Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points, to 4%” counts as a change; “voted to maintain Bank Rate at 4%” does not). This determination will be based on the wording in the BoE’s Monetary Policy Summary for that meeting.

Resolution rule:
- Resolve Yes if the BoE’s Monetary Policy Summary and minutes for either 6 November 2025 or 18 December 2025 states that the MPC changed Bank Rate (as defined above). Resolve No if both the 6 November 2025 and 18 December 2025 Monetary Policy Summaries and minutes state that Bank Rate was maintained (i.e., no change at either meeting).

Primary resolution sources (any one is sufficient; the Monetary Policy Summary text governs):
- The BoE’s “Monetary Policy Summary and minutes” index, which links to each meeting’s announcement and is published at 12 noon on Thursdays eight times a year.
- The November 2025 Monetary Policy Summary and minutes page (marked “to be published at 12pm”) and the December 2025 page (marked “to be published at 12pm”).

Secondary corroborating source (if needed):
- The BoE Official Bank Rate database, which lists the current and historical Official Bank Rate values and can confirm the rate before and after the relevant announcements.

Edge cases and contingencies:
- Only decisions announced in the Monetary Policy Summary and minutes for the specified 6 November 2025 and 18 December 2025 meetings count. Inter‑meeting changes (if any) do not affect resolution unless the change is explicitly decided at one of these two meetings and stated in the corresponding Monetary Policy Summary.
- If either meeting is rescheduled but the corresponding Monetary Policy Summary for that meeting is still published within 2025, that publication will count for this question; otherwise, if a meeting is cancelled or its Monetary Policy Summary is not published by 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, treat that meeting as “no change” for the purpose of this question and resolve based on the remaining meeting.
- The question resolves as soon as the first of the two specified Monetary Policy Summaries indicating a change is published (Yes), or after the 18 December 2025 publication if neither indicates a change (No).

question: Between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, will the Ksi Lisims LNG project announce a positive Final Investment Decision (FID)?
background:
Overview and current status as of October 1, 2025:
- Project identity: The “Ksi Lisims LNG – Natural Gas Liquefaction and Marine Terminal Project” is a proposed floating LNG export facility on Nisga’a Nation land near the community of Gingolx on Canada’s northwest Pacific coast. The project proponents are Nisga’a Nation, Rockies LNG Limited Partnership, and Western LNG LLC.
- Regulatory status: On September 15, 2025, the federal Minister of Environment and Climate Change issued an Impact Assessment Decision Statement, effectively green-lighting the project at the federal level under the Impact Assessment Act and setting legally binding conditions for the proponents. On September 16, 2025, the Government of British Columbia announced that the project received its provincial Environmental Assessment Certificate; the announcement noted that the partners had not yet made a final investment decision at that time.
- Capacity and design: Public reporting and proponent materials describe the project as a 12 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) LNG facility.
- Official information sources likely to host an FID announcement: The official Ksi Lisims LNG website has a News page (https://www.ksilisimslng.com/news) that hosts press releases. Western LNG also maintains a News page (https://www.westernlng.com/news). The IAAC project page provides authoritative project documentation and updates , and the Government of British Columbia posts related provincial announcements.

Key definitions and scope for this question:
- Time window and timezone: Only announcements published between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025 are eligible.
- Project covered: “Ksi Lisims LNG – Natural Gas Liquefaction and Marine Terminal Project,” as identified by Canada’s Impact Assessment Agency project page.
- Proponents: Nisga’a Nation; Rockies LNG Limited Partnership; Western LNG LLC.
- “Final Investment Decision” (FID) for the purpose of resolution: An explicit announcement by one or more proponents that a “final investment decision” (or “FID”) has been made and is positive/affirmative, committing the project to proceed. For resolvability, the announcement must include the phrase “final investment decision” or “FID.” 

Notes for forecasters:
- As of mid-September 2025, the project cleared major federal and provincial assessment milestones, but an FID had not yet been taken.
- Market, financing, offtake, and EPC readiness typically influence LNG FID timing; however, this question resolves solely on the presence of an explicit FID announcement within the defined window.
resolution_criteria:
How this question will resolve:
- Resolve YES if, between 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, there is an official announcement explicitly stating that a positive “final investment decision” (or “FID”) has been made for the Ksi Lisims LNG project, where:
  - Eligible announcements include: 
    - A press release or website update posted on any official proponent website (e.g., Ksi Lisims LNG News page: https://www.ksilisimslng.com/news ; Western LNG News page: https://www.westernlng.com/news ; Rockies LNG News page: https://www.rockieslng.com/news ).
    - An announcement on an official government page confirming the FID (e.g., Impact Assessment Agency of Canada or Government of British Columbia news/updates).
    - Coverage by a major, reputable outlet (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg) directly quoting or citing an official proponent or government statement that a positive FID has been made.
  - The announcement must include the exact phrase “final investment decision” or “FID” and indicate that the decision is positive/affirmative. Announcements of intent to reach FID, “pre-FID” steps, conditional or deferred FIDs, or generic terms like “sanction” or “approval” without explicit reference to a “final investment decision” or “FID” do not count.
  - If multiple announcements exist, the earliest publication timestamp within the window (standardized to UTC) will be used to confirm eligibility.
- Resolve NO if no eligible announcement meeting the above criteria is published within the time window.

Verification steps (for resolvers):
1) Check the Ksi Lisims LNG News page and the proponents’/government pages listed above for any press releases explicitly stating a positive “final investment decision” or “FID”.
2) If necessary, verify via major wire services (e.g., Reuters) that directly quote a proponent/government confirming a positive FID.
3) Record the publication date/time and confirm it falls within the defined UTC window.

Edge cases:
- If an announcement uses synonyms (e.g., “project sanctioned”) but does not explicitly include “final investment decision” or “FID,” it will not count unless accompanied by a direct statement that a positive FID has been made.
- If an announcement is published on December 31, 2025 in a local timezone after 23:59:59 UTC, it will not count. The resolver must convert timestamps to UTC when needed.
- If an announcement is later retracted within the window, the question resolves based on the status at 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025; a retraction before that cutoff negates eligibility.

Primary sources for resolution:
- IAAC Canada news/updates and project page 
- Government of British Columbia news releases 
- Proponent websites: Ksi Lisims LNG News page ; Western LNG News page ; Rockies LNG News page 
- Major wire services directly quoting officials, if needed

question: Will Boeing complete its acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025 and 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025?
background:
Summary of the transaction and current status (as of 2025-10-01):
- Transaction: The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA) seeks to acquire Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: SPR). As part of the broader package around the deal, Airbus is set to take on certain Spirit Europe-focused activities (including Spirit’s Prestwick, Scotland and Subang, Malaysia operations that support Airbus programs), while Spirit’s Belfast operations not supporting Airbus programs would be sold, according to reporting on Boeing’s submitted remedies to the European Commission (EC).
- EU antitrust review: Boeing has offered remedies/commitments to the European Commission in order to secure approval. Following submission of these commitments, the EC extended its decision deadline for the deal to October 14, 2025, and is expected to gather market feedback before deciding whether to accept the remedies or open an in-depth (up to four-month) investigation.
- UK competition review: The UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) cleared the anticipated acquisition on August 8, 2025.
- Shareholder approval: Spirit AeroSystems shareholders approved the acquisition at a special meeting held on January 31, 2025.

Why this is forecastable now: The EC’s provisional decision deadline of October 14, 2025 means the key remaining obstacle could be cleared (or extended to in-depth review) just before the start of the resolution window (October 15). Depending on that outcome, the transaction could close in Q4 2025 or be delayed, making both Yes and No plausible by year-end.

Key references and where to track updates:
- EU review: European Commission merger case page for Boeing/Spirit (case M.11578). Reuters coverage confirms remedies submission and the Oct 14, 2025 deadline extension.
- UK review: CMA case page records the Phase 1 clearance on August 8, 2025.
- Company approvals: Spirit’s January 31, 2025 shareholder approval is documented on the company’s investor relations site.
- Closing confirmations (once/if the deal completes): Company press releases on their investor relations pages and SEC EDGAR Form 8-K filings (Form 8-K is the current report used by U.S. public companies to announce material events).

Definitions and useful links (for clarity):
- Acquisition/closing: For this question, “complete its acquisition” means the transaction has closed (i.e., become effective/consummated) such that Boeing becomes the owner of Spirit AeroSystems via completion of the merger under the governing merger agreement, as evidenced by official company disclosures (see Resolution Criteria). Closing is typically reported in a Form 8-K “current report” filing and/or a press release.
- Time standard: UTC refers to Coordinated Universal Time (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time). Date and time windows in this question are measured in UTC.
- Official company communications: Press release is a public announcement posted on an official corporate press/IR site (e.g., Boeing investor relations: https://investors.boeing.com; Spirit investor relations: https://investor.spiritaero.com). SEC EDGAR database: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch.

Status quo snapshot:
- EC review ongoing; decision deadline extended to Oct 14, 2025 after Boeing offered remedies, with market testing expected and a possible four-month in-depth investigation if concerns remain.
- CMA has cleared the deal (Phase 1) as of Aug 8, 2025.
- Spirit shareholders approved the acquisition on Jan 31, 2025.
- Form 8-K is the standard SEC mechanism for companies to announce material events such as deal closings.
resolution_criteria:
Binary resolution (Yes/No).

Time window for eligible events:
- Start: 00:00:00 UTC on October 15, 2025
- End: 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025

Question restated precisely: Resolve “Yes” if Boeing’s acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems is completed (i.e., the transaction closes/merger becomes effective) at any time during the window above, as evidenced by the acceptable sources below. Resolve “No” otherwise.

Acceptable resolution evidence (primary sources preferred):
Any one of the following is sufficient for a Yes resolution, so long as it unambiguously states that the acquisition has closed (or the merger has been consummated/become effective) and the closing date falls within the window above (interpreting date-only statements as UTC dates):
1) A Form 8-K filed on the SEC’s EDGAR system by either The Boeing Company or Spirit AeroSystems that explicitly states the closing/completion of the acquisition/merger (e.g., Item 2.01 Completion of Acquisition or a filing that clearly states the merger closed on [date]). Form 8-K is the SEC “current report” used by public companies to announce material events.
2) A joint or concurrent press release posted on the official investor relations/press pages of both companies that explicitly states that the transaction has closed (e.g., “Boeing completes acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems”).

Secondary corroboration (if needed for clarity, but not required if a primary source is clear): Reports by major, reputable outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, Bloomberg) that the deal has closed on [date]. Note: If there is any discrepancy between press reports and the companies’ official disclosures, the companies’ Form 8-K filings and official press releases take precedence.

Interpretation rules and edge cases:
- Date-only statements: If a source states only a calendar date for closing (without a time), interpret it as occurring on that UTC date. If multiple sources give different dates, prefer the date stated in a Form 8-K, if available.
- After-hours filings: If an SEC filing is timestamped outside the window but explicitly states that closing occurred on a date within the window, it counts as Yes.
- Partial asset transfers/divestitures: The question concerns completion of Boeing’s acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems. Related divestitures (e.g., transfers to Airbus) do not need to have closed for this question to resolve Yes, provided the Boeing–Spirit transaction itself is completed as per the companies’ official disclosures.
- Termination: If the transaction is terminated or remains unclosed through 23:59:59 UTC on December 31, 2025, resolve No.

Pre-identified sources to check at resolution time:
- SEC EDGAR company pages for Boeing and Spirit (for Form 8-K filings).
- Boeing and Spirit investor relations news pages (for press releases). 

Context for forecasters:
- As of Oct 1, 2025, the EC has extended its decision deadline to Oct 14, 2025 following Boeing’s submission of remedies and is expected to conduct market testing; it may accept the remedies or open a four-month investigation. The UK CMA cleared the deal on Aug 8, 2025. Spirit shareholders approved the acquisition on Jan 31, 2025. These milestones frame the regulatory path remaining before potential closing within the window.

question: By December 31, 2025 (23:59:59 UTC), will the United States publish an official instrument that explicitly caps tariffs on EU- or Japan‑origin pharmaceutical products at 15% ad valorem?
background:
Status quo as of 2025-09-30:
- EU framework implementation: A Federal Register notice amending the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) to implement elements of the August 21, 2025 U.S.–EU framework states that, for automobiles and parts, the combined tariff rate (MFN plus reduced Section 232 rate) is capped at 15% ad valorem for EU‑origin products and that certain goods (including generic pharmaceuticals and their ingredients and chemical precursors) are treated separately. CBP subsequently issued guidance explaining HTSUS implementation details, including an exemption from reciprocal tariffs for EU generic pharmaceuticals (using heading 9903.02.77), effective September 1, 2025.
- Japan agreement implementation: A Federal Register notice implementing tariff‑related elements of the U.S.–Japan agreement establishes a baseline 15% ad valorem tariff structure for nearly all Japanese imports, with sector‑specific treatment for automobiles, aerospace, generic pharmaceuticals, and certain natural resources; it includes effective‑date and in‑transit exceptions. A White House presidential action page similarly describes the baseline 15% structure and authorizes zero reciprocal tariffs for generic pharmaceuticals and related inputs.
- Public statements on pharmaceuticals: Reuters reported EU and Japan officials’ confidence that U.S. tariffs on pharmaceuticals would not exceed 15% under joint statements with Washington, referencing a 15% ceiling for EU exports including pharmaceuticals. CNN reported President Trump’s announcement of a 100% tariff on branded/patented pharmaceutical products effective October 1, 2025, while noting that the White House confirmed it would honor a 15% tariff cap agreed in trade deals with the EU and Japan, implying capped rates for EU/Japan‑origin pharmaceuticals.

Interpretation and current uncertainty:
- As of today, specific codified HTSUS or agency‑level text that explicitly caps EU‑ or Japan‑origin pharmaceutical products at 15% ad valorem (covering all HTSUS Chapter 30 pharmaceuticals, not only generics) has not been clearly identified in the cited notices; autos and certain sectoral carve‑outs are explicitly treated, and generic pharmaceuticals are addressed separately (exemptions/zero reciprocal tariffs), but an explicit 15% cap covering pharmaceutical products broadly would require a further instrument or explicit language.

Key definitions and scope for forecasters:
- Pharmaceutical products: For this question, “pharmaceutical products” means goods classified under HTSUS Chapter 30 (“Pharmaceutical Products”). See HTSUS Chapter 30 (U.S. International Trade Commission) at https://hts.usitc.gov/reststop/file?release=currentRelease&filename=Chapter%2030.
- Country of origin: Determined under U.S. non‑preferential rules of origin and CBP practice (see 19 CFR Part 102, Rules of Origin) at https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-19/chapter-I/part-102.
- Tariff (ad valorem): A customs duty stated as a percentage of the customs value (see “Tariff” overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff; “Ad valorem tax”: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_valorem_tax).
- EU and Japan: The European Union (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union) and Japan (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan).

Why this is forecastable with meaningful entropy:
- Public statements indicate intent to cap EU/Japan pharmaceutical tariffs at 15%, but codification specific to pharmaceuticals—especially patented/brand‑name drugs—may require additional instruments (e.g., HTSUS modifications or agency guidance) that could be issued or not by year‑end. The interplay between the baseline 15% Japanese tariff structure and sector‑specific carve‑outs, and the EU framework’s sectoral exemptions, leaves open whether an explicit cross‑sector cap for pharmaceuticals will be published in official text.
resolution_criteria:
Event window and resolution time:
- Window: From 2025-10-15 00:00:00 UTC through 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.
- Resolve at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC.

Question resolves “Yes” if, within the window, a U.S. official instrument is publicly posted that explicitly establishes a 15% ad valorem maximum (cap/ceiling) applicable to pharmaceutical products of EU or Japan origin, as defined below. Otherwise “No.”

Qualifying official instrument (any one suffices):
- A Federal Register notice (Commerce/USTR/CBP) that amends the HTSUS or sets tariff application rules, or a Presidential Executive Order/Proclamation posted on whitehouse.gov/federalregister.gov, or a CBP CSMS bulletin/guidance, or an official USTR or Commerce directive/notice that is publicly accessible on an official.gov domain.

What “explicitly caps at 15%” means:
- The instrument must, in its operative language, state either: (a) “pharmaceutical” or “pharmaceutical products” or otherwise clearly reference HTSUS Chapter 30 goods and an applied tariff ceiling of 15% ad valorem for EU‑ or Japan‑origin entries; or (b) provide HTSUS modifications or headings that unambiguously result in a combined applied duty rate (base Column 1 duty plus any additional duties under Sections 232/301/IEEPA/reciprocal tariffs, etc.) not exceeding 15% ad valorem for EU‑ or Japan‑origin Chapter 30 entries.
- The cap must apply to pharmaceutical products broadly (HTSUS Chapter 30) and not be limited solely to “generic” pharmaceuticals; instruments that only exempt generics (non‑patented pharmaceutical applications) without capping branded/patented products do not qualify.

Scope definitions for resolution:
- “Pharmaceutical products”: All goods classifiable under HTSUS Chapter 30. Link: https://hts.usitc.gov/reststop/file?release=currentRelease&filename=Chapter%2030.
- “EU‑ or Japan‑origin”: Country of origin determined under U.S. non‑preferential rules of origin. Link: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-19/chapter-I/part-102.
- “Tariff” and “ad valorem”: A duty assessed as a percentage of customs value. Links: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_valorem_tax.
- “Official instrument” and “published”: Content posted on official U.S. government sites (e.g., federalregister.gov, whitehouse.gov, cbp.gov, ustr.gov, commerce.gov) that is public by the resolution time.

Verification guidance for resolvers:
- Check Federal Register notices implementing EU or Japan frameworks and any subsequent amendments for explicit pharmaceutical 15% cap language or HTSUS headings that produce a 15% ceiling.
- Review White House presidential actions and Executive Orders that might modify reciprocal tariffs or sectoral treatment.
- Review CBP CSMS bulletins/guidance for tariff application instructions to Chapter 30 entries from EU or Japan (note: existing CSMS already exempts generics but does not constitute a broad cap).
- Cross‑check credible reporting only as confirmation of official issuance (e.g., Reuters/CNN), but the resolution requires the instrument itself to meet the explicit cap standard; statements of intent alone do not qualify.

Edge cases:
- If multiple instruments exist and one meets the explicit cap standard, resolve “Yes,” even if others are silent or conflicting.
- If an instrument establishes a 15% ceiling for only EU or only Japan pharmaceutical products, resolve “Yes.”
- If an instrument caps only a subset of Chapter 30 (e.g., specific headings) and leaves others above 15%, resolve “No.”
- If an instrument provides exemptions or zero reciprocal tariffs for generic pharmaceuticals only, with no cap on branded/patented products, resolve “No”.
